papers.title: Lower and upper solutions for boundary value problems with bounded $\Phi$-laplacian Stieltjes-differential inclusions
papers.authors: Rodrigo Lopez Pouso, Paula Vazquez Garcia
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of solutions between given lower and upper solutions for several types of boundary value problems involving bounded Phi-Laplacian inclusions. We consider derivatives in the Stieltjes sense, that is, derivatives with respect to nondecreasing and left-continuous functions. This framework includes, as particular cases, both differential and difference equations, even allowing for impulses at the discontinuity points of the derivator. To the best of the authors knowledge, this paper presents the first application of the method of lower and upper solutions to second-order boundary value problems with Stieltjes derivatives.

papers.title: Endpoint Exclusion for Bounded Damping on the Standard Flat Two-Torus
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed nonzero nonnegative bounded damping $W$ on the standard flat two-torus, the stationary damped wave operator satisfies $\|(-\Delta-s^2+isW)^{-1}\|_{L^2\to L^2}=o(|s|)$. Consequently, for initial data in $H^2\times H^1$, the uniform decay rate of the square root of the energy improves from $O(t^{-1/2})$ to $o(t^{-1/2})$. This excludes the endpoint quasimodes proposed by Kleinhenz in 2024. The proof combines a uniform $L^4$ estimate, equidistribution of densities when the largest Fourier coefficient tends to zero, and a one-dimensional equation for a nonzero modulated weak limit. No continuity of the damping is required. The improvement may depend on $W$ and does not assert a fixed gain in the polynomial exponent.

papers.title: Symmetry, boundary conditions, and the Noether correspondence of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation
papers.abstract: Conserved quantities of nonlinear dispersive wave equations are typically derived on the whole plane, whereas numerical simulations evaluate them on a torus. We examine how compactifying one or both spatial directions affects the Noether correspondences of the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation, obtained from its potential Lagrangian, on the family of domains $\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{T}\}^2$. The outcome is a three-valued classification: intrinsic, chart-dependent, or defective. Only the two first moments, whose characteristics carry an undifferentiated coordinate weight, are affected. A moment can become defective only if its weighted direction is compact and the mass flux crosses the seam of the chosen fundamental domain; for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation this happens exactly for the longitudinal moment when $x$ is compact. The status of each moment depends only on the boundary condition along its weighted direction. When $x$ is compact, the Galilean boost still maps solutions to solutions, but no global Noether charge corresponds to it.

papers.title: A Proof of a P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} Conjecture: A PDE Approach to Capacity Inequalities
papers.abstract:
We prove a planar capacity-ratio inequality conjectured by Polya and Szego, together with its extension to adjacent dimensions: for every integer $n\geq2$ and compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $C_{n-1}(K)\leq \left[ rac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\sqrt\pi \Gamma((n+1)/2)}ight]^{1/(n-1)}C_{n-2}(K),$ where $C_s$ denotes the length-homogeneous Riesz capacity and, when $n=2$, $C_{n-2}=C_0$ is logarithmic capacity. Closed balls attain equality, so the constant is sharp. Starting from an exterior Dirichlet problem and its nonnegative boundary flux, we construct a function $ho$ in one higher dimension, with coordinates $X=(x,z)$, and prove that, for $z
e0$, $\Deltaho= rac{n-1}{ho}|

Green's formula on the exterior of level sets of $U$ then bounds the Dirichlet integral by the total flux at infinity, and the Dirichlet principle yields the capacity bound. papers.title: Almost-sure quenched KAM tori for nonlinear wave equations with a spatial white-noise potential
papers.authors: Yingdu Dong, Wenwen Jian, Xiaoping Yuan
papers.abstract:
Let \[
  A_\omega=-\partial_x^2+ho\,\partial_xB(x,\omega),
  \qquad ho

Here $B$ is Brownian motion in the spatial variable $x$, and $\partial_xB$ denotes its distributional derivative. We consider the nonlinear wave equation \[
  u_{tt}+A_\omega u+f(u)=0, \] where $f$ is odd and real analytic near zero, with $f(u)=\kappa u^3+O(u^5)$ and $\kappa
e0$. We show that, on a single event of probability one, no nontrivial finitely supported integer combination of the positive wave frequencies is an integer, and the quartic twist matrix is nonsingular for every finite tangential set of positive modes. After fixing a path in this event, we construct a partial Birkhoff normal form of the Hamiltonian up to degree ten. For every finite nonempty tangential set $J$ of cardinality $b$ associated with positive eigenvalues, we obtain a Cantor family of real-analytic, small-amplitude invariant $b$-tori in $H^1_0(0,\pi;\mathbb{R})	imes L^2(0,\pi;\mathbb{R})$. The family is parametrized by a Cantor subset of $[

papers.title: Nonexistence of $(1,6)$-sign soliton solutions for the damped nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation in 2D
papers.abstract: We consider the two-dimensional damped nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation $$\begin{align*} \partial_t^2u-\Delta u+2\alpha\partial_tu+u-|u|^{p-1}u=0 \end{align*}$$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $\alpha>0$ and $p>2$. We study multi-soliton solutions asymptotic in the energy space, in the full-time limit $t\to\infty$, to a superposition of translated ground states, with one soliton having the sign opposite to that of the other $k$ solitons. C\^{o}te and Du conjectured nonexistence for $k\geq7$ in the regular polygonal setting and identified the hexagonal case $k=6$ as critical. In this paper, we prove that $(1,k)$-sign soliton solutions do not exist for any $k\geq6$, without imposing any symmetry assumptions.

papers.title: Overview and recent progress on the classical Bernoulli free boundary problem
papers.abstract: This survey gives an overview of the Bernoulli or one-phase free boundary problem, with emphasis on recent progress.

papers.title: Boundary remainders and optimal convergence rates for planar spectral partitions
papers.abstract: Let $S_m(\Omega)$ denote the infimum of the sum of the first Dirichlet eigenvalues over partitions of a bounded connected planar domain $\Omega$ into exactly $m$ nonempty connected open cells. We study the convergence of $|\Omega|S_m(\Omega)/m^2$ to its universal limit $c_*$. If the full topological boundary has zero area, we bound the absolute error by the area of its tubular neighborhood at scale $m^{-1/2}$, together with an $O(m^{-1/2})$ term. This yields rates $O_\Omega(m^{-1/2})$ on Lipschitz domains and $O_\Omega(m^{-\alpha/2})$ on domains with finitely many $C^{0,\alpha}$ boundary charts, $0<\alpha<1$, for all sufficiently large integers. The square and a fixed smooth domain have positive matching lower bounds of order $m^{-1/2}$. For each $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a fixed H\"older graph domain attains the order $m^{-\alpha/2}$ along a subsequence. Little H\"older domains satisfy the corresponding little-$o$ estimate, but no prescribed additional factor tending to zero works for the whole class, even with domain-dependent constants. An auxiliary energy with variable cell count gives the boundary estimate; a positive correction on the square and sparse graph constructions yield the lower bounds.

papers.title: Almost sure scattering for the energy-critical Hartree equation with radial data below the energy space
papers.authors: Yuli Feng, Yuyang Ye, Han Yang
papers.abstract: We study the energy-critical Hartree equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge5$, with randomized radial initial data of supercritical regularity. To handle the nonlocal Hartree interaction, we exploit the Riesz smoothing of the Hartree convolution through a bilinear decomposition adapted to the regularity of the interacting terms. This leads to a Hartree bilinear estimate that allows us to combine probabilistic weighted spacetime estimates with weighted and interaction Morawetz estimates. For every $d\ge5$, we establish almost sure local well-posedness for randomized radial data below the energy regularity, together with a conditional scattering criterion. For $d\ge7$, we further prove almost sure global existence and scattering. The uniform energy and Morawetz bounds are established through a double bootstrap argument combining the Hartree bilinear decomposition with an energy increment estimate.

papers.title: The maximum area of a snake polyomino in a $12 \times n$ rectangle
papers.abstract: A snake polyomino is a set of cells of the square lattice whose cells, under edge adjacency, induce a path. Let $T(m,n)$ be the largest number of cells of a snake polyomino contained in an $m \times n$ rectangle, equivalently the largest number of vertices of an induced path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ (OEIS A360917). Blondin Mass\'e and Goupil determined $T(m,n)$ for all $m \le 5$ and proposed the general case as a conjecture; for $m = 12$, entry A397153 of the OEIS records a conjectured generating function, contributed by Goupil in July 2026, which has remained unproved. We prove it. For every $n \ge 1$ other than $n \in \{2,3,\dots,10,12\}$ one has $T(12,n) = 44k + c_r$ where $n = 6k+r$ with $0 \le r < 6$ and $(c_0,\dots,c_5) = (5,12,19,27,34,42)$, and the ten remaining values are $18,26,33,40,47,55,62,70,77$ and $92$. The proof has two independent halves. The upper bound comes from a column-profile transfer system read in the max-plus semiring: a single entrywise inequality $v_{46} \le 44 + v_{40}$ between two value vectors on its useful core propagates to all larger indices because the max-plus action is monotone and additively homogeneous. The lower bound comes from explicit periodic snakes, one for each residue class, which are checked against the definition of a snake and not against the transfer system. The same method settles every height up to $12$; heights $6$ through $11$ had no formula in the literature, and we record them as well.

papers.title: Improving Razmyslov's (1974) bound: the Nagata-Higman index is at most $n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$
papers.abstract: Let $d(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every associative (not necessarily unital) algebra over a field of characteristic zero satisfying the identity $x^n=0$ also satisfies $x_1x_2\cdots x_m=0$; this is the Nagata-Higman index. Razmyslov proved $d(n)\le n^2$ in 1974; Kuzmin proved $d(n)\ge n(n+1)/2$ and conjectured equality; this is the Kuzmin (1975) conjecture. We prove $d(n)\le n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$ (and, by a simpler case of the same method, $d(n)\le n^2-1$ for $n\ge2$); in particular $d(6)\le34$. To our knowledge, $n=6$ is the first case in which the new bound improves the known bounds, and this is the first improvement of Razmyslov's bound for general $n$. For $m=n^2-1$ and $m=n^2-2$, Formanek's criterion reduces $d(n)\le m$ to the statement that no nonzero linear combination of $(m+1)$-cycles lies in one particular isotypic block of the group algebra of $S_{m+1}$. For $m=n^2-1$ this statement follows from the branching rule; for $m=n^2-2$ we prove it using the Jucys-Murphy elements and a theorem of Frobenius on the characters of the alternating group. These bounds have also been proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Sparse Gabor representations of metaplectic operators: controlled exponential decay and Schr\"odinger confinement" [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828]
papers.authors: Elena Cordero, Gianluca Giacchi, Edoardo Pucci, Salvatore Ivan Trapasso
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is to correct some quantitative estimates and computations in [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828]. The proofs of Theorem 1.3 and Lemma 3.6 there contain gaps, and consequently some of the numerical decay coefficients that depend on them need adjustment. Some identities concerning Hamiltonian flows and Euler decompositions in Section 6 also require correction. Theorem 1.2 and the qualitative conclusions of the general metaplectic estimates in [Adv. Math. 490 (2026) 110828], namely Gabor sparsity and exponential confinement for quadratic Schr\"odinger evolutions, are not affected.

papers.title: The Construction of Directed Partial Orders on the Complex Field by Puiseux Series and Stratification
papers.abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the complex field C admits a lattice order compatible with the ring operations. Schwartz and Yang proved in 2011 that C admits directed partial orders. We give a new construction that by using a transcendence basis of C over Q, we embed C into a field of Puiseux series F{{s}}, so that every complex number acquires a series expansion, and we define positivity by a condition on the leading coefficient. Every directed partial order we construct is placed in a stratification by how much of the expansion a rule has to read. Reading one term, a window of fixed width, or a sensitivity condition on small changes, we obtain five nested conditions and six types. Relative to the fixed level valuation, cones satisfying B correspond to the cards satisfying a product and a sum condition. Cones satisfying C are never lattice orders, which excludes Types 1, 2, 3. We give an example of Type 4 that is not a lattice order either. The existence of a lattice order on C and the existence of orders of Types 5 and 6 still remain open. This is a stratification rather than a complete classification because only Types 1 - 4 are shown to be nonempty.

papers.title: Nonlinear skew Lie-type centralizers on $\ast$-algebras
papers.authors: Mohammad Afajal Ansari, Mohammad Ashraf, Md Shamim Akhter
papers.abstract: Let \(\mathcal{A}\) be a unital \(\ast\)-algebra over the complex field \(\mathbb{C}\), with center \(\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\). For any \(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\in\mathcal{A}\), define recursively $ p_1(X_1)=X_1,$ $p_2(X_1, X_2)=[X_1,X_2]_{\ast}=X_1X_2-X_2X_1^{\ast}$ and $p_n(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n)=[p_{n-1}(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1}),X_n]_{\ast}$ for all integers \(n\geq 2\). In this paper, we prove that if a map \(\Phi:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) satisfies $\Phi(p_n(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n))=p_n(\Phi(X_1),X_2,\ldots,X_n)$ for all \(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\in\mathcal{A}\), then \(\Phi\) necessarily has the form $\Phi(X)=ZX,$ where \(Z=Z^{\ast}\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\). As an application, we establish that, under suitable assumptions, every nonlinear generalized skew Lie \(n\)-derivation \(G:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) admits a standard form $G(X)=ZX+D(X),$ where \(Z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\) and \(D:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) is an additive \(\ast\)-derivation. Finally, we apply this result to several important classes of unital \(\ast\)-algebras, including unital prime \(\ast\)-algebras, standard operator algebras, and von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Extremal Ky Fan $p$-$k$ norms of graphs
papers.abstract: We study a two-parameter extension of Nikiforov's extremal problems for graph norms, focusing on the quantity $$ S_{p,k}(G) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(G)^p\right)^{1/p}, $$ where $p\ge1$, and $\sigma_1(G) \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_n(G)$ are the singular values of the adjacency matrix of an $n$-vertex graph $G$. This quantity provides a common generalization of the Ky Fan $k$-norm and the Schatten $p$-norm, which correspond to the cases $p=1$ and $k=n$, respectively. We establish upper and lower bounds and characterize extremal and near-extremal graphs within specified parameter ranges. For each fixed $k \ge 4$, we determine an explicit exponent $\vartheta_k \in [1,2)$ such that the balanced complete $k$-partite graph is the unique maximizer for all sufficiently large orders, and we characterize the unique graph attaining the second-largest value. In particular, this determines the maximum Ky Fan $4$-norm for all sufficiently large orders. At these exponents, any maximizer with a fixed edge deficit from the Tur\'{a}n graph's edge count belongs to an explicit finite family of complete $k$-partite graphs (whenever such a realization exists), whereas a fixed edge surplus is uniquely maximized by adding a star inside a largest part of the balanced graph. Furthermore, we quantify the relation between small absolute norm deficits and graph structure, demonstrating that relative near-optimality alone does not guarantee structural proximity. We also obtain a vertex-partition lower bound featuring an optimal universal remainder coefficient and complete equality conditions. These results provide structural answers to Nikiforov's norm questions in the two-parameter setting, linking extremal values to uniqueness, prescribed edge counts, and the structure of near-extremal graphs.

papers.title: The Manhattan cospectrality of the cocktail party graph
papers.authors: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ of order $N$ with adjacency eigenvalues $\lambda_{1}(G)\geq \cdots\geq\lambda_{N}(G),$ the cospectrality of $G$ is the smallest value of $\sum_{i}\left\vert \lambda_{i}(G)-\lambda_{i}(H)\right\vert $ over all graphs $H$ of order $N$ not isomorphic to $G.$ Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that the cospectrality of the cocktail party graph $CP_{n}$ is attained exactly at the graph $H_{n}.$ This graph is obtained from $K_{1,2,\ldots,2}$ by attaching a pendant vertex to the vertex of the part of size one. We prove this conjecture for every $n\geq2$ by showing that only three explicit graphs (two for $n=2$) are at distance less than $2$ from $CP_{n}.$ We work with the complement of a competing graph. First we remove its components $K_{2}.$ Then we treat the case in which its main component has a dominating vertex. The remaining cases are reduced to finitely many small graphs. The proof is computer-assisted, and all computations concern explicit finite lists of graphs.

papers.title: Detour different-distance sets in graphs
papers.abstract: The detour distance $D(u,v)$ between two vertices of a connected graph is the length of a longest $u,v$-path. A set $S$ of vertices is a detour different-distance set if no vertex outside $S$ has the same detour distance to two vertices of $S$. We study the lower and upper detour different-distance numbers $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)$ and $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$, the smallest and largest orders of maximal such sets; this is the detour analogue of the different-distance sets of Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder. The two notions coincide on trees, cycles, complete bipartite graphs and the Petersen graph, but differ in general: for instance, detour different-distance sets may contain triangles or induce $4$-cycles. We determine both numbers for many families, among them wheels, fans, windmills, hypercubes, helms, flowers, books, ladders, prisms, M\"obius ladders, crowns, gears, Dutch windmills and complete multipartite graphs, and for joins, coronas and lexicographic products. We prove that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$ is at most the detour diameter; that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a path; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=1$ whenever two vertices are joined by Hamiltonian paths to all other vertices; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=2$ for Hamiltonian-laceable graphs and, more generally, for bipartite graphs in which each part contains two vertices whose detour distances to the other part are constant; and that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ for Hamiltonian graphs.

papers.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
papers.abstract: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Bara\'nski, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpi\'nska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{\lambda z} + Be^{-\lambda z}$, where $AB\lambda \neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.

papers.title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
papers.abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).

papers.title: M\"obius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $\lambda\in F^\times$, \[
  \card{A+\lambda A^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a M\"obius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

papers.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $\gamma\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $\gamma N$, and that near each threshold $\gamma k$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-\Delta_V^{(k)}=-\Delta_V\otimes 1_{\mu_k}-d\Gamma_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-\Delta_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $\gamma^{-1}$ below $\gamma k$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-c\gamma})$ for every $c<2\delta_V$. Here $\delta_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

papers.title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Tur\'an graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.

papers.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
papers.abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.

papers.title: A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems
papers.abstract: The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.

papers.title: Arinkin's sheaf and Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract:
Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincar\'e bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincar\'e kernel for an elliptic surface.
  As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both. We also construct an explicit deformation that connects Markman's construction of a projectively hyperholomorphic bundle on products of hyper-K\"ahler manifolds of K3${}^{[g]}$-type to that of Hartlieb and Shah. This answers a question of Hartlieb and Shah.

papers.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $\sigma$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\in\sigma+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.

papers.title: Partial sums of Rogers-Ramanujan functions
papers.abstract: Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial Approximants vanishing arbitrarily close to the origin
papers.authors: Athanasios Beslikas, Christopher Felder, Douglas T. Pfeffer
papers.abstract: This work concerns a sequence of stable polynomials on the bidisk whose affine optimal polynomial approximants in the Hardy space of the bidisk have zero varieties that come arbitrarily close to the origin.

papers.title: Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.

papers.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi(P)=|P|\mu_1(P)$, where $\mu_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $\Phi$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $\Phi(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szeg\H{o}--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.

papers.title: Connected Cayley Approximation of Power Graphs of Finite Groups
papers.abstract: For a nontrivial finite group \(G\), we define its connected intersection density as the maximum, over all connected Cayley graphs on \(G\), of the proportion of edges that also belong to the undirected power graph of \(G\). We show that this density is \(1\) if and only if \(G\) is cyclic, and that it is \(1/4\), \(1/6\), and \(1/12\) for \(A_4\), \(S_4\), and \(A_5\), respectively. For the dihedral group of order \(2n\), with \(n\geq 3\), we give a general formula and show that the connected intersection density equals \((\binom{n}{2}+1)/n^2\) if and only if \(n\) is a prime power. We also give a formula for the connected intersection density of dicyclic groups. For generalized quaternion groups of order \(2N\), where \(N=2^{m-1}\geq 4\), the density is \(\frac{N^2+8}{2N(N+1)}\). For the elementary abelian group \(C_p^r\), where \(p\) is prime and \(r\geq 1\), the density is \(p^{1-r}\).

papers.title: Square-root cancellation in three hyperbolic counting problems via maximal estimates
papers.abstract: We study three counting problems for lattice orbits in hyperbolic space: counting orbit points within a prescribed distance of a fixed closed geodesic or a totally geodesic hyperplane, and counting orbit points above a prescribed height at a cusp. For almost every base point, we obtain error bounds of square-root size up to logarithmic factors. For the geodesic and hyperplane counts, these bounds match the conjectured exponents and improve earlier results due to Good and Laaksonen. For these two problems, we adapt the method of maximal estimates developed by Chatzakos and Dimakis for hyperbolic lattice counting, formulating it in both a discrete and a continuous framework. For the hyperplane problem, we also obtain an asymptotic formula for the spatial second moment of the error term, involving an almost periodic function. For the cusp problem, the square-root bound can be deduced from work of Yu, which incorporates Schmidt's dyadic maximal argument. We present a proof, together with an $\Omega$-result supporting the optimality of the exponent $1/2$ for at least one cusp of any group that is not essentially cuspidal. In contrast, for the modular group, we obtain a power saving over the exponent $1/2$ for every base point.

papers.title: DNN-Assisted Deterministic Policy Learning for Adaptive IRS-NOMA-OWC Networks
papers.authors: Ahrar N. Hamad, Ahmad A. Qidan, Taisir E. H. El-Gorashi, Jaafar M. H. Elmirghani
papers.abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has been considered a promising technology in optical wireless communication (OWC) networks due to its potential to overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) blockage issue and enhance coverage. In this paper, a dynamic IRS-assisted indoor non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-OWC network is modeled, and an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the sum rate subject to the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of multiple mobile users, by jointly optimizing the power allocation and the IRS mirror orientations, from which the user's decoding order is induced rather than being fixed. Since the problem is non-convex and the channel conditions vary with user mobility, conventional optimization methods may incur considerable computational overhead. Therefore, a two-stage deep neural network-deep reinforcement learning (DNN-DRL) framework is proposed. In the first stage, the DNN estimates the user's positions and orientations in real time, removing the need for perfect knowledge of the user state. In the second stage, a deterministic policy gradient (DPG)-based DRL algorithm uses these estimates to jointly optimize the power allocation and IRS mirror orientations, with the decoding order updated according to the resulting effective channel gains. The results show that the proposed framework approaches the performance upper bounds and outperforms standard DRL algorithms, conventional optimization methods, and deployments without IRS in terms of sum rate and fairness, while achieving faster convergence. Furthermore, online adaptation of the decoding order maintains higher QoS satisfaction than a fixed decoding order, particularly under high user mobility.

papers.title: Cohomology of twisted tensor products over commutative rings
papers.abstract: Over a commutative ground ring, cohomology of a twisted tensor product of two rings mixes their cohomology via the twisting. We focus on bicharacter twistings and give explicit descriptions when the ground ring is itself a module. We state our main results for ground rings that are hereditary and contain roots of unity corresponding to finite grading groups. As a class of examples, we compute cohomology rings of Taft orders over cyclotomic integers.

papers.title: Generalized anti-Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: The anti-Ramsey number was introduced by Erd\H{o}s, Simonovits, and S\'os and is defined to be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color the edges of a graph to avoid a rainbow copy of some graph. One can generalize this by, instead of forbidding a rainbow copy of a graph, putting a cap on the number of colors that appear on any copy of that graph. To be precise, let $\AR(G,H,q)$ be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color $E(G)$ so that every copy of $H$ sees at most $q$ colors. One can see that $\AR(G,H,q)$ is nondecreasing in $q$. In this paper, we investigate the linear and quadratic thresholds of $\AR(G,H,q)$ when $G=K_n$ and $H$ is connected.

papers.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $\xi$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

papers.title: Pathwise Factorization and Uncertainty Quantification for Impedance Obstacles with Random Boundaries
papers.abstract: We develop a factorization method with finite-sample statistical guarantees for two-dimensional acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles whose boundary is random and whose data are finitely many noisy multistatic measurements. In the two-dimensional far-field normalization, the symmetrization must act on a phase-rotated far-field operator; we prove the optical and range identities for every realization of a compact family of uniformly bi-Lipschitz domains, with jointly measurable regularized indicators. A quadrature-weighted finite-sample analysis separates angular approximation, measurement noise, test-vector error, and regularization, and yields a consistency theorem for empirical means and variances, joint in all data parameters. Bounded indicators admit simultaneous confidence bands, a diagonal threshold recovers the probability that a sampling point lies in the random obstacle, and a nested design yields unbiased variance components. Computations use a combined-field integral equation proved invertible at all frequencies, and the finite-grid guarantees are examined in a coverage study against a high-accuracy Monte Carlo reference.

papers.title: A reciprocal-matrix proof of Sendov's theorem and applications to control theory
papers.abstract: This proof grew out of the author's research on interpreting mathematical statements from the viewpoint of control theory. Its value lies both in the understanding it brings and in the applications that arise from the argument. Let $a$ be a simple zero of a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points, counted with multiplicity, then the reciprocals $1/(a-c_j)$ are the eigenvalues of an explicit matrix built from the other zeros. A failure of Sendov's bound at $a$ would therefore make the associated discrete-time system asymptotically stable. This observation leads to an alternative proof of the quadratic inequality of Tang and Zhang, including its equality case. Building on the reflection and centering arguments of Mazur, Tao and Zhang, we estimate the change in the integral of the derivative product when all the reciprocal displacements are replaced by their mean $s$. An exact pairwise cancellation bounds the difference in terms of the variance. For an interior zero rotated to $0<a<1$, the normalized trace $s$ determines a contour through $\overline{s}/a$. If the mean squared reciprocal distance is at most one, integration along this contour gives $(n-1)(2a\Re(s)-a^2)<20$. A uniform phase estimate and reflection at $1/a$ then rule out this possibility in every degree $n\ge 257$. A fourth-moment estimate treats degrees two through five. For degrees five through 256, three bounds derived from one polynomial moment identity exclude the full range of the two remaining real parameters by exact integer arithmetic. As an application, Sendov's theorem illustrates how differentiating the denominator of a closed-loop transfer function can increase robustness in discrete-time systems and decrease it in continuous-time systems. The proofs have been formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: An Optimal Liouville Theorem for the Fully Fractional Heat Equation
papers.authors: Yahong Guo, Yugao Ouyang, Jiongduo Xie
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonnegative entire classical solution of the fully fractional heat equation $(\partial_t-\Delta)^s u=u^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero for $n\geq2$, $0<s<1$, and $1<p<(n+2s)/(n-2s)$. No global boundedness, decay, or symmetry assumptions are required for the solutions. The exponent range is sharp, since the critical equation admits positive stationary solutions. Our result provides a fractional counterpart of Quittner's optimal Liouville theorem for the classical semilinear heat equation, while our proof follows a new and simpler approach. For bounded solutions, we combine elliptic nonexistence and compactness to control superlevel set measures by the local energy dissipation of the weighted extension. A local energy inequality then gives nonexistence by iteration. Doubling, local regularity, and a nonlocal convergence theorem yield a universal pointwise bound in terms of the parabolic distance to the boundary, which implies our Liouville theorem for general solutions.

papers.title: Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three
papers.abstract:
We prove that every sequence of lists of size three admits an infinite square-free word, establishing that the Thue choice number of the path is three. More precisely, the number of compatible square-free words of length $n$ is at least $c(5/4)^n$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.
  The proof combines a computer-assisted construction of weights with the weighted counting method previously introduced by the author. We first consider words avoiding only squares of bounded period and use a finite state model to certify a uniform lower bound on their growth. The counting argument then controls the loss caused by excluding longer squares. The main new ingredient is a coarser description of the states, which makes the computation feasible without restricting the union of the lists.
  The same computation yields a deterministic polynomial-time strategy for constructing an infinite square-free word when each list is chosen adversarially after the preceding letters have been fixed.

papers.title: A rigorous Abel-summed Hardy-type identity for $p$-circle domains via regularized Poisson summation
papers.abstract: In our previous work, a generalized Hardy-type identity (GHI) for astroid-type $p$-circle domains was formally derived in terms of generalized $p$-Bessel functions. However, the direct application of the Poisson summation formula to the indicator functions of these domains leaves the convergence and rigorous justification of the resulting oscillatory series unresolved. In the present paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an anisotropic regularization based on convolution kernels with Fourier multipliers $e^{-t(|\xi_{1}|^p+|\xi_{2}|^{p})}$. We establish the corresponding regularized Poisson summation identity and rigorously justify the limiting process through uniform estimates for lattice-point sums. A key feature of our analysis is the determination of boundary contributions: smooth boundary points carry weight $1/2$, whereas the contributions from axial cusps vanish for $0<p<1$. These results lead to an Abel-summed GHI, expressed in terms of the distorted-angle-dependent $p$-Bessel functions introduced in our previous work, with explicit boundary corrections. In particular, for $p=2$, the identity recovers the Abel-summed form of the classical Hardy--Vorono\"i Bessel series. Our result provides a rigorous regularized counterpart of the previously proposed identity, while the convergence of the corresponding unregularized series remains a separate problem.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
papers.authors: Levent Alp\"oge, Tristan Buckmaster, Matei P. Coiculescu
papers.abstract: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction.

papers.title: Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
papers.abstract: The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order H\"older source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius larger than the circumradius. For a simply connected obstacle with analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and conformal center inside the obstacle, a Faber--Vekua normal form gives the sharp spectral law in terms of logarithmic capacity, with the same leading constant as for the disc. This class includes every convex analytic obstacle. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral transition and illustrate its use in choosing the regularization level. The analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component.

papers.title: Isolation in Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $\gamma(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $\iota(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$. We also identify a transition in the gap $\gamma(G)-\iota(G)$ when $\log(1/p)=o(\log n)$. This gap tends to infinity in probability when $p$ is well below $(\log\log n/\log n)^2$ and is at most one with high probability when $p$ is well above this scale. Finally, for every fixed graph $F$, we show that the classical minimum degree bound for domination is asymptotically sharp for $F$-isolation, even for regular host graphs.

papers.title: Compression with wildcards: The maximum anticliques of K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graphs
papers.abstract: By definition a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph is such that the cardinality of each maximum matching equals the cardinality of each minimum vertex-cover. Each bipartite graph has this property. We unravel the structure of the family MACL(G) of all maximum anticliques (independent sets) of a K\"onig-Egarv\'ary graph G. This enables us to enumerate $MACL(G)$ not only in output polynomial time, but also in a compressed format (using wildcards). All of this can be viewed as an instance where ALL minimum solutions of a submodular function can be enumerated efficiently.

papers.title: Opposite filtrations on the parabolic compactified Jacobian
papers.abstract: We show that the Hikita filtration on the cohomology of the parabolic compactified Jacobian of the plane curve singularity $x^m=y^n$, $(m,n)=1$, is opposite to the perverse filtration in a precise sense. This implies the parabolic Hilb-vs-Quot conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19633, and consequently the main conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115 for these singularities. The new ingredient is an analysis of how the Bott-Mitchell filtration on the homology of the affine Grassmannian of $SL_n$ relates to both of the above filtrations.

papers.title: The 1-Loop and Ohtsuki-Takata Invariants for Alternating Braids
papers.abstract: In a step towards resolving the 1-loop conjecture, Ohtsuki and Takata defined their own eponymous invariant in terms of an open knot diagram, and showed that it is equal to the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for two-bridge knots. Garoufalidis and Yoon then showed that the 1-loop invariant is equal to the Ohtsuki-Takata invariant using a technique involving a collapsed octahedral decomposition. This paper expands those techniques to relate the matrix determinants of the 1-loop and Ohtsuki-Takata invariants for the case of reduced alternating braids.

papers.title: A functional Breuer-Major theorem under finite variance, with application to the $R/S$ test for long memory
papers.abstract:
The Breuer-Major theorem (Breuer and Major, 1983) states that, for a function $G$ of Hermite rank $m$ such that $\mathbb{E}(G^{2}(X))<\infty$, and a stationary Gaussian sequence whose correlation function $r$ satisfies $\sum_{i}|r(i)|^{m}<\infty$, the finite dimensional distributions of the normalized partial sum process of $G(X_{i})$ converge to those of a Brownian motion. Whether the functional version of this result holds under these sole conditions has remained open for a long time, the tightness being known only under additional moment assumptions. In this paper we prove that the functional central limit theorem holds under finite variance only. More generally, we give a high order expansion of the partial sum process which covers both short and long-range dependence: the long-range dependent components converge to Hermite processes, while the remainder converges to a Brownian motion.
  As an application, we discuss the question of testing long-memory in observed data using the $R/S$ statistics. We derive the limiting distributions of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics, prove the consistency of the test and propose a data-driven choice of the truncation parameter. A Monte Carlo study compares the performances of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics for both short-memory and long-memory sequences.

papers.title: Thurston measure is stationary with exponential Teichm\"uller moment
papers.abstract: In 1967, Furstenberg proved that every lattice in a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center admits a probability measure whose stationary measure on the associated Furstenberg boundary belongs to the Lebesgue measure class. We prove an analogue of this theorem for the action of the mapping class group on Teichm\"uller space. Every regular probability measure in the Thurston measure class on the space of projective measured foliations is the stationary measure of a non-elementary random walk with a finite exponential moment in the Teichm\"uller metric.

papers.title: Nonholonomic Event-Triggered Source Seeking
papers.authors: Victor Hugo Pereira Rodrigues, Tiago Roux Oliveira, Miroslav Krstic
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an event-triggered source seeking control (ET-SSC) strategy for autonomous vehicles modeled as nonholonomic unicycles. The key feature of the proposed design is the separation between the continuous probing motion required for gradient extraction and the event-triggered update of the source-seeking correction. This separation enables aperiodic computation and transmission of the correction while the periodic probing signals remain continuously active. The triggering mechanism acts on a low-pass-filtered gradient estimate, obtained by high-pass (washout) filtering, demodulation, and low-pass filtering of the measured signal, and combines a relative and an absolute threshold. Stability is proved with a time-periodic Lyapunov function constructed along the exponentially stable periodic solution of the filtered closed loop, establishing practical exponential convergence of the vehicle to a neighborhood of the unknown source. The guaranteed minimum dwell time is strictly positive and independent of the probing frequency, which excludes Zeno behavior. Unlike available Lie-bracket analyses of the forward-velocity design, the proposed averaging-based analysis accommodates anisotropic quadratic source fields with distinct spatial curvatures. The resulting ET-SSC framework therefore provides a resource-aware implementation in which the source-seeking correction is updated aperiodically while the information-generating probing motion remains continuous.

papers.title: Studies on a Relationship Between Tate Homology and Local Cohomology of Tensor Products of Modules
papers.authors: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Olgur Celikbas, Arash Sadeghi
papers.abstract: We study the local cohomology of finitely generated modules with respect to specialization-closed subsets over commutative Noetherian rings. Our main result establishes a relationship between the local cohomology of tensor products of modules and Tate homology over Gorenstein rings. We present several consequences of our main result, which are of independent interest. For example, we study various aspects of the cohomological rigidity property of tensor products of modules and generalize results of Huneke-Wiegand in this direction. We determine conditions under which the vanishing of a single local cohomology module of a tensor product implies the vanishing of all lower ones, establish bounds for the depth of tensor products of modules, and obtain criteria for freeness of modules over complete intersection rings. Along the way, we also provide a splitting criterion for vector bundles on smooth complete intersections.

papers.title: Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
papers.authors: Kaiyue He, Faisal Suwayyid, Guo-Wei Wei
papers.abstract: We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of \`Alvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $\lambda_{p,q}(\kk[\Delta])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.

papers.title: Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.authors: Tina Torabi, Cheuk Hin Ho, Christoph Ortner, Ruo Ning Qiu
papers.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.

papers.title: A Column-Generation Approach to Length-Constrained Shortest Paths under Cascading Causal Failures
papers.authors: Nicol\`o Aicardi, Zuyuan Zhang, Sridhar Radhakrishnan, Kash Barker, Dritan Nace
papers.abstract: In the study of cascading causal node failures, the failure of one set of nodes can trigger the failure of another, possibly non-adjacent, set, and these triggers can propagate in cascades. Given a graph, a set of causal failures, a source-terminal pair, and a constant $\alpha \geq 1$, we study the length-constrained shortest-path problem of finding the maximum subset of causalities whose application preserves a source-terminal path of length at most $\alpha$ times the original distance. We show that the problem is NP-hard, a hardness that reflects the non-local, cascading nature of causal failures. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming formulation with explicit node-integrity variables that decouple the node state from routing, a column-generation algorithm built on a path-based reformulation whose pricing subproblem is solved by a three-level cascade (beam search, label-capped $A^*$, and exact $A^*$ with warm start), and a greedy heuristic as a fast baseline. On the IEEE 300 and Power 5000 benchmarks, all three methods are competitive. In dense synthetic networks of 10,000 to 15,000 nodes, the exact model exhausts its time budget or returns an order of magnitude fewer causalities, whereas column generation remains fast and accurate, emerging as the method of choice for large instances.

papers.title: Polynomial sequences of Simplex pivots on 0/1-polytopes
papers.abstract:
We study the number of Simplex pivots needed to solve linear programs over $0/1$-polytopes, starting from an arbitrary feasible basis and counting degenerate pivots. It has been known since the 1990s that from any extreme point of a 0/1-polytope there exists a monotone path of linear length to an optimal one. However, translating this into a polynomial sequence of Simplex pivots, i.e., improving basis exchanges, has remained an open question.
  We here provide an affirmative answer, showing that for every 0/1-polytope $\mathcal P \subseteq \mathbb R^d$, an optimal basis can be reached with $O(d^3)$ Simplex pivots, independently of the number of inequalities and of the size of the coefficients.

papers.title: Large 4-tangles in matroids are characterized by large internally 4-connected minors
papers.authors: Nick Brettell, Johannes Carmesin, Tony Huynh, Matthew E. Kroeker, Florian Lehner, Geoff Whittle
papers.abstract: Tangles were first introduced by Robertson and Seymour as an abstract way of treating highly connected substructures in graphs and matroids. For any truly highly connected substructure in a graph or matroid, all of the low-order separations in the object can be oriented towards it. This gives rise to a tangle. A standard question is whether every tangle of a given order in fact arises from some concrete highly connected substructure, such as a minor. It is well known that tangles of order two and three (in both graphs and matroids) are characterized by maximal $2$-connected and $3$-connected minors, respectively. For tangles of order four, it is necessary to consider a weaker notion of connectivity. Carmesin and Kurkofka showed that, for graphs, internal $4$-connectedness suffices. For matroids, Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple and Whittle showed that $4$-tangles arise from weakly $4$-connected minors, that is, minors in which every $3$-separation has a side with at most four elements. In the latter case, the breadth of the tangle (a measure of its complexity) can be preserved exactly, but the authors also asked whether a stronger notion of $4$-connectivity could be used while preserving some fraction of the breadth. In this paper, we answer this question in the affirmative by showing that, in a matroid, any $4$-tangle of sufficiently large breadth is determined by an internally $4$-connected minor whose unique $4$-tangle also has large breadth.

papers.title: The double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We adapt the near-far argument of Hadama and Toyoshima to establish the double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations.

papers.title: Hypocoercivity estimates via maximum principle in short and long time scales
papers.abstract: We prove decay estimates for a large class of linear drift-diffusion operators with hypoelliptic structure. In the main example, the diffusion consists of (possibly superposing) local or nonlocal operators acting on a restricted set of variables, while diffusivity is transported to the whole space thanks to H\"ormander-type conditions on the drift term. We prove both short-time and long-time oscillation estimates on the solutions, including bounded-to-Lipschitz smoothing in the sharp time scale and exponential decay, as time goes to infinity, whenever a strict supersolution, with the role of Lyapunov function, is supposed to exist. The estimates are proved with a unifying approach relying on doubling variables and coupling methods, using maximum principle in suitably time scaled moving frames. Applications range from nonlocal kinetic Fokker-Planck equations to heat conduction models in a chain of coupled oscillators.

papers.title: Analytic Projective Finsler Metrics and Sprays
papers.abstract:
We study projective Finsler metrics and sprays on an open subset $U$ of $R^n$. They are characterized by the Hamel equations \[
  P_{x^m y^k}y^m=P_{x^k}, \] where $P=P(x, y)$ are function on $TU$ with positive homogeneity: $P(x, cy)= c (x,y)$, $c >0$. This is the Hilbert's Fourth problem in the regular case. We determine all solutions analytic in the base variable. We compare this local representation with earlier work on Hilbert's fourth problem and with the restricted Taylor expansions arising for projective Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature. We conclude with explicit nonlinear projective Finsler metrics and sprays on Euclidean space, including one-sided complete examples and a nonflat complete example.

papers.title: A dynamic variational principle on phase space for Wasserstein cubic splines
papers.abstract: Wasserstein cubic splines have been introduced to provide a smooth interpolation in time between prescribed probability measures on $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Their construction for $N$ measures is based on a multi-marginal optimal transport problem on a space of dimension $N\! \cdot \! d$, thus becoming very high-dimensional already for a small number of prescribed measures. We prove that the dimension can be reduced to a fixed number $2d+1$ via a dynamic variational principle on phase space. We also give an example showing that the Monge ansatz, which would also reduce the dimension to a fixed number, fails to capture exact solutions and is in general ill-posed, even for absolutely continuous measures.

papers.title: Inexact Proximal Method on Hadamard Manifolds
papers.authors: M. S. Louzeiro, R. Serra, S. Vieira
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze two inexact proximal point methods for unconstrained geodesically convex optimization on Hadamard manifolds. The first, a standard inexact proximal point method (SIPPM), accepts approximate subproblem solutions directly as new iterates and applies to arbitrary Hadamard manifolds under a summability condition on the relative error tolerances. The second, a hybrid inexact proximal point method (IHPPM), augments each inexact proximal step with a metric projection onto a half-space-like separating set, allowing the summability requirement to be relaxed to a fixed relative error tolerance at the cost of assuming geodesic convexity of the separating sets. For both methods we establish full asymptotic convergence, global $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iteration-complexity bounds for approximate stationarity, and, under a local growth condition, local $Q$-linear convergence rates---with $Q$-superlinear acceleration for SIPPM when the proximal parameters tend to zero and a refined contraction factor for IHPPM. We further prove that the geodesic convexity of the separating sets holds automatically on Hadamard surfaces and on Hadamard manifolds of constant sectional curvature.

papers.title: Finite propagation speed for evolutionary equations
papers.abstract: We study finite speed of propagation in the framework of evolutionary equations introduced by Rainer Picard in 2009. We establish sufficient conditions on the material law, which is represented by an analytic and bounded operator-valued function, and the unbounded spatial operator that ensure finite speed of propagation of information for solutions. Assuming a linear-in-frequency coercivity bound for spatially local material laws, we prove propagation on backward light cones for weighted $L_2$ solutions without a finite initial time, thus identifying hyperbolic-type evolutionary equations. The characteristic-speed threshold depends on the coercive coefficient and the principal spatial matrices, but not on bounded memory or delay terms or potential positive fractional temporal contributions. We illustrate the result with the scalar wave equation, Maxwell's equations, a fractional model in elasticity, and dual-phase-lag thermoelasticity.

papers.title: Small spherical 7-designs in prime dimensions
papers.abstract: For every prime $p\ge 29$, we construct an antipodal spherical $7$-design on $S^{p-1}$ with $42(p-1)(p+2)^2$ points. The construction uses eigenlines of finite Weil operators.

papers.title: Structure of linear extensions of posets and lexicographic shelling
papers.abstract: We study some structure of linear extensions of a finite poset $P$ by investigating partial orders on the maximal chains of the lattice of order ideals $J(P)$. These partial orders on the maximal chains of $J(P)$ are called maximal chain descent orders (MCDO). MCDOs come from EL-labelings of finite bounded posets and encode the structure of shellings arising from EL-labelings. Every linear extension of $P$ gives an EL-labeling of $J(P)$, and so generates an MCDO. Our main question is: when do different linear extensions of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs? We give partial answers to this question. In particular, we prove that linear extensions that are related by an automorphism of $P$ result in isomorphic MCDOs. Additionally, we show that for a certain family of posets, a linear extension $l$ and Sch\"utzenberger's evacuation of $l$ generate isomorphic MCDOs. In this case, the isomorphism comes from a well known isomorphism of the weak order on permutations.

papers.title: Yau's first eigenvalue conjecture for embedded minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Let $M^n$ be a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere. Suppose that $M$ has constant scalar curvature. We prove that its first positive Laplace eigenvalue is $n$ and that the ambient coordinate functions span its first eigenspace. To prove both assertions, we consider an eigenfunction $f$ with eigenvalue $0<\lambda\le n$ orthogonal to every coordinate function. We use $f$ as the density of a single-layer potential on the sphere. The geometry of $M$ gives a lower bound for the Dirichlet energy of this potential. The spherical heat kernel gives a smaller upper bound for the same energy. This contradiction rules out every such nonzero $f$.

papers.title: On the cyclic and dihedral Ramsey numbers of separated caterpillars and nested matchings
papers.authors: Ivan Damnjanovi\'c, Daniil Furmanov, Jon A. Maccarello, Julien Menet
papers.abstract:
We consider all graphs to have vertex sets of the form $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n-1\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For graphs $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$, the cyclic Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is the smallest $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $k$-edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H_j$ in color $j$ for some $j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$, with the vertices appearing in the same cyclic order as in $H_j$. The dihedral Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ is defined analogously, with the difference that the direction of the cyclic order is ignored.
  For $n \ge 2$, a separated caterpillar of order $n$ is a graph obtained by a cyclic shift of the vertex labels from a tree of order $n$ whose edges can be written as $u_1 v_1, u_2 v_2, \ldots, u_{n-1} v_{n-1}$ so that $u_1 \leq u_2 \le \cdots \le u_{n-1} < v_{n-1} \le \cdots \le v_2 \le v_1$, while the trivial graph $K_1$ is the separated caterpillar of order one. For even $n \ge 2$, the nested matching of order $n$ is the $1$-regular graph in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $n - 1 - v$.
  We prove that if $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k$ are separated caterpillars, then $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ and $R_{\mathrm{dih}}(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_k)$ are both equal to the Ramsey number of stars of the same orders, which was determined by Burr and Roberts. We also prove that $R_{\mathrm{cyc}}(F, H) = R_{\mathrm{dih}}(F, H) = 1 + (a-1)(b-1)$ for any graph $F$ of order $a \ge 2$ in which each vertex $v$ is adjacent to $(v + 1) \bmod a$ and any separated caterpillar $H$ of order $b \in \mathbb{N}$. Moreover, we determine the multicolor cyclic Ramsey numbers whose arguments are stars and nested matchings, provided that at most one of these nested matchings has order divisible by four. Some special cases of these results were recently obtained by Kucheriya, Petr and Yan.

papers.title: On a potential type II singular model of the Navier Stokes equations
papers.abstract: It is shown that a particular class of partial type I or type II functions are not singularity models for the three dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with or without smooth, compactly supported forces. This extends part of the results for the axially symmetric case to the full three dimension case. Some connections to the recent literature are also discussed.

papers.title: Steady Generalized Ricci Solitons with SO(3) Symmetries in Dimension Three
papers.abstract: We completely classify all gradient, complete, steady generalized Ricci solitons in dimension three with $SO(3)$ symmetry, extending a result of Podest\'a-Raffero. We further extend this analysis to $n$-forms on $n$-manifolds with an $SO(n)$ symmetry.

papers.title: The Strong AJ Conjecture for Hyperbolic Prime Knots is False
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a knot in $S^3$. The strong AJ conjecture relates two of its invariants. The first is the minimal-order annihilator $\widehat A$ of the $n$th colored Jones polynomial $J(n)$. The second is the two-variable $A$-polynomial of Cooper, Culler, Gillet, Long, and Shalen. The conjecture says that after specialization $\varepsilon^*(\widehat A)\asymp A$. Zhang gave the first family of composite-knot counterexamples. For $8_{11}$ the specialization of $\widehat A$ carries an extra trefoil factor $L+M^6$. We prove this by verifying L\^e's $\widehat P=\widehat A$ conjecture. Zhang's corrected formulation of the AJ conjecture agrees with L\^e's weak AJ conjecture, which we prove for $8_{11}$. Li, Li, and Sun have since reported counterexamples of the weak AJ conjecture among non-hyperbolic prime knots. This work was AI assisted, and parts of it have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
papers.abstract: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of DRL methods depends on the evaluation setting: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and its recurrent variant are the only methods that improve on the QMIP both in fully simulated races and when the actual 2024 races are replayed. Averaged over eight circuits, PPO improves on the QMIP by 0.33 and 0.49 positions in the two settings and Recurrent PPO by less, and in the replay PPO finishes 0.66 positions ahead of the drivers' actual strategies simulated in the same races. The QMIP performs similarly to the other methods, even though it cannot anticipate yellow flag events. Finally, we use the trained PPO policy as a look-ahead decision-support tool that shows the strategist the distribution of race outcomes under each candidate pit-stop action. Applied retrospectively to eight 2024 races, the look-ahead identifies the laps where the actual decision, the recommendation, or a third action was preferable.

papers.title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
papers.abstract:
Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(\Delta^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $\Delta$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants.
  A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides with the Kashiwara--Kim--Oh--Park seed of $\Delta^{m-2}$. Hence it is the quantum Grothendieck ring of a monoidal localization, at the frozen modules, of a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(\Delta^{m-2})$ with the same simple objects, and a quantization of the braid variety $X(\Delta^{m-1})$. The whole algebra $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ is a skew Laurent extension of $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ in $(m-1)(n-1)$ frozen variables.

papers.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

papers.title: On generation of the coefficient field of a primitive HMF by a single Fourier coefficient: An application of Nekov\'a\v{r}'s Theorem
papers.abstract:
Let $f$ be a non-CM primitive Hilbert modular form (HMF) over a totally real number field, of parallel even weight $k\geq 2$, with coefficient field $E_f$, and let $F_f \subseteq E_f$ denote the field fixed by the inner twists of $f$.
  In this article, we establish an analogue of Ribet's large image theorem for the residual Galois representations associated with $f$, by applying Nekov\'a\v{r}'s large image theorem (cf.~\cite[Theorem B.5.2]{Nek12}) to the automorphic representation $\pi(f)$ associated with $f$. As a result, we prove that if $f$ has no nontrivial inner twists, then $E_f$ is generated by a single prime Fourier coefficient, for a set of prime ideals of Dirichlet density one. We derive this result as a consequence of a more general theorem established for $F_f$.

papers.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
papers.abstract: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^\alpha(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $\alpha$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$. We derive this relation and the two initial congruences using theta-function dissections. A separate theta-series argument establishes divisibility by $8$.

papers.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
papers.authors: Wenyi Wang, Lei Li, Yiwen Lin
papers.abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

papers.title: Tensor products of additive groups as reciprocity sheaves
