papers.abstract: We compute the Nisnevich reciprocity sheaves associated with tensor products of the cube-invariant objects for the additive and multiplicative groups, with at least one additive factor. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, these sheaves decompose into direct sums of absolute K$\"a$hler differential sheaves with binomial multiplicities. As an application, we compute the associated reciprocity sheaves of the Hochschild homology of the additive object.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.

papers.title: Strong numerical radius orthogonality on bounded linear operators
papers.authors: Shaoxing Sun (Air force engineering university), Xiaofei Qi (Shanxi University), Jinchuan Hou (Taiyuan University of technology)
papers.abstract: Orthogonality is an important tool for studying bounded linear operators. In this paper, we introduce the concept of strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators and then, discuss the properties about numerical radius orthogonality, strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators as well as relationship between them.

papers.title: Stability of independence polynomials of well-covered Ferrers graphs
papers.authors: Ta Quang Anh, Do Trong Hoang, Nguyen Minh Nhat
papers.abstract: We prove that every root of the independence polynomial of a well-covered Ferrers graph lies in the open unit disk centered at $-1$, that is, $|x+1|<1$. Consequently, the polynomial is strictly stable. We also exhibit a general Ferrers graph whose independence polynomial is not stable.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian quotient equations on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Dirichlet problem for a class of sum Hessian quotient equations involving a gradient term on the right-hand side on Riemannian manifolds. Under the assumption of the existence of a subsolution, based on the a priori estimates for the solutions, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of $(k-1)$-admissible solutions for the Dirichlet problem on compact Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundary. Our existence results cover the case $0\le l<k<n$ with $k\ge 2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $(k-1)$-admissible, and the case $k=n$ with $0\le l\le n-2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $n$-admissible.

papers.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
papers.abstract: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.

papers.title: $n$-absorbing ideals of rings of continuous functions I: minimal primes, common zero sets, and non-$z$ ideals
papers.abstract: Let $C(X)$ be the ring of real-valued continuous functions on a Tychonoff space $X$, and for an ideal $I$ let $\K(I)$ be the set of common zeros of its members. We show that a proper $z$-ideal of $C(X)$ is $n$-absorbing if and only if it has at most $n$ minimal primes, if and only if it is an intersection of at most $n$ pairwise incomparable primes, if and only if its filter of zero sets is $n$-absorbing; the algebraic part of this equivalence is valid for radical ideals of any commutative ring. We prove that $|\K(I)|\le n$ for every $n$-absorbing ideal $I$ and that this bound is sharp. We further prove that the $z$-closure of every $n$-absorbing ideal is an $n$-absorbing $z$-ideal and has the same common zero set. Finally, every $n$-absorbing ideal of $C(X)$ is a $z$-ideal if and only if $X$ is a $P$-space. Moreover, for every non-unit $f\in C(X)$, the principal ideal $(f)$ is $n$-absorbing if and only if $\Z(f)$ is clopen and $(f)$ has at most $n$ minimal prime ideals.

papers.title: Persistent Mayer Path Homology and Mayer Path Laplacian
papers.abstract: In topological data analysis, path homology accounts for directed graph while combinatorial Laplacian extends homology groups to spectral theory. However, these approaches are built on a boundary operator with condition $\partial^2=0$. Mayer homology replaces this condition with $N$-nilpotent boundary map $\partial^N=0$. By using the primitive $N$-th root of unity in the boundary operator, it relates each degree $n$ to the degrees $n-q$ and $n+N-q$. This work introduces persistent Mayer path homology. We show that Mayer path homology is functorial for strict digraph maps, which gives persistent Mayer path homology for filtered digraphs, and prove that its barcodes are stable under perturbations. For $N=3$ we derive formulas that reduce $\beta_0^{3,1}$ and $\beta_2^{3,2}$ to the classes of vertices identified by squares and the rank of a small matrix indexed by triangles. We also introduce the Mayer path Laplacian and its persistence theory, prove that their kernels recover (persistent) Mayer path homology, show that they distinguish digraphs with the same Mayer path Betti numbers, and prove a stability bound for the eigenvalues of the persistent up-Laplacian. We demonstrate that persistent Mayer path homology detects the formation of feed-forward loops, whose formation is not detected by ordinary path homology. In an application to cucurbit[7]uril, filtered by an interatomic distance normalized by van der Waals radii, Mayer path homology separates contacts that only close cycles from contacts that close feed-forward triangles, and changes at almost four times as many filtration values as path homology after the bonded framework is formed.

papers.title: A simple approach to ends of manifolds and the Freudenthal compactification
papers.abstract: In this note we give an alternative definition of the Freudenthal end-compactification of a non-compact manifold by defining ends to be the filters of open subsets with compact boundaries that have a base of connected subsets. We start by defining these notions and proving that the resulting compactification is equivalent to the Freudenthal compactification. In particular, we explicitly discuss the equivalence between our definitions and those from two different approaches: maximal binding families and inverse limits. After that, we give an example of a non-metrizable manifold, showing how these new definitions make it easier to identify ends and understand the topology of the end-compactification. We also prove a well-known metrization theorem, showing an application of our definition. Finally, we also give an alternative proof of the topological characterization of the Freudenthal compactification.

papers.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.

papers.title: The upward conformal limit
papers.abstract: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, both the Higgs bundle moduli space and the de Rham moduli space have stratifications by holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations over the space of complex variations of Hodge structure. The $\hbar$-conformal limit gives a biholomorphic identification of the fibers of the two strata over a stable complex variation of Hodge structure. We introduce here the $\hbar$-upward conformal limit, which is the limit at infinity rather than at zero. The main results of this paper relate the irreducible components of the nilpotent cone on $X$, which are Lagrangian submanifolds, with Lagrangians in the Morse strata on $\bar{X}$, called zero velocity Lagrangians, via the $\hbar$-upward conformal limit. In particular, Higgs bundles that flow up to the zero of the Hitchin section on $X$ are identified with opers on $\bar{X}$.

papers.title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
papers.abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

papers.title: The Order of the Inertia Bound for Random Graphs
papers.abstract: For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $n_{\geq0}(G)$ be the minimum number of nonnegative eigenvalues among zero-diagonal Hermitian matrices supported on $G$, allowing zero edge weights. For $n\geq2$ and $G\sim G(n,1/2)$, we prove $n_{\geq0}(G)\geq c_2n/\log(2n)$ with probability at least $1-\exp(-c_1n\log(2n))$, where $c_1,c_2>0$ are absolute constants. This proves a Hermitian extension of the Kwan--Wigderson conjecture. With high probability, $n_{\geq0}(G)=\Theta(n/\log n)$ and $n_{\geq0} G)/\alpha(G)=\Theta(n/(\log n)^2)$, where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number. Using Alon's constructions, we obtain, for every sufficiently large $n$, a $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ and $n_{\geq0}(G)=\Omega(n^{1/3})$. For infinitely many $n$, we also obtain $n$-vertex graphs $H$ with Shannon capacity $3$ and $n_{\geq0}(H)=\Omega(n^{1/4})$.

papers.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
papers.abstract:
The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story.
  During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve.
  We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, someone must judge whether the definitions and statements express the intended mathematics and whether future updates preserve that meaning. This work, even when done, can only be trusted. We must therefore return to the usual trust model: relying on the mathematical judgment of maintainers and expert communities.
  But semantic review is expensive, making it tempting to keep producing code and take successful kernel checks as sufficient grounds for trust. This shortcut accumulates semantic debt: definitions and results with unchecked mathematical interpretations are reused as foundations for further work. A library may keep compiling and produce the desired formal theorem while users lose track of which mathematical claims they can responsibly rely on.
  Reliable reuse is also a prerequisite for Terence Tao's vision of formal mathematics as something people can navigate, explain, learn from, and build with. This paper takes our work connecting the VOA and CFSG repositories for the Moonshine Conjecture as a case study of the challenges of reliable reuse as formal developments scale.

papers.title: A linearly decoupled structure-preserving BCFD method for the two-species Keller--Segel chemotaxis system
papers.authors: Ao Zhang, Bingyin Zhang, Hongfei Fu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a fully discrete, linearly decoupled block-centered finite difference scheme for the two-species Keller--Segel chemotaxis system. Based on the Slotboom transformation, the cell-density equations are reformulated into a symmetric form, providing a natural framework for the construction of a structure-preserving discretization. The resulting scheme is shown to unconditionally preserve the positivity of both the cell densities and the chemoattractant concentration, while ensuring exact mass conservation of each cell density and the original energy dissipation. Furthermore, optimal-order error estimates for the proposed scheme are rigorously established through a higher-order consistency analysis. In particular, the cell densities exhibit first-order temporal and second-order spatial convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm, whereas the chemoattractant concentration achieves the same convergence orders in the discrete $H^1$-norm. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to verify the theoretical results and demonstrate the reliability of the proposed scheme in simulating the finite-time blow-up phenomenon.

papers.title: The Ritt problem is decidable
papers.authors: Jason Fang, James Freitag, Matthew Harrison-Trainor
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative solution to the Ritt problem.

papers.title: Nowhere-zero $9$-flows of signed graphs
papers.authors: Miaomiao Han, Jiaao Li, Rong Luo, Xiangqian Zhou
papers.abstract: In 1983, Bouchet conjectured that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $6$-flow. DeVos et al.\ proved that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $11$-flow. In this paper, we show that every flow-admissible signed graph admits a nowhere-zero $9$-flow.

papers.title: Constructing toric diagonal modules with short linear resolutions
papers.abstract: For a complete simplicial toric variety $X$, we construct a collection of Cohen--Macaulay modules with linear resolutions where the associated sheaf is the diagonal. Through this work, we see that the resolutions constructed by Favero--Huang from homotopy path algebras and those constructed by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev can be viewed as two dual methods to construct resolutions of the diagonal starting from a compatible $\mathbb{Z}^n$-stratification.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
papers.authors: Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky
papers.abstract: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.

papers.title: Carleman estimates and $\phi$-null controllability for a fully discrete fourth-order parabolic equation
papers.authors: P\'ia Bizama, V\'ictor Hern\'andez-Santamar\'ia, Ariel A. P\'erez, Jose Solarte
papers.abstract: We consider a fully discrete approximation of a one-dimensional fourth-order parabolic equation with clamped boundary conditions, obtained by centered finite differences in space and the implicit Euler method in time, and controlled by two boundary controls acting at the left endpoint. We prove a Carleman estimate for the corresponding discrete adjoint operator, in which the large Carleman parameter is connected to the space and time discretization parameters $h$ and $\Delta t$. As a consequence, we obtain a relaxed observability inequality and a $\phi(h)$-null controllability result, in which the controls are bounded uniformly with respect to $h$ and $\Delta t$, and the norm of the solution at the final time is of order $\sqrt{\phi(h)}$, with $\phi(h)$ exponentially small, provided $\Delta t\le h^{\mu}$ for some $\mu\ge1$.

papers.title: An explicit Cassels--Tate pairing in characteristic $2$ and the parity of $2$-Selmer ranks
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a global field of characteristic $2$ and $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ the Verschiebung of an ordinary elliptic curve $E/K$ with a rational point of order $2$. We prove an explicit formula for the homogeneous-space Cassels--Tate pairing on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$ as a sum of local Artin--Schreier symbols, show that it coincides with Kramer's descent pairing and, on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$, with the pairing induced by Milne's flat duality, and deduce that it is non-degenerate on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]/\hat\varphi(\Sha(E'/K)[2])$. For every ordinary elliptic curve $A/K$ we express the parity of $\mathrm{rk}\,A(K)+\dim\Sha(A/K)[2]$ by local terms (after Kramer), and identify these with local root numbers at places of semistable or potentially multiplicative reduction, and in further cases using curves with finite $\Sha$. We determine $\Sha$ in examples, and extend the formula to rational points of any prime order $\ell$, the new case being $\ell=\operatorname{char}K$.

papers.title: Inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator: a computational perspective
papers.authors: Peter C. Gibson, Basant Lal Sharma
papers.abstract: We revisit inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator with compactly supported perturbation. We consider a computational perspective, adapted to the case of a digitally sampled reflection coefficient, to determine the perturbation in the form of a Jacobi matrix, including a computation of the length of the smallest interval supporting the perturbation. A new representation of scattering data in terms of orthogonal polynomials underpins the computational results. A key technical role is played by polynomials on the circle constructed from pairs of successive orthogonal polynomials on the line. The inverse algorithm is demonstrated on numerical examples.

papers.title: Period maps and the $C_{\rm st}$ conjecture
papers.authors: Pierre Colmez, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}, Xinyu Shao
papers.abstract:
We construct a family of elliptic curves over an open disc whose total space violates the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture in degree $1$. Hence the conjecture, known for proper and for Stein varieties, as well as for products of such, does not extend to proper families over Stein bases.
  This is an instance of a general criterion: the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture holds for the total space of a smooth proper family over a sufficiently small open disc if and only if its period map is constant, i.e., all Gauss--Manin Higgs fields vanish or, equivalently, the $p$-adic local systems $R^if_*\mathbf{Q}_p$ are geometrically constant. This criterion is special to curves: over a $2$-dimensional polydisc, we give a family of $p$-adic analogues of non-K\"ahler elliptic surfaces whose period maps and local systems are constant, but whose total space violates the conjecture.

papers.title: Real-analytic actions of lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact $n$-manifolds
papers.abstract: We classify real-analytic actions of arbitrary lattices in $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ on compact connected $n$-manifolds without boundary, $n\geq 3$, with no invariant-volume assumption. After finite-index restriction, the action has finite image, extends to a connected Lie group locally isomorphic to $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ with an equivariant finite cover when needed, or is obtained by analytic surgery with at least one torus piece. In the last case the lattice is commensurable with a conjugate of $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb Z)$. As a main input, we prove a general cocycle superrigidity theorem for real analytic germs.

papers.title: Sparse IRSs in Acylindrically Hyperbolic Groups that Surject Onto $\mathbb{Z}$
papers.abstract: For a non-elementary acylindrically hyperbolic group $\Gamma$ that surjects onto the integers, we construct an invariant random subgroup $\Lambda$ of $\Gamma$ for which the expected word-length of the shortest non-trivial element of $\Lambda$ is infinite. We refer to these as ``sparse" IRSs. The construction employs properties of renewal processes on $\mathbb{Z}$ as well as work of Dahmani, Guirardel, and Osin (arxiv:1111.7048v5) on the freeness of normal closures of certain elements in non-elementary acylindrically hyperbolic groups. We contrast this with the case of property (T) groups which cannot possess such IRSs. As an application, we answer a question posed in (arxiv:1612.09510v1) by constructing IRSs of $\mathrm{Isom}^+(\mathbb{H}^n)$ which have infinite expected injectivity radius, something which is impossible for higher-rank geometries due to work by Abert, Bergeron, et al. (arxiv:1210.2961v4)

papers.title: Long-time existence for wave systems with derivative nonlinearities
papers.authors: Wei Dai, Mengyun Liu, Chengbo Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study wave systems with power-type derivative nonlinearities in space dimensions $n\geq3$, for small, spherically symmetric initial data. Under suitable assumptions on the nonlinear powers, we establish global existence and sharp lifespan lower bounds. To achieve this, we develop weighted energy and local energy estimates adapted to the null directions, together with corresponding pointwise decay estimates.

papers.title: Demazure-Lusztig type operators and correspondences on Kato Catalan varieties
papers.abstract: We study the integral equivariant cohomology rings of Kato Catalan varieties $\mathscr{X}_\Psi$ associated with arbitrary root ideals $\Psi$ in type $A$. These varieties are smooth projective compactifications of the vector subbundles $T^*_\Psi\mathcal{B}$ of the cotangent bundle of the complete flag variety $\mathcal{B}$. Let $K$ denote the product of the general linear group (or its maximal torus) with the loop rotation torus $\mathbb{C}^\times$. We give an explicit presentation of $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_\Psi;\mathbb{Z})$ with relations expressed in terms of divided difference and Demazure-Lusztig type operators. Furthermore, for every simple reflection preserving $\Psi\cup(-\Psi)$, we construct a geometric realization of the associated Demazure-Lusztig type operator on $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_\Psi;\mathbb{Z})$ via correspondences. These correspondences yield a faithful graded action of the subalgebra of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra generated by these reflections and the polynomial subalgebra. For the maximal root ideal $\Psi=\Delta^+$, our construction recovers the cohomological counterpart of the $K$-theoretic Steinberg correspondences of Cautis and Kamnitzer.

papers.title: Stable phase retrieval from operator measurements
papers.authors: Deanna Needell, Yaniv Plan, Tomasz Szczepanski, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz
papers.abstract:
A known result of Cahill, Casazza and Daubechies [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B3(2016), 63-76] states that no frame in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space does stable phase retrieval. We show that stable recovery becomes possible for more general operator measurements, but only at a single exponent. Given a system of bounded operators $\{A_j\}_{j\in J}$ on a real or complex Hilbert space $H$, we study recovery of $f\in H$ up to a global phase from the quadratic measurements $\langle A_j f,f\rangle$ and from their phase preserving square roots.
  We consider $p$-Bessel systems ($2\leq p<\infty$) for which we measure the quadratic data in $\ell_{p/2}$ and the square root data in $\ell_p$. In infinite dimensions, we show that whenever $p\neq 4$, no $p$-Bessel system of operators does stable phase retrieval. In the case of $p=4$, we show that stability still fails on any system of semidefinite operators. Nevertheless, we construct a system of rank-one operators, not all self-adjoint, for which stable recovery is possible. We also show that stability can be achieved on a system of self-adjoint operators of rank-two.
  For both types of measurements, we show that the stability can be tested on orthogonal pairs. This reduction preserves the optimal constant for quadratic measurements and, when the operators are semidefinite, for their phase preserving square roots. We deduce that in finite dimensions, uniqueness of recovery implies its stability.
  Finally, we show that whenever only the moduli of the measurements are retained, both the orthogonal reduction and the implication from uniqueness to stability can fail, already in dimension two. We also give second moment measurements in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as a motivation for the quadratic model.

papers.title: On the convergence of greedy algorithms in one-dimensional Wasserstein space
papers.authors: Genevi\`eve Dusson, Carlo Marcati, Maximilian Penka
papers.abstract: We study the convergence of the greedy algorithm for approximating a compact set by barycenters in metric spaces, in particular in the space of one-dimensional measures endowed with the 2-Wasserstein distance. To this end, we compare several metric $N$-widths, which measure the best error achievable with $N$-point barycenters, using either classical barycenters having nonnegative weights or signed barycenters, with weights of arbitrary sign summing to one. For the analysis we exploit that quantile functions embed the one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space isometrically into a convex cone of $L^2(0,1)$, and barycenter sets correspond to nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls. We prove, both in the algebraic and exponential case, that the convergence rate of the greedy algorithm using signed barycenters matches the one of the metric $N$-width defined with classical barycenters. We provide counterexamples showing that this fails for the other combinations.

papers.title: Idempotent generically stable measures in NIP groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a global generically stable Keisler measure on a type-definable group in an NIP theory. Then $\mu$ is idempotent if and only if it is the unique translation-invariant measure on its type-definable stabilizer subgroup. This resolves the NIP case of the Idempotent Measure problem studied by Chernikov, Gannon, and Krupi\'nski.

papers.title: Szeg\H{o} kernels and logarithmic flatness of K\"ahler metrics
papers.authors: Peter Ebenfelt, Ming Xiao, Hang Xu
papers.abstract: Let $(L,h)$ be a positive Hermitian line bundle over a complex manifold $M$, inducing a K\"ahler metric $g$. We give a detailed account of the Hardy space and Szeg\H{o} kernel of the unit circle bundle of $(L^*,h^*)$ when $M$ is possibly noncompact. Assuming that $M$ admits a complete K\"ahler metric and that the Ricci curvature of $g$ is bounded below, we use the framework developed in our earlier work on Bergman logarithmic flatness to establish a diagonal expansion of the Szeg\H{o} kernel and characterize its logarithmic singularity in terms of the Tian--Yau--Zelditch--Catlin expansion of the Bergman kernels of $(L^k,h^k)$. This extends and answers a question of Lu--Tian. We introduce the notions of Szeg\H{o} and Bergman logarithmic flatness for K\"ahler metrics, not necessarily globally polarized, and prove that every compact locally homogeneous polarized metric is Szeg\H{o} logarithmically flat. For K\"ahler--Einstein metrics, we prove Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness implies Bergman logarithmic flatness. Examples arising from Bryant's metrics show that Bergman logarithmic flatness does not imply Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness.

papers.title: Threshold Representations and Realization Fibers of Specialization in Chang Fuzzy Topologies
papers.abstract: We investigate the information retained by fuzzy-point specialization in Chang fuzzy topologies and the fibers realizing a prescribed G\"odel specialization relation. Every reflexive, minimum-transitive fuzzy preorder has a greatest stratified Chang realization. Its realization fiber is a singleton precisely for the constant relation $1$; otherwise, below each member lies a continuum-sized descending chain with no lower bound in the fiber, also within the Alexandrov subclass. On finite support sets, every nontrivial stratified fiber has cardinality continuum without assuming Alexandrov completeness; this remains true for Alexandrov fibers on countable sets. We describe the entire two-point Alexandrov fiber order as the reverse of a product of classes of join-preserving threshold functions. For arbitrary Chang topologies, quasi-specialization determines membership specialization and its kernel completion, which in turn determine G\"odel specialization; the converse determinations fail in general. A central reconstruction result identifies the greatest quasi-specialization realization by \emph{exact agreement on every one- or two-point restriction}, equivalently by closure in a product of discrete grade intervals. In particular, quasi-specialization determines every Chang topology on a finite support set. We also represent general Alexandrov Chang topologies by matrices of join-preserving threshold maps and isolate the additional scalar compatibility law required for reconstruction from the graded relation. These results separate information encoded by finite-coordinate point comparisons from global restrictions on fuzzy open families.

papers.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large radial initial data without swirl, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. On the disk we require the initial acceleration to have zero trace at the wall. The initial density is bounded away from zero and, in the plane, approaches a positive constant at infinity. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. Throughout the strictly dissipative range of viscosity coefficients, every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, the result applies to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly in time. On the disk, the density converges exponentially to its spatial mean and the velocity to zero in the Sobolev norm of order three. In the plane, convergence in the same norm holds to the prescribed far-field state. The argument also applies to a class of non-power viscosity laws.

papers.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
papers.abstract: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

papers.title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
papers.abstract: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$. Following the method of the result in type $\mathbb{A}$, we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{B}_n}$ is a polynomial ring.

papers.title: Degree-stratified randomized projection for spectral clustering
papers.authors: Junghyun Eom, Youngjin Hwang, Euihyun Kim, Yongseok Jang
papers.abstract: Many real-world networks have heavy-tailed degree distributions, in which a few high-degree nodes coexist with many low-degree nodes. Randomized range finders reduce the cost of computing the eigenspace used in spectral clustering, but their random test matrices are constructed independently of the node degrees. We propose degree-stratified randomized projection (DS-RP), which partitions the nodes into dyadic degree strata, distributes a fixed sketch dimension across the strata, and draws an independent local sketch for each stratum. We bound the angle between the sampled range and the target eigenspace and show that the gain comes from the allocation of the sketch dimension rather than from the stratification itself. The bound improves when more sketch dimensions are assigned to the strata on which the target eigenspace is concentrated. For the degree-corrected stochastic block model, we prove that the leverage scores of this eigenspace are proportional to the node degrees, so that the allocation can be determined from the degrees alone. A Rayleigh--Ritz bound that requires no smallness assumption carries the estimate over to the computed spectral embedding. Numerical experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world networks show that DS-RP improves the clustering accuracy of standard Gaussian and CountSketch projections at the same sketch dimension and essentially the same computational cost.

papers.title: Independence number, clique number, and maximum degree
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $r \ge 3$, every $K_r$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G) > (5r-11)n/(5r-5)$ satisfies $\alpha(G) \ge n/(r-1)$. This resolves a conjecture posed by Brandt in 2001 and establishes the sharp minimum-degree threshold for guaranteeing an independent set of size at least $n/(r - 1)$ in $K_r$-free graphs.

papers.title: Nonreduced Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c Schubert schemes
papers.authors: Marc Besson, Jiuzu Hong, Huanhuan Yu
papers.abstract: We develop an effective numerical criterion ($\theta$-minimality) to detect the nonreducedness of Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c (FM) Schubert schemes via tangent-space comparisons at arbitrary torus-fixed points. We completely classify the dominant coweights admitting $\theta$-minimal pairs. As an application, we obtain nonreduced FM Schubert schemes in every type other than $A_n$ and $C_n$. In particular, every nontrivial FM Schubert scheme of type $E_8$ is nonreduced. In type $D_n$, we show that some nonreduced FM Schubert schemes and their corresponding spherical Schubert varieties have the same tangent space at the base point. Our methods use the Frenkel-Kac construction of basic representations and Segal-Sugawara operators.

papers.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
papers.authors: Yiqiao Zhang, Fang Yang, Tao Qian
papers.abstract: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(\Omega,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(\Omega), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(\xi) Z_Y(d\xi), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For \alpha>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^-)), where B_\alpha^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(\omega,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_\alpha = B_\alpha^2(C^+) \oplus B_\alpha^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. In L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha), we apply stochastic pre-orthogonal adaptive Fourier decomposition (SPOAFD) to U_+ and U_- separately, using normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman spaces as dictionaries. The adaptive selection is determined by the spectral density. Finally, using the Poisson kernel and SPOAFD expansions, we establish weak mean-square convergence of the original process against test functions in C_c^\infty(R).

papers.title: Isomorphic nonembeddings of Lorentz spaces under tensor products
papers.authors: Ying Xu, Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu
papers.abstract:
The Lorentz quasi-norm on $L_{p,q}(0,1)$ is
  \[
  \|f\|_{p,q}
  =\left(\int_0^1 [t^{1/p}f^*(t)]^q\,\frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/q},
  \]
where $f^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|f|$. Motivated by the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces (KuryakovSukochev2015,HuangSukochev2021), we ask whether $\ell_{p,q}\not\hookrightarrow L_{p,q}(0,1)$ persists under projective tensoring with a common factor. For $1<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and $p\ne q$, we obtain the following results.

Nonzero finite-dimensional factors preserve the nonembedding, as do nonzero $\ell_1$-FDD factors when $q>1$.
A single factor $U$ makes both tensor products isomorphic to $U$ throughout this range. For each pair with $q>1$, there are two
nonisomorphic separable absorbers with the metric approximation
property.
For $1<q<p<2$, a scalar $L_1(\Omega,\mu)$ factor over a standard
probability space yields an embedding exactly when the nonatomic part of $\mu$ has positive measure.

For $1\le p<\infty$ and $0<q<1$, we construct common absorbers under $r$-projective tensoring after equivalent renorming.

papers.title: A Higher-Order Algorithm for Solving Time-Fractional Differential Equations via Rational Approximation of z^{\alpha} as a Herglotz-Nevanlinna function
papers.authors: Miao-jung Yvonne Ou, Gamze Tano\v{g}lu, Jiangming Xie
papers.abstract: Time-Fractional derivatives (TFDs) have been widely used in mathematical modeling of physical phenomena such as anomalous diffusion and memory effects of materials. Traditionally, TFD is handled {either by a direct method which saves almost all the memory and hence computationally expensive or a sum of exponential method (SOE) which decomposes the time domain improper integral into a local term and a history term} {approximated by} a sum of exponential functions. The limitation of the SOE approach is that{ the approximation error of the local term might result in large errors if the unknown function is not smooth enough at $0$ and can lead to over-dissipation of energy.} In this paper, we take a different approach and will focus on the Caputo derivative because the Caputo time derivative of a constant function is 0. We present a simple time-stepping algorithm based on the theory of Stieltjes-Markov functions, a subclass of the Herglotz-Nevanlinna functions. The key is in identifying the Stieltjes-Markov function structure hidden in the Laplace transform of the kernel function. Compared to most of the current methods in literature, the novelty of the results in this paper is manifold. First, no decomposition of integral is needed and our resulting approximation in the time domain contains a Dirac measure with carefully calculated strength, leading to a drastic decrease in the number of exponential functions needed in the approximation. Secondly, the choice of our interpolation points is based on the Mellin's inversion theorem and hence the interpolation error in the transformed domain is explicitly and rigorously linked to the error in the time-domain. {Finally, the resulting system is almost diagonal and hence can be easily sped up by using the Schur complement method.}

papers.title: The distortion problem and orthogonality
papers.abstract: Schlumprecht [Israel J. Math. 76 (1991), 81--95] constructed an arbitrarily distortable Banach space. We further study distortion on this space under orthogonality constraints and obtain the following results. The exact distortion of his renormings is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when the unit vectors satisfy both mutual Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality for any finite family of equivalent norms. There are basic sequences of unit vectors satisfying both orthogonality conditions pairwise whose norms in the renormed space converge to the lower distortion endpoint. The proof combines finite-dimensional norm estimates with supporting functionals and the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. Further results concern finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality for auxiliary norms.

papers.title: When Speed Changes Where to Build: Optimal Placement of an Optional Fast Connection
papers.abstract: Express roads, limited-stop transit, and air taxis speed up only the trips that choose them, while others stay on the ground network. Where should such a connection's terminals go? Because its users change with the design, expected travel time is nonconvex and nonsmooth in the terminal locations. Previous models have therefore been solved numerically or in restricted settings. We solve a canonical case exactly: uniform trips in a square with grid streets and a straight link. We find that every optimal design is centered and diagonal or axis aligned, and the alignment switches once, near 2.18 times ground speed. The two designs tied there differ sharply in coverage and ridership. A planner also choosing speed, at a smooth cost of speed, never selects the switching speed. If the cost is proportional to speed, above a threshold unit cost the planner builds a slower diagonal link, below it a faster axis-aligned one, and the optimal speed skips a band around the switch. On a rectangle, every optimum is again centered, centered designs have a closed-form travel time, and only two families of links can be optimal, those along the long axis and those tilted toward the long side.

papers.title: Weak-strong uniqueness for the Landau equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the spatially inhomogeneous Landau equation with soft potentials, including the Coulomb case. Let $f$ and $g$ be nonnegative, uniformly continuous distributional solutions on $[0,T]$ with the same initial data. We prove that $f=g$ on $[0,T]$ if both solutions have sufficient polynomial decay in velocity and the diffusion matrix of $f$ satisfies the usual anisotropic lower bound. For weak solutions, this proves a stronger form of \cite[Conjecture~1.4]{HW}, with no prescribed modulus of continuity for the initial datum. The proof is by duality. We obtain a weighted $L^2$ estimate for the velocity Hessian of the solution to a backward adjoint equation. In the second-order nonlocal term, we write $g$ as the sum of its velocity mollification and a remainder. Uniform continuity makes the remainder small. For the mollified part, two integrations by parts give a bound proportional to the length of the time interval.

papers.title: Radio antipodal number for the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path
papers.abstract: A radio antipodal labeling of a graph $G$ is a function $f$ that assigns a non negative integer to each vertex in such a way that for any pair of distinct vertices $x$ and $y$, the condition $|f(x)-f(y)| \geq d-d(x,y)$ is satisfied, where $d$ and $d(x,y)$ represent the diameter of graph $G$, and distance between $x$ and $y$ in graph $G$, respectively. The span of radio antipodal labeling $f$ is defined as $span(f) = \max\{|f(x)-f(y)| : x,y \in V(G)\}$. The radio antipodal number of graph $G$, denoted by $an(G)$, is defined as $an(G) := \min_{f}\{span(f)\}$ with minimum taken over all radio antipodal labelings $f$ of $G$. A radio antipodal labeling $f$ of $G$ is optimal if $span(f) = an(G)$. In this paper, we give the exact radio antipodal number of the Cartesian product of a complete graph and a path.

papers.title: Conformally flat Mercator equation and conserved quantities of conformal circles
papers.abstract: We study properties of solutions of the conformal Mercator equation on the conformal sphere. We focus on conformal circles and give two different approaches of finding their conserved quantities from conformal Killing vector fields - variational and tractorial. We find a direct relation between the two sets of quantities.

papers.title: The parallel postulate characterizes the Euclidean plane
papers.abstract: We prove that every complete Riemannian plane satisfying the parallel axiom is isometric to the Euclidean plane. More generally, we characterize the Euclidean plane among complete Riemannian planes without conjugate points by an asymptotic condition on geodesic intersection probabilities. This also answers affirmatively a question of Croke asking whether a complete Riemannian plane must be Euclidean if almost every pair of geodesics intersects exactly once.

papers.title: Equivariant extension of $I_N$-finite tempered distributions on real flag varieties
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a real linear reductive group and let $P=L_PU_P$ and $Q=LN$ be parabolic subgroups. For a Casselman--Wallach representation $F$ of $L_P$, let $\mathcal{E}_F$ be the unnormalized homogeneous tempered bundle on $G/P$ induced from $F$. We prove that every $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on a $Q$-stable Nash open subset of $G/P$ extends to an $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on $G/P$.

papers.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
papers.abstract: We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $\Gamma_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.

papers.title: Simple Yetter-Drinfeld Modules and Extensions over Fractional Infinite-Dimensional Taft Algebras
papers.abstract: We classify all simple Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a fractional infinite-dimensional Taft Hopf algebra $T=T(\underline m,t,\xi)$, including the infinite-dimensional induced family and the finite-dimensional truncated and cyclic families. We determine their explicit structures and isomorphism criteria, and classify first extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules together with their middle modules. We also establish the primary decomposition with respect to $z^t$ and prove that every nonzero-eigenvalue component is wild when $m>1$.

papers.title: Tight Probabilistic Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs
papers.abstract:
Friends-and-strangers graphs, introduced by Defant and Kravitz, model arrangements of people on positions. We consider two graphs $X$ and $Y$ on $n$ vertices. The vertices of $X$ represent positions with edges denoting adjacencies while the vertices of $Y$ represent people with edges denoting friendships. Their \emph{friends-and-strangers graph} is denoted by $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$. Its vertices are all one-to-one placements of people on positions, and two placements are adjacent if one can swap two friends on adjacent positions to get from one placement to the other.
  A fundamental question is whether or not a friends-and-strangers graph is connected. A natural probabilistic analog is ``If $X$ and $Y$ are independently sampled Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graphs with $n$ vertices and edge probability $p,$ what is the threshold probability for $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$ to be connected with high probability?'' Alon, Defant, and Kravitz (2023) showed that $p = n^{-1/2+o(1)}$ is the threshold probability and conjectured that $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}).$ Milojevi\'{c} (2024) disproved this by showing $p = \Omega(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ is necessary for connectivity with high probability. In this work, we prove a matching upper bound, thus establishing that the threshold is $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}).$

papers.title: Parareal Approximation of Stochastic $L^2$-Boosting
papers.abstract: We study Parareal approximations of stochastic \(L^2\)-boosting, reusing the learner draws of the sequential algorithm in the fine propagators. We establish mean-square error bounds whose order improves with each correction, characterize the limiting distributions of normalized errors, including non-Gaussian components and the effects of coarse discretization, and derive sufficient conditions for preserving the statistical limit laws and validation-based stopping behavior of the sequential algorithm. Numerical experiments with sample-dependent coordinate and nonlinear residual-fitting learners examine the predicted convergence rates and limiting distributions, while computational benchmarks assess the efficiency of the method relative to sequential implementations.

papers.title: Combinatorial relative orientability for toric and tropical geometry
papers.abstract: Many problems in enumerative geometry are solved by computing the degree of the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle. Results from $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy theory allow to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields, replacing the top Chern class by the Euler class in Chow-Witt groups. For its degree to be well-defined, one needs the vector bundle to be relatively oriented. Another way to solve enumerative problems is to translate them to tropical geometry, where they become combinatorial problems. In this paper, we give a combinatorial description of relative orientability for vector bundles over smooth proper toric varieties. We show that it behaves well under tropicalization, establishing a tropical version of relative orientability, which will allow to the use of tropical geometry to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields. As a demonstration, we prove a quadratically enriched version of the Bernstein-Khovanskii-Kushnirenko theorem via tropical geometry. Lastly, we define the notion of $k$-phase structures on tropical hypersurfaces, generalizing the real case.

papers.title: The Power Of Enumerations
papers.abstract:
We study the computational strength of enumerations of generic and random sets, particularly its interplay with computing these `typical' sets. We show that, while enumerations of $2$-generics can compute $2$-generics, this fails at higher levels---every $3$-generic has an enumeration which computes no weak $3$-generic. The analogous statement holds for randoms---every weak $2$-random has an enumeration which computes no $1$-random.
  We then analyze the total degrees above a quasiminimal enumeration degree, showing certain restrictions as well as certain positive results on the possible Turing degrees in such a cone. This answers a question of Slaman and Sorbi, by showing that there are quasiminimals with no minimal Turing degrees above them. We also show that while every total degree above some quasiminimals compute dimension $1$ sets, the total degrees above any quasiminimal fail to be a subset of the PA degrees.

papers.title: Parameterized Subset Sum for Integers and Solvable Permutation Groups
papers.abstract: We show that parameterized subset sum for binary-encoded integers belongs to $\mathsf{W}[2]$, where the parameter is the number of selected integers. This improves a result of Buss and Islam, who proved membership in $\mathsf{W}[3]$. The proof uses an fpt-reduction to weighted CNF satisfiability without changing the parameter. For every fixed integer $d\geq1$, we also show that parameterized subset sum for permutation groups of derived length $d$ belongs to $\mathsf{W}[2d]$. The proof combines positive CNFs for addition in small abelian groups with an affine decomposition of a solvable permutation action. This gives circuits of weft at most $2d$ and depth depending only on $d$ for product evaluation. For every fixed nilpotency class, we obtain the stronger bound $\mathsf{W}[2]$ by an fpt-reduction to subset sum in abelian permutation groups. The reduction uses Hall's polynomial coordinates in a free nilpotent group and the Magnus embedding. For nilpotent permutation groups without a fixed class bound, we prove $\mathsf{W}[2]$-hardness, already for permutation $2$-groups.

papers.title: The Number of Real Eigenvalues of a Random Sign Matrix
papers.abstract: Let $R_n$ count the real eigenvalues of an $n\times n$ matrix with independent uniform $\pm1$ entries. We prove that $R_n/\sqrt n$ converges in $L^1$ to $\sqrt{2/\pi}$. In particular, $R_n=\Theta(\sqrt n)$ with probability tending to one, as conjectured by Vu.

papers.title: User-Irrepressible Sequences for Multiple-Packet Reception
papers.authors: Yen-Ling Shih, Yuan-Hsun Lo, Yijin Zhang, Ying Miao
papers.abstract: This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes based on protocol sequences for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception (MPR) channels without feedback or synchronization of sequence phases. Each user schedules its transmissions according to a preassigned periodic binary sequence. A sequence set has the user-irrepressible property with MPR capability $\gamma$ ($\gamma$-UI) if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of the relative cyclic shifts. We propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) for arbitrary MPR capability $\gamma\geq 2$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified CRT-based construction framework for $\gamma$-UI sequences over this full range, without requiring conflict-avoiding codes with prescribed parameters. We establish the $\gamma$-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations and show that suitably selected subsets support one additional active user without increasing the sequence length. We also derive exact average individual delay expressions over all possible cyclic shifts and extend the delay analysis to $\gamma$-UI sequence sets obtained from conflict-avoiding codes.

papers.title: A periodic Ambrosetti-Prodi problem with sign-changing nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We study the periodic solutions of the second-order equation \begin{equation*} u''+f(t,u)=s, \end{equation*} where $s\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter and $f$ is periodic in the time variable and satisfies the one-sided sublinear growth condition \begin{equation*} f(t,x)\geq a(t)|x|^p+b(t), \qquad 0<p<1, \end{equation*} for some $a,b\in L^1([0,T])$ with $\int_0^T a(t)\,\mathrm{d}t>0$. We establish an Ambrosetti--Prodi type theorem: there exists a threshold $s_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the equation has zero periodic solutions for $s<s_0$, at least one for $s=s_0$, and at least two for $s>s_0$. The main novelty of our result is the removal of the non-negativity assumption on the weight $a$, which is replaced by the weaker requirement of a positive mean value, thus allowing for sign-changing nonlinearities.

papers.title: No solvable group is isospectral to the symmetric group of degree 10
papers.authors: D. V. Lytkina, V. D. Mazurov
papers.abstract: We prove that no finite solvable group has the same spectrum as the symmetric group of degree 10. The proof analyzes the two possible Frobenius structures of a Hall $\{5,7\}$-subgroup and the actions of the corresponding subgroups on normal $\{2,3\}$-sections.

papers.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty
papers.abstract: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.

papers.title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.

papers.title: From data pencils to image representations of continuous-time LTI systems
papers.authors: Timo Reis, Philipp Schmitz, Karl Worthmann
papers.abstract: The continuous-time fundamental lemma describes the set of all trajectories of a linear time-invariant system by a Gramian matrix built from measured input--output data and their derivatives. The jet of a trajectory is represented as the Gramian applied to a nonunique parameter satisfying a differential-algebraic equation. We determine the complete Kronecker structure of the associated data pencil for multiple-input multiple-output systems. This enables the construction of a polynomial image representation of the input--output behavior directly from the data. The resulting image matrix has column degrees equal to the controllability indices, and its latent variable is free and serves as a flat output of the system. The computation relies on an orthogonal staircase reduction followed by basis reconstruction using polynomial kernels. We also propose a structure-preserving preconditioning of the Gramian to improve its condition number and facilitate rank decisions in the reduction. We illustrate our approach on a chain of mass-spring-damper systems.

papers.title: Data Informativity for Robust Feedback Rectification of Switched Linear Systems
papers.authors: Hannes Gernandt, Philipp Schmitz, Maria C. Honecker, Karl Worthmann
papers.abstract: Feedback rectification is a method for switched linear systems that constructs a mode-dependent state feedback such that the closed-loop subsystems share a common eigenvector basis. If the assigned eigenvalues lie inside the unit disk, this yields a common quadratic Lyapunov function and guarantees exponential stability under arbitrary switching. In this paper, we study robust feedback rectification from input-state data affected by bounded disturbances. Using the concept of data informativity, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for approximate feedback rectification without requiring full row-rank of the collected input-state data. If the rectification error is smaller than the stability margin of the prescribed eigenvalues, we obtain global exponential stability under arbitrary switching in the disturbance-free case, and practical global asymptotic stability under bounded disturbances. The approach is illustrated by a mass-spring-damper chain with varying stiffness, where prescribed poles are assigned in every mode from data that do not determine the system matrices uniquely.

papers.title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression
papers.abstract:
This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work.
  I thus reconstruct Badiou's own arguments in a corrected form, while transferring them to a categorical framework. The aim is not to introduce new mathematical results, but to identify what is conceptually lost through their reduction to set-theoretic formalism. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking.
  This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos as merely a formal container for mathematical objects, I propose reading it as a body of mathematical expression, aligning with Johnstone's characterization of a topos as a 'universe of discourse'. At the same time, the geometrization of logic allows Badiou's own four-fold typology of change - when applied to topos theory itself as a mathematical 'event' - to be anchored to various historical definitions of a topos.
  In this way, the article bridges Badiou's two major works while clarifying how his own limited expression of mathematical formalism embodies his 'dialectical', ultimately singular concept of the event, and the way it clouds his philosophical understanding of locality and temporality.

papers.title: The Four-Cycle Extremal Number of the Seven-Cube
papers.authors: Zheli Zhou, Haitong Ma, Ruofeng Yang, Tianzhi Ren, Kuan Yang, Shuai Li
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest number of edges in a four-cycle-free subgraph of the seven-dimensional hypercube is 304. In a hypothetical 305-edge subgraph, three-star counting and a local computational lemma force every degree to be four or five. A square-counting identity and an inequality for opposite facets then reduce the proof to five candidate facet profiles, excluded by two further local statements. The three computational statements concern only six-dimensional cubes and are certified by 21 propositional refutations.

papers.title: Half-integrality and an upper bound for slopes of Drinfeld cuspforms of level $\Gamma_1(t^r)$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a rational prime, let $q>1$ be a power of $p$ and let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the field of $q$ elements. Let $k\geq 2$ and $r\geq 1$ be integers. Let $S_k(\Gamma_1(t^r))$ be the $\mathbb{C}_\infty$-vector space of Drinfeld cuspforms of rank two, level $\Gamma_1(t^r)$ and weight $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$. In this paper, we prove that every finite $t$-adic slope of the Hecke operator $U_t$ on $S_k(\Gamma_1(t^r))$ belongs to $\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}$ and is at most $k-2$. If $q$ is odd, then every such slope is an integer.

papers.title: Two-phase visco-elastic FENE-P model: Thermodynamically consistent modeling, sharp interface limit analysis and unconditionally energy stable numerical scheme
papers.abstract: Although mathematical modeling and numerical simulations for two-phase Newtonian flows have been extensively studied for many years, relatively little work has focused on developing thermodynamically consistent models for two-phase Non-Newtonian viscoelastic flows, and to the author's best konowledge, no structure-preserving numerical methods have been reported for such models. In this paper, we focus on modeling the two-phase non-Newtonnian visco-elastic FENE-P model based on the energetic variational approach (EnVarA). In the model, a phase-field function is introduced to describe the diffuse interface which satisfies the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation. And all the physical variables can be connected smoothly. We conduct a matched asymptotic analysis for the sharp interface limit, which shows the diffuse interface model will converge to the sharp interface model when the interface thickness trends to zero. We then reformulate the model in an equivalent form that facilitates the construction of the numerical scheme. A weakly decoupled scheme is proposed for the resulting FENE-P-CH system, and its unconditional energy stability is proved theoretically. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted to validate the model and assess the performance of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: Chern classes, Poincar\'e polynomials, and Bernstein-Sato polynomials of plane curves
papers.abstract: We show that the Poincar\'e polynomial of a reduced plane curve $C$ is the Chern polynomial of the dual of the bundle of Jacobian syzygies of $C$. Using the Zeuthen-Segre formula, we prove that its value at $t=-1$ equals the Euler number of the complement of $C$ up to the correction term $\mu(C)-\tau(C)$, so the two numbers coincide if and only if all singularities of $C$ are quasi-homogeneous. As applications, we show that the defect in a combinatorial inequality for free $d$-arrangements is the square of the difference of the exponents, extend the addition technique to arbitrary reduced plane curves, and locate the roots of local Bernstein-Sato polynomials at ordinary singular points.

papers.title: Stochastic Differential Equations on the Simplex
papers.abstract: We propose a framework for simplex-valued diffusion processes, formulated as solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by antisymmetric Brownian motion. Our edge-wise representation includes the multivariate Jacobi processes and the general class of continuous simplex-valued polynomial diffusions. Also, it allows bounded, locally Lipschitz state-dependent drift rates and edge weights. We establish weak solutions, as well as global strong existence and pathwise uniqueness for strictly positive initial states under a sufficient boundary non-attainment condition.

papers.title: The geometric expansion of the coarse trace formula of GL(4)
papers.authors: Haoyang Wang, Xinghua Cui, Weilong Zhang, Zhifeng Peng
papers.abstract: We study the non-semisimple terms in the geometric side of Arthur's trace formula of $\rm{GL}(4)$ for the further study of the invariant trace formula. After modifying the zeta function and Arthur's definition of the weighted orbital integrals, we compare the two ways to calculate the distributions $J^T(f)$ of the geometric side, we can obtain that the distributions can be written as the linear combanition of the weighted orbital integrals. In particular, we get the coefficients $a^M(S,\gamma)$, for all $\gamma\in \rm{GL}(4,F)$, expressed by the measure and zeta functions.

papers.title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
papers.abstract: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

papers.title: Conservative Implicit and Explicit Solvers for Reactive Conformable Transport with Multirate Memory
papers.abstract: In this article, we analyze conservative implicit and explicit schemes for reactive transport with a conformable time scale and multirate exchange. The conformable derivative defines a local change of time coordinate, while exchange with immobile regions supplies the memory. Positive Gauss--Jacobi quadrature approximates the prescribed exchange spectrum by finite compartments. Both schemes use conservative finite-volume fluxes. Forward Euler gives the explicit update; backward Euler initializes the implicit second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2). Eliminating the compartment states reduces each implicit step to a tridiagonal system. Under stated mesh and regularity conditions, we prove implicit solvability, conditional explicit positivity and stability, and discrete mass balance. A cell-average error estimate separates spatial, compartment and temporal contributions. Its proof accounts for the boundary fluxes and the BDF2 startup error. Source-specific bounds make the temporal and memory prefactors uniform under mesh and compartment refinement. For a broader positive-history model, continuous residual estimates have coefficients independent of memory strength and kernel mass. Local coercivity gives a sharper coefficient. Manufactured tests recover second-order spatial convergence, first-order Euler convergence and second-order BDF2 convergence. Separate experiments examine the memory and combined estimates. In a prescribed porous-medium application, the finest numerical states differ by $3.57\times10^{-5}$ in relative space--time $L^2$. Independent resolution checks support the computed pulse attenuation, immobile storage and release after injection ends.

papers.title: A fast automatically adaptive integral equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems
papers.authors: Tianze Zhang, Yixuan Ma, Jun Wang
papers.abstract: We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.

papers.title: The non symmetric Hikita conjecture
papers.abstract:
We construct local and global comparison maps for the Hikita conjecture in quiver gauge theories and study their analogues for finite non symmetric Cartan pairs. The construction uses quiver Hecke description of Coulomb branch and microlocal geometry. It yields comparison maps from B-algebras to the cohomology of some Lagrangians of quiver varieties.
  For arbitrary symmetric types, the local and global comparison maps are surjective and are isomorphisms under a B-algebra dimension bound. In finite non symmetric types, the local image is the image of the Kirwan map, i.e., the tautological subalgebra. It can be proper. Under some assumptions we also construct a non symmetric global comparison map.
  Crystal theoretic methods identify the set of nonempty Lagrangians with the set of isomorphism classes of simple modules of the category $\mathscr O$ of the Coulomb branch, and proves that the Lagrangians are nonempty for $\ell$-dominant $\ell$-highest weights.
  The proof uses microlocal modules of Coulomb branches that we define. We prove they form integral bases of the Grothendieck group of the category $\mathscr O$, with Jordan-H\"older multiplicities given by characteristic cycles.
  In symmetric type we prove an isomorphism between based quasimap modules at homogeneous polarized points of quiver varieties and co-specialized microlocal modules. The proof uses hyperbolic restriction and Braden's theorem. We conjecture an extension to all homogeneous points and a relative version.

papers.title: Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured: a study via Schatten estimates for the additive Richardson iteration
papers.authors: Samuele Ferri, Valerio Loi, Stefano Serra-Capizzano, Giacomo Tento
papers.abstract: In the present work, we first study the additive Richardson iteration for the Karcher mean of complex Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrix sequences, by obtaining normalized Schatten estimates independent of the matrix dimension. These estimates are used to prove that Karcher means of structured matrices are asymptotically structured and this is proven for input HPD Toeplitz and generalized locally Toeplitz (GLT) matrix sequences. More precisely, we provide the a.c.s. approximation, which is the key for demonstrating the GLT closure under Schatten spectral bounds, and the GLT conclusion can be extended to matrix sequences with symbols that are positive definite almost everywhere. Ad hoc numerical experiments illustrate the spectral distribution consequences of these results and few related computational advantages. Concluding remarks and open problems are provided in the final section.

papers.title: A general reduction and explicit remoteness formulas for exact slow 2-Nim
papers.abstract: In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$. If $N$ is even, its remoteness equals $D$ when $2D\le N$ and is either $N/2$ or $N/2-1$ otherwise. Both values can occur for the same $N$, $D$, and number of piles. We determine $D$ explicitly for five piles. This gives a six-pile remoteness formula and a rule for selecting an optimal move. Both take $O(b)$ bit operations when each pile size has at most $b$ bits. We also give a closed formula for positions with any number of unit piles and two further piles of arbitrary size. For the GM move rule, we prove the proposed descriptions of the exceptions in the four- and five-pile games and give the exact threshold at which a specified six-pile move ceases to be optimal as the largest pile grows. Finally, we classify all outcome-preserving sorted translations for five and six piles.

papers.title: A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics
papers.abstract: We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

papers.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
papers.authors: Kaijian Yang, Feng Wang, Guojun Han, Xin Wang, Vincent K. N. Lau
papers.abstract: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

papers.title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
papers.authors: Yongcun Song, Shangzhi Zeng, Jin Zhang, Lvgang Zhang
papers.abstract: Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution.
