Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.

papers.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
papers.authors: Celia Taboada, Luis Nu\~nez, Ang\'elica Casero, Pedro Navas
papers.abstract:
Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance.
  Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution.
  Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.

papers.title: Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
papers.authors: Benedikt Jahnel, Lukas L\"uchtrath, Christian M\"onch
papers.abstract: We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $\lambda\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $\lambda_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $\lambda_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate.

papers.title: Linear Convergence of Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Methods: A Unified Framework
papers.abstract: We establish a unified Lyapunov framework for adaptive accelerated gradient methods on smooth, strongly convex objectives. Conditions on local curvature, stepsize ratios, and coefficient variation ensure eventual linear convergence without assuming stepsize convergence. We verify these conditions for specified AdaNAG-G, smooth unconstrained AC-FGM, and AdaAGM policies and use them to design VC-FG and CC-FG. The verified adaptive main iterations require neither global smoothness nor strong-convexity parameters and avoid restart and backtracking. The framework also sharpens a fixed-step FISTA/NAG-type bound. Experiments on four smooth, strongly convex problem families illustrate complementary performance of the new methods.

papers.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $\lambda_1A^3/I>9\pi^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $\lambda_1A^3/I>12\pi^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.

papers.title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
papers.abstract: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_\lambda(x)=x^{3q-1}+\lambda x^{2q}+\lambda x^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_\lambda$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $\lambda=0$, or $\lambda\ne0$ and $X^3+X+\lambda^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $\lambda$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_\lambda$ parameterized by $P_\lambda(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $\lambda$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

papers.title: A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four
papers.abstract: We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class. The normal forms prove that the twelve primitive extreme-ray generators form the entire Hilbert basis: eight have magic sum two and four have magic sum four. We exhibit the underlying regular unimodular triangulation and a single perturbation direction producing all half-open boundary conventions. The resulting positive multivariate generating function specializes to an explicit rational function and a quasipolynomial of period four in the magic sum. A further consequence is a reflexive lattice polytope associated with positive symmetric magic squares.

papers.title: A Structured Levenberg--Marquardt Method for Binary Tensor Completion
papers.authors: Yannan Chen, Xihong Yan, Bobin Zheng
papers.abstract: We develop a structured Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) method with trust-region globalization for binary tensor completion, using triple decomposition and a logistic loss. Under a local component-residual error bound and positive outer curvature, we prove quadratic convergence of the exact iteration for damping exponents $1\le\delta\le2$, without requiring full row rank. A constant-rank criterion and an explicit rank-one certificate provide sufficient conditions for the residual error bound. The analysis decomposes the local error into outer-loss linearization, factor linearization, and regularization contributions. For a symmetric nonquadratic logistic--LSE family with $\delta=2$, cancellation improves the objective-model error to fourth order and the decrease-ratio error to second order. A synthetic experiment illustrates the local quadratic convergence rate. On the HCP and Enron datasets, the proposed method improves binary tensor completion accuracy while requiring fewer outer iterations than the first-order methods.

papers.title: Very weak solutions of nonlinear elliptic systems with Orlicz growth
papers.abstract:
In this work we consider non-linear elliptic equations with respect to Orlicz growth, for instance equations of the form
  $$
  \mathrm{div}(\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) 
abla u)= 0.
  $$ We study very weak solutions to this system, that is, solutions that are not a priori in the correct energy space to this equation ($\varphi(\vert 
abla u \vert) \vert 
abla u \vert^2 \in L^1$). On the one hand, using rather mild assumptions on the corresponding Orlicz space (we need either the $\Delta_2$ or $
abla_2$ condition, but not both at the same time), we can show that the integrability of very weak solutions improves to the energy space, provided that the initial integrability is close enough to the energy space. On the other hand, mirroring the construction of Colombo and Tione (Non-classical solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation, J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2024), for the $p$-Laplacian, we give a construction of 'wild' solutions for a $L \log L$-type Laplacian.

papers.title: Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc
papers.abstract: We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_\sigma$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Model Reduction of Metriplectic Systems via Oblique Projections and Block Structure
papers.abstract: Metriplectic systems combine conservative and dissipative dynamics and are characterized by energy conservation and entropy production. The degeneracy conditions underlying these properties are generally not preserved by standard projection-based model order reduction. We develop two structure-preserving reduction strategies. The first enforces degeneracy conditions through oblique projections and combines gradient-preserving and matrix empirical interpolation for hyper-reduction. The second constructs reduced bases adapted to available operator block structure, preserving degeneracy without online oblique corrections. We establish sufficient conditions for preserving the Jacobi identity and derive a priori error estimates. Numerical tests on benchmark problems demonstrate accuracy, thermodynamic consistency, and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Boundary concentration and Pohozaev identity for the fractional p-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We prove a Pohozaev-like identity for bounded weak solutions of the fractional p-Laplace equation with a locally Lipschitz nonlinearity on bounded C^2 domains, provided that s>max{1/2-1/p,0}. We compare the weak equations for the solution and its spatial deformation to show that the first-order contribution of the energy remainder is concentrated at the boundary. The boundary term involves the weighted trace, with a coefficient expressed by an integral of the one-dimensional boundary profile.

papers.title: Real stable multivariate Delannoy polynomials and their Rayleigh differences
papers.abstract: The univariate Delannoy polynomials are known to have only real zeros. We construct a real stable multivariate refinement of these polynomials using weighted lattice paths and give both algebraic and combinatorial proofs of stability. More strongly, we show that every Rayleigh difference of the multivariate Delannoy polynomials is a perfect square and give an explicit factorization.

papers.title: Improved perimeter bounds for Hausdorff approximation by convex polygons
papers.abstract: We investigate how closely a convex polygon with at most n vertices can approximate a plane convex body of given perimeter. For free approximation in the Euclidean Hausdorff metric we improve Popov's bound for every $n \geq 3$. We also improve his inscribed bound for every $n \geq 3$ and his circumscribed bound for $n = 3$. The common step is to join successive boundary contacts of the body and estimate the perimeter lost in passing to their convex hull.

papers.title: Claw-free difference graphs of finite groups
papers.abstract: Let $\D(G)$ be the difference graph of a finite group $G$: the graph on the non-isolated vertices of $\PE(G)-\Pg(G)$, where $x\sim_{\D} y$ if and only if $\gen{x,y}$ is cyclic and neither of $x,y$ lies in the cyclic group generated by the other. A claw is the graph $K_{1,3}$ and a graph is claw-free if it has no induced claw. We prove that for every finite group $G$, $\D(G)$ is claw-free if and only if it is a disjoint union of copies of the path $P_3$, if and only if the element orders of $G$ are prime powers or $6$, every element of order $3$ has at most one involution in its centralizer, and every involution has at most one subgroup of order $3$ in its centralizer (equivalently: $C_G(a)$ has a normal Sylow $2$-subgroup of order at most $2$ for every $a$ of order $3$, and $C_G(u)$ a normal Sylow $3$-subgroup of order at most $3$ for every involution $u$). Consequences: a nilpotent group that is not a $p$-group has claw-free $\D$ if and only if $G\cong C_6$; $\D(\Sym_n)$ is claw-free if and only if $n\le 5$; $\D(\Alt_n)$ is claw-free if and only if $n\le 6$; a non-abelian simple group has claw-free $\D$ if and only if it is EPPO or $\PSL_2(11)$ or $\PSL_2(13)$, proved family by family (this uses the classification of finite simple groups). For soluble groups we obtain a complete classification: the non-EPPO soluble groups with claw-free $\D$ are $C_6$, $D_{12}$, $C_3\rtimes C_4$ and the Frobenius groups $N\rtimes K$ with $N$ an abelian $r$-group, $r\ge 5$, and $K\cong C_6$ or $C_3\rtimes C_4$. For every group with claw-free non-empty $\D$ we show $|O_2(G)|\le 2$ and $|O_3(G)|\le 3$, and we give non-soluble examples ($\Sym_5$, $\PGL_2(7)$, $\PSL_2(11)$, $\PSL_2(13)$). We also prove that the full enhanced power graph is claw-free only for cyclic groups and clarify the relations between claw-freeness of $\D(G)$, $\Pg(G)$ and $\PE(G)$.

papers.title: Reset Quantum Channels
papers.abstract: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.

papers.title: Non-local ergodic measures in symplectic dynamics
papers.abstract:
We consider the direct product of two symplectomorphisms, one of which exhibits a basic set and the other one acts on a compact surface and has a non-degenerate elliptic equilibrium. Under a local domination condition we show that a typical real-analytic perturbation of this system displays a large normally hyperbolic lamination on which the natural invariant measure is ergodic.
  The proof, which introduces a novel geometric source of semi-local ergodicity, combines tools ranging from KAM theory to geometric measure theory and is robust enough to be of interest in more general configurations.

papers.title: Lower bounds for mixed moments of modular and Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a fixed holomorphic Hecke cusp form of level one. For every fixed positive integer $k$, we prove a lower bound of order $q(\log q)^{2k^2}$ for the $2k$-th moment of $L(1/2,f\otimes\chi)L(1/2,\chi)$ over primitive characters modulo a sufficiently large prime $q$.

papers.title: Consensus of Consensus: Decentralized Consensus-Based Optimization
papers.authors: Stefania Bellavia, Massimo Fornasier, Greta Malaspina, Tim Roith
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a decentralized variant of Consensus-Based Optimization (CBO) for the global minimization of continuous, possibly non-convex functions accessible only through a stochastic, possibly biased, zeroth-order oracle with bounded mean-squared error. The agents are split among $N$ units of an undirected communication network. Each unit evolves its swarm of $M$ agents towards a local tracking variable, which follows the network average of the local consensus points through one round of neighbour-to-neighbour communication via a doubly stochastic mixing matrix, without any central coordinator. We show that, under an explicit condition linking the drift and diffusion parameters to $M$, all agents reach consensus almost surely, at an exponential mean-square rate governed by the spectrum of the mixing matrix. Using a finite-agent quantitative Laplace principle, we prove that, for large $\alpha$ and provided some agent visits a neighbourhood of the global minimizer with sufficient probability, the expected mean-squared distance of the swarm from the minimizer falls below any tolerance within an explicit number of iterations, at a rate that deteriorates for poorly connected networks. We verify this hitting assumption for a simplified dynamics. Experiments on benchmarks up to dimension $d=1000$, with stochastic objectives, and on a federated learning task demonstrate the method's effectiveness.

papers.title: The Garnett--Jones distance theorem for rectangles
papers.abstract: For the family of all axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d>1$, we characterize the distance of a real- or complex-valued function of rectangular bounded mean oscillation (little bmo) to $L^\infty$ by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent. For each $\alpha>0$ at which the rectangular exponential moment of $f$ is finite, we construct a bounded correction so that the residual has mean absolute oscillation bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times $1/\alpha$ on every rectangle. The proof bounds products of coordinate maximal operators between two sets in terms of the supremum of their density product over common test rectangles. Selecting a longest interval along each path lets us remove repeated visits to a coordinate, so the density exponent is independent of the number of factors. The maximal-operator estimate holds with every positive density exponent below $1/6$ in two dimensions and below $1/24$ in three dimensions.

papers.title: Gradient Stability of the Morrey and Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract: We find that the quantitative gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality in a ball $B_R$ fails with respect to any exponent of the {\it gradient-level} distance $D_M(u):=\inf\{\|\nabla u-\nabla v\|_{L^p(B_R)}:v\in \mathcal{M}\}$. Instead, the estimate holds with $D_M(u^\star),$ the gradient-level distance between the Schwarz symmetrization $u^\star$ and the space of Morrey extremals $\mathcal{M}$. Nevertheless, we establish a gradient stability estimate for the Morrey inequality by slightly `weakening' the above distance. We also obtain analogous gradient stability for the geometric $L^p$-Hardy inequality in certain domains. Distinct behaviors in the stability of these two inequalities have been discussed. Furthermore, in the $L^2$-case, we investigate the optimal constants and their attainability in both the Morrey and Hardy gradient stability inequalities.

papers.title: A 2D Free Boundary Model for Atherosclerosis with Diffusion and Elasticity
papers.authors: Ghada Abi Younes, Nader El Khatib, Nicolai Bessonov, Vitaly Volpert
papers.abstract: We propose a coupled elasticity--diffusion model on a deformable domain to describe the interaction between diffusion and mechanical deformation. We first study the two-dimensional formulation and investigate its numerical behavior. A quasi-stationary formulation is then derived, and a linear relation between the total mass of the diffusing species and the volume change of the domain is established. Next, a one-dimensional reduction is introduced as a particular case of the two-dimensional model to provide additional analytical insight into the coupled dynamics. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to a model of atherosclerosis, where numerical simulations illustrate the influence of the model parameters on inflammatory wave propagation and arterial wall deformation.

papers.title: The Tamura-Shafer Problem for Monoids
papers.abstract: Let \(\Pow(S)\) denote the semigroup of all nonempty subsets of a semigroup \(S\), with multiplication induced from \(S\). We prove that every monoid \(M\) is reconstructible from \(\Pow(M)\), even among arbitrary semigroups: if \(\Pow(M)\cong\Pow(T)\), then \(T\) is a monoid and \(M\cong T\). The resulting isomorphism is uniquely determined by the singleton subsets of units and the two-point subsets \(\{1,a\}\) of nonunits. The main difficulty is to recover multiplication without assuming that an isomorphism of power semigroups preserves singletons. We resolve it by reconstructing finite multiplication cycles and the translation geometry of infinite mixed-power orbits. We also describe the induced split epimorphism between automorphism groups and exhibit examples where nonregular singletons are not preserved.

papers.title: Diameter Growth of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ under Cliff Metrics
papers.abstract: Cliff metrics are right invariant Riemannian metrics on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ introduced by Nielsen and his collaborators in the geometric approach for gate complexity in quantum computations. In this paper, we compute the exponential growth rate for the diameter of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ equipped with cliff metrics as $N \rightarrow \infty$. We prove that if the norm of most generalized Pauli matrices are sufficiently large, this growth rate coincides with the growth rate of maximal gate complexity obtained by Knill.

papers.title: On the AF embedding problem
papers.abstract: This article gives a survey of the AF-embedding problem for $C^*$-algebras. The problem asks when a given $C^*$-algebra $A$ embeds into an \emph{approximately finite dimensional} (AF) $C^*$-algebra (a direct limit of finite dimensional $C^*$-algebras). This is largely based on my paper ``Subalgebras of simple AF algebras,'' which shows that separable, exact $C^*$-algebras satisfying the UCT and admitting a faithful, quasidiagonal trace embed into a unital, simple AF algebra. Some other results are also discussed.

papers.title: There are hard braids
papers.abstract:
Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question.
  Hard braids exist. For every number of strands starting from 4, for every even length starting from 16, we present examples of hard trivial braids of that size.
  Our smallest example is minimal. We prove that there are no hard braids on three strands. On four strands our shortest example, of length 16, is a shortest hard braid.
  The hard braids in that family can be untangled without increasing their length if we use Reidemeister moves and an infinite family of moves $\sigma_i^{\varepsilon}\sigma_j^{m}\sigma_i^{-\varepsilon} \leftrightarrow\sigma_j^{-\varepsilon}\sigma_i^{m}\sigma_j^{\varepsilon}$, which involve only three strands.
  We also build a harder family of hard braids which no moves confined to a bounded number of strands can untangle. For every $m$ we construct a trivial braid on $4m$ strands, of length $16m^2$, which can be untangled without increasing its length by moves on $2m+1$ strands but not not on $2m$ strands.

papers.title: An affine surface with 3-step nilpotent fundamental group
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth complex affine surface $Y$ such that $\pi_1(Y)$ is virtually $3$-step nilpotent, but not virtually $2$-step nilpotent. This gives a negative answer to the quasi-projective version of Campana's nilpotency problem.

papers.title: Scattering by two parallel semi--infinite arrays of sound--soft scatterers
papers.abstract: This article considers the scattering of an acoustic wave by two identical semi--infinite arrays of point scatterers which are positioned parallel to one another. The resulting system of scattering coefficients is formulated as a pair of coupled discrete Wiener--Hopf equations with a full $2\times2$ matrix kernel composed of two scalar kernel functions that represent interaction within the selected array and between the two arrays. Exploiting the symmetry of the two arrays, we introduce symmetric and antisymmetric components of the scattering coefficients, which decouple the matrix Wiener--Hopf system into two independent scalar problems with kernels given by the sum and difference of the two original kernel functions. The scalar Wiener--Hopf equations are then solved using the Wiener--Hopf technique in a very similar way to what has previously been used to solve the semi--infinite array problem. The original definitions of the two scalar kernels are represented by a lattice sum and practical evaluation techniques are discussed. Comparisons with previous work are also critically discussed. The resulting formulation provides an exact analytical solution to a coupled semi--infinite array problem and illustrates how symmetry can reduce a discrete matrix Wiener--Hopf problem to two scalar problems.

papers.title: Boundary gradient asymptotics for superquadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations via optimal control
papers.abstract:
We study the boundary behavior of the maximal solution of \[
  -\Delta u + |\nabla u|^{p} + \lambda u = f \] on arbitrary bounded $C^{2}$ domains, where $p > 2$ and $\lambda > 0$. For bounded state-dependent terms $f$, we resolve a conjecture of Lasry and Lions by establishing sharp boundary gradient asymptotics without geometric restrictions on the domain. Previously, such asymptotics were established only for certain classes of domains with additional restrictions on $p$ and $f$. We also extend the analysis to state-dependent terms that may be singular near the boundary and obtain sharp boundary profiles and gradient asymptotics.
  Our approach relies on stochastic optimal control and boundary blow-up analysis. Dynamic programming estimates and comparisons of near-optimal trajectories establish tangential invariance of boundary blow-up limits, leading to the identification of one-dimensional profiles and the asymptotic formulas. For the associated state-constrained control problem, we establish sharp asymptotics for the minimizing feedback and deduce its admissibility and optimality, with corresponding results for the ergodic problem.

papers.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
papers.abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_\sigma$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(\Omega, \mathcal F_0; L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.

papers.title: Constraint-Aware Anticlustering Decomposition for Certifying Pairwise-Constrained Clustering
papers.authors: Anna Livia Croella, Veronica Piccialli, Antonio M. Sudoso
papers.abstract: Certifying the quality of feasible solutions to large-scale minimum sum-of-squares clustering with pairwise must-link and cannot-link constraints remains challenging, as it requires strong lower bounds on the optimal objective value. We propose a decomposition framework that partitions the data points into smaller subsets, called anticlusters, and solves the induced clustering subproblems to obtain a certified optimality gap for the original problem. To preserve pairwise information, we introduce the Constrained Anticlustering Problem (CAP), which assigns each connected component of the constraint graph to a single anticluster while seeking geometrically representative subsets. We formulate CAP as a mixed-integer second-order cone program and develop a variable neighborhood search heuristic to construct high-quality decompositions. The resulting lower bound remains valid even when the induced subproblems are not solved to global optimality. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets with up to approximately 4,000 observations show that our approach can achieve mean optimality gaps below 1% at a modest computational cost.

papers.title: Solutions with one dimensional concentration for a two dimensional Schr\"odinger model with general potential and involving mass subcritical and supercritical exponents
papers.authors: Lipeng Duan, Suting Wei, Jun Yang
papers.abstract:
We prove the existence of solution $(\tilde u, \lambda)$ which concentrates on stationary and non-degenerate curve, as $p_\epsilon \to 6$, to the following mass-constraint nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \begin{align*} \begin{cases}
  - \Delta \tilde u + W({\bf y}) \tilde u - |\tilde u|^{p_\epsilon-2} \tilde u = \lambda \tilde u, \quad {\bf y} \in \mathbb{R}^2, \\[2mm]
  \int_{\R^2} |\tilde u|^2 {\mathrm d} {\bf y} =a. \end{cases} \end{align*} Here $\lambda$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $ W({\bf y})$ is a real-valued potential, $a \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is a constant, $p_\epsilon = 6 \pm \epsilon, \epsilon \ll 1$ and $6$ is the $L^2$-critical exponent in the sense of concentration on a codimension 1 submanifold. When constructing the solution concentrating on a curve, we utilize some delicate transformations to overcome the challenges posed by the non-uniform boundedness of length of concentrating curves.
  In addition, we employ some refined analytical techniques to overcome the strong resonance phenomena caused by the $L^2$ constraint. Our result partially answers the Ambrosetti-Malchiodi-Ni conjecture in the setting of the mass-constrained nonlinear elliptic equation.

papers.title: Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain
papers.abstract: We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.

papers.title: Operative Representation of Quasi-Arithmetic Means, Complex Branch Structure, and Covariant Commutator Defects in Iterated Logarithmic Operation Hierarchies
papers.abstract: We investigate the bidirectional family of commutative binary operations $\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[x,y] = f_a^{(-m)}(f_a^{(m)}(x) + f_a^{(m)}(y))$ ($m \in \mathbb{Z}$) generated by iterating the scaled logarithmic Cauchy isomorphism $f_a(z) = \frac{1}{a}\ln(z)$ ($a > 0$). Our analysis focuses on three structural properties of this hierarchy. First, we show that for all $m \ge -1$ the associated quasi-arithmetic Kolmogorov-Nagumo means $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x})$ admit a closed two-stage operative representation $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathrm{Op}_{m+1}^{(a)}[\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[\mathbf{x}], N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n)]$ with normalization factor $N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n) = f_a^{(-m)}(1/n)$, and prove that this internal operative normalizability via a distributive adjacent level characterizes logarithmic generators among continuously conjugated group operations. Second, we show that for $m \le -2$ and $n \ge 2$ the normalization factor leaves the positive real domain $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, motivating the analytic continuation onto the Riemann surface of the logarithm; there, a fundamental dichotomy emerges between the internal branch-index invariance of $\mathrm{Op}_{-1}^{(a)}$ and the associativity defect $\omega(x,z)$ generated by $\mathrm{Op}_2^{(a)}$. Third, for arbitrary levels $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sample sizes $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we derive the general covariance pushforward theorem $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = f_a^{(-m)}(\mathrm{Cov}(f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{x}), f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{y})))$ governing the commutator defect between mean formation and the adjacent operation.

papers.title: Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)
papers.abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).

papers.title: Approximating technique for the solution to the ${H}^{\infty}$ -optimal control problem
papers.abstract: This paper continues the results published in [G. Marinoschi, Appl. Math. Optimiz. 94:44, 1-29, 2026], by presenting an approximating method of calculating the solution to the $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem, which solves the robust stabilization of a system by a feedback controller, and to the associated Riccati equation. This method generates a sequence of infinite dimensional systems approximating the original system and the solution to the approximating $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem is proved to converge to the solution of the original $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem. An example for calculating the solution to the Riccati equation and the feedback controller is provided at the end.

papers.title: Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
papers.authors: Gao Chen, Junbang Liu, Sijie Nie
papers.abstract: We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact K\"ahler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.

papers.title: Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps
papers.abstract: Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero. The proof gives a uniform positive lower bound for symbol discrepancies at all sufficiently large times. For self-similar Bruin maps with primitive period substitution, the same condition also implies weak mixing. We apply the nonrigidity condition to an explicit self-similar infinite-type Bruin map on eight intervals, specifying its algebraic parameters and verifying its return words.

papers.title: Squarefree powers of simplicial forests
papers.authors: Marie Amalore Nambi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Dharm Veer
papers.abstract: The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related. We also investigate the corresponding question for undirected path ideals of forests. Here the highest nonzero squarefree power always has linear quotients for $3$-path ideals, whereas the analogous assertion fails for $4$-path ideals of trees.

papers.title: Real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices preserving an ergodic volume
papers.abstract: We classify real-analytic actions of higher-rank lattices that preserve an ergodic smooth volume on a compact manifold. On an invariant open dense set of full volume, the action is analytically conjugate to the restriction of an affine action on finitely many copies of one double quotient. The conjugacy carries Haar probability to the given volume. Analytic germ superrigidity supplies local coordinates with measurable dependence on the center. The conditional measures on coarse Lyapunov manifolds determine the law of a displaced center. A two-point joining pairs charts whose evaluations agree there and gives the change of coordinates. The resulting analytic frame bundle carries a coframe whose vector fields integrate to the homogeneous model. This gives the open homogeneous classification in Zimmer's program.

papers.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
papers.abstract: We study the isotropic $ L_{p} $-Minkowski problem. The equation is affine invariant at the exponent $ p = -n-1 $, where all origin-centered ellipsoids with the volume of the unit ball are solutions, and it is known that the unit sphere is the only solution for $ p \in (-n-1, 1) $. We prove uniform $ C^{0} $ estimates for all solutions in the supercritical range $ p < -n-1 $. This allows us to prove a key spectral estimate of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator on solutions. We then utilize the Rayleigh quotient method with position vectors as test functions for the operator adapted from Ivaki-Milman to prove uniqueness in the range $ p \in (-n-1- \delta_{n}, -n-1) $ for some $ \delta_{n} > 0 $.

papers.title: Counting cliques in optimal $1$-planar graphs
papers.abstract: Extremal problems concerning the maximum number of cliques in $n$-vertex graphs from a given graph class have been widely investigated. In this contribution, we present several results on counting cliques that extend beyond the existing framework. Firstly, we address this problem for the class of optimal 1-planar graphs where we determine the maximum numbers of copies of $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ in an $n$-vertex optimal 1-planar graphs and characterize all extremal graphs. This resolves Question {\b 8.1} of Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Secondly, we prove that every 3-connected plane quadrangulation on $n\geq14$ vertices has at most $2n-14$ 3-separators and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs. This confirms Conjecture {\b 8.2} posed by Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Lastly, we construct, for every integer $r\geq1$, a simple 2-planar graph with $5r+3$ vertices and $44r+1$ triangles, thus disproving Conjecture {\b 8.3} of theirs. Our proofs use radial graphs, tree decomposition and SPQR trees.

papers.title: Incentive-Based Regulatory Mechanism for Tariff Design in District Heating and Cooling Networks
papers.authors: Hossein Hesamzadeh, Wicak Ananduta, Eric Dumont, Zacharie De Greve
papers.abstract: Low-temperature district heating and cooling networks exchange heat bidirectionally at near-ambient temperatures. When one supplier owns the shared loop, it controls both the tariff and the network temperature that sets every user's conversion efficiency. Existing price-cap and cost-based rules leave this non-price instrument unregulated and reach neither the first-best dispatch nor an explicit division of gains. This paper proposes a two-part, incentive-based tariff that anchors the supplier's lump-sum fee, per building and hour, to an audited outside alternative and divides the participation gains through one regulated share. We model a mixed-integer bilevel Stackelberg game in which the supplier sets hourly tariffs and the temperature regime, anticipating the buildings' co-optimization of electricity and thermal exchange. We prove that the mechanism attains the first-best welfare, posts the shadow price of the efficient dispatch as its tariff, keeps every building at or above its outside option every hour, and keeps the supplier solvent whenever operation adds surplus. A Belgian case study confirms these properties. The mechanism reproduces the centralized welfare whenever operation is worthwhile, declines to operate otherwise, holds the loop at its first-best temperature, and outperforms cap-based regulation and Ramsey pricing in welfare, user protection, and cost recovery.

papers.title: Regular quadratic lattices are rare over real quadratic fields
papers.abstract: We show that a positive definite regular quadratic lattice of rank at least 4 over a totally real number field contains a regular sublattice that represents precisely the totally positive integers lying in an ideal. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis and a conjecture on class numbers, it follows that, for each $m$, real quadratic fields admitting a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and $m$ have density 0. Unconditionally, only finitely many real quadratic fields of narrow class number 1 admit a positive definite regular lattice of some rank between 4 and 7.

papers.title: A proof of Cigler's quadratic recurrence for Hankel determinants of Motzkin path generating functions
papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge0$ let $a_{n,k}(x,c)$ be the generating polynomial of the Motzkin paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,k)$ that never go below height $0$, where level steps have weight $c+x$ at height $0$ and weight $c$ at positive height, and let $D_{k,n}(x,c)=\det(a_{i+j,k}(x,c))_{0\le i,j\le n-1}$. We prove that for all $k\ge0$ and $n\ge2k+2$ $$D_{k,n}D_{k,n-2k-2}-x^2D_{k,n-1}D_{k,n-2k-1}=(1-x^2)D_{k,n-k-1}^2,$$ a quadratic recurrence conjectured by J. Cigler in 2023 (eq. (18) of arXiv:2309.15557 and MathOverflow question 456683). As a by-product we obtain an expression of $D_{k,n}$ as a $k\times k$ determinant built from Chebyshev polynomials reduced modulo $U_k-xU_{k-1}$, together with a bilinear identity for these $k\times k$ determinants that holds for all integer shifts. We also give a proof of Cigler's companion conjecture that $D_{k,n}(x,c)$ equals the determinant of an explicit matrix $H_{k,n}(x)$ with entries $0$, $1$ and powers of $x$, and in particular does not depend on $c$; this statement has recently been proved by V. Jandhyala, and our proof was found independently. The proofs use Chebyshev polynomials, a model of $\mathbb{Q}(x)[X]/(U_k-xU_{k-1})$ by antisymmetric Laurent polynomials, a lemma on complementary minors, and a three-term Pl\"ucker relation.

papers.title: Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?
papers.authors: Jaemin Oh, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis
papers.abstract: Trunk-basis (TB) preconditioners build the coarse space of a two-level Schwarz preconditioner from the trunk functions of a trained deep operator network (DeepONet), restricted to subdomains. Their effectiveness has been attributed to spectral bias since networks learn low frequencies first, complementing a smoother that removes the high-frequency error. Spectral bias, however, is a property of training, whereas a randomly initialized trunk with a smooth activation is already smooth. We therefore ask whether TB preconditioners need training. In one dimension, we prove that on each subdomain the span of untrained trunk functions is close to the space of low-degree polynomials under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerically, for the Poisson equation and three-dimensional linear elasticity with constant coefficients, untrained TB and piecewise polynomial coarse spaces of equal dimension yield close conjugate gradient iteration counts, while training with the standard \(\ell^2\) loss sometimes increases them. Training can improve iteration counts when high-contrast coefficients make the low-energy modes non-smooth, and if the loss measures the error in the energy norm. For the Poisson equation with contrast \(10^5\), energy-trained TB coarse spaces need fewer iterations than piecewise polynomials of equal dimension, whereas \(\ell^2\)-trained ones do not. For a topology-optimized elastic cantilever with contrast \(10^6\), the energy-trained TB space enriched with the rigid-body modes gives the fewest iterations at larger coarse dimensions. This suggests that for neural operator-based hybrid solvers, a network's inductive bias and training objective should match the solver.

papers.title: Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.

papers.title: Energy-constrained Brownian motion
papers.abstract: For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length $N$, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary reaches $M$; this random `lifetime' comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity $M$, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to $M$ on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of $N$ and $M$; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem, for one scaling regime in the case of a ball, and conjectures on the behaviour in general domains.

papers.title: Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields
papers.abstract: We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria. Notably, the exceptional components of an $F$-pure surface singularity are geometrically reduced unless the singularity is a rational double point.

papers.title: The Boolean completion of $\mathsf{S}(L)$: a refinement of localic mereology
papers.authors: M. Andrew Moshier, Imanol Mozo Carollo
papers.abstract: We construct and study the Boolean completion of the coframe $\mathsf{S}(L)$ of sublocales of a frame $L$. Realizing $\mathsf{S}(L)$ as a basis for an Alexandroff topology on $L$ and passing to the regular elements of the associated frame, we obtain a complete Boolean algebra $\mathsf{P}(L)$ whose elements are certain subsets of $L$ generalizing sublocale sets; we call them the \emph{parts} of $L$. We show that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ embeds into $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the left adjoint of a Galois connection and that the canonical embedding of $L$ into $\mathsf{S}(L)$ extends to $\mathsf{P}(L)$. From a mereological standpoint, this completion is motivated by universalism: after proving that mereological sums and exact joins coincide for separative posets, we identify $\mathsf{P}(L)$ as the sum-completion (equivalently, the exact-join-completion) of $\mathsf{S}(L)$, thereby supplying the mereological sums that $\mathsf{S}(L)$ lacks. Finally, we single out several distinguished parts of a frame: the pointless part, which extends Ball's construction beyond the $T_1$ setting, together with the part of merely points and the topological glue, the former of the two having no counterpart in the classical theory of sublocales.

papers.title: Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates
papers.abstract: In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $\mu_0$ and the first moment $\mu_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $\mu_0$, $\mu_1$ and the second moment $\mu_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$ on its own. This condition defines at once a vector space which is studied via barycentric coordinates and elementary exterior algebra, thereby yielding families of equilibrium equations for systems with any consistent number $n$ of particles and dimension $d$. As before, the present equilibrium equations are homogeneous as well as invariant by oriented isometries (for interactions depending only on mutual distances). Our method also develops and extends the approach by A. Albouy from central configurations of codimension $c=(n-1)-d$ equal to one, the so-called Dziobek configurations, to equilibria of systems of interacting particles of arbitrary codimension. Despite the similar appearance, our generalized Albouy equations constitute new equilibrium equations when $c$ is greater than one, even in the case of central configurations. The paper closes with applications to central configurations, with specific results for $n=5,6$ in dimension $d=2$.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for generalized inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract:
We consider the initial value problem for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \begin{equation*}
  i\partial_t u+\Delta u=a(x)|u|^\alpha u, \end{equation*} where $a(x)$ is a spatially dependent coefficient. We study a general class of coefficients that includes the usual inhomogeneous nonlinearity $a(x)=\lambda|x|^{-b}$ and coefficients with multiple singularities. We establish local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for both the $H^s$-subcritical and $H^s$-critical cases under suitable assumptions on $a(x)$. We also extend a fractional difference estimate of Fujiwara to Lorentz spaces.

papers.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
papers.authors: Roman Ku\v{z}el, M\'aty\'as Koniorczyk, Janez Povh
papers.abstract: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.

papers.title: Generalized Markov numbers and plane lattices
papers.abstract: We give new explicit constructions of lattice rules in the two-dimensional square and torus. It is well-known that uniformly distributed lattices (in the sense of low-discrepancy) arise from continued fractions with bounded partial denominators. We demonstrate how integers solutions of the generalized Markov equation $x^2+y^2+z^2 = kxyz-k+3$ give rise to such lattices.

papers.title: The Global Solutions to Nonlinear Thermoelastic Systems under a Null Condition
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for a class of homogeneous, isotropic nonlinear thermoelastic systems in three space dimensions. Under a null condition for purely elastic part of our system which is different from those considered by Sideris, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global classical solutions with smallness assumptions on the initial data. We use Klainerman--Sideris weighted energy estimates and time-weighted energy estimates for the heat equation to establish global existence. Moreover, we improve upon the global existence result of Ponce and Racke, who assumed that the purely elastic nonlinear terms vanish.

papers.title: On the prime index elements graph of finite groups
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, the prime index elements graph $\G(G)$, introduced by Anitha and Rajkumar, has vertex set $G$, two distinct elements being adjacent if the cyclic subgroup generated by one has prime index in that generated by the other. We show that $\G(G)$ is a bipartite blow-up of a weighted graph $\Hq(G)$ on the cyclic subgroups of $G$, which is a cartesian product of trees when $G$ is nilpotent, and use this to study several graph invariants. We characterize the groups for which $\G(G)$ is a star, a cograph, a chordal graph, or has a perfect code. We compute the sharp bounds for the independence and domination number. We give an exact formula for the strong metric dimension, bound the metric and strong metric dimensions in terms of the quotient graph, show that the upper bounds for the strong metric dimension are attained for cyclic p-groups, and all upper bounds for groups whose prime index elements graph is complete bipartite, and determine the groups attaining the lower bounds: the strong metric dimension attains it only for $\Z_p$ with $p$ odd, and we give a criterion for the metric dimension, which we solve completely for cyclic groups. For nilpotent $G$ we give necessary conditions for $\G(G)$ to be Hamiltonian, in terms of the numbers of covers of cyclic subgroups in the Sylow subgroups, and prove that they are also sufficient when all Sylow subgroups but one are cyclic. We also show that a nilpotent group with a Hamiltonian path is $\Z_3$ or of the form $K\times\Z_2$ with $|K|$ odd, and that in the abelian case above a Hamiltonian path exists exactly when a Hamiltonian cycle does. Finally, we characterize the finite groups $G$ for which $\G(G)$ is planar, toroidal or of genus two.

papers.title: Essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of the essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. As direct applications of our main results, we obtain compactness criteria for such composition operators.

papers.title: The categorical graph minor conjecture and matching complexes
papers.abstract: In the graph minor category $\mathcal G$ of Miyata, Proudfoot and Ramos, the morphisms are the ways of obtaining one connected graph from another by deleting and contracting edges. The categorical graph minor conjecture asserts that every submodule of a finitely generated $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is finitely generated; it is known for graphs of bounded first Betti number. We disprove this conjecture: it fails for the module assigning to each graph the free module on its spanning trees, which is generated by one element. A quotient of this module has unbounded torsion. We prove, however, that the conjecture holds for all modules depending on a minor morphism only through the induced injection of edge sets. This applies to matching complexes. Let $M_d(G)$ be the complex of edge sets of $G$ spanning subgraphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We prove that the $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module $G\mapsto H_i(M_d(G);\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated for all $i$ and $d$, which for $d=1$ confirms a conjecture recorded by Ramos, and that a positive integer depending only on $i$ annihilates the torsion of all these groups. The proofs combine Robertson and Seymour's labelled graph minor theorem with a new criterion: if a category has a faithful functor to finite sets and injections and, for every finite set of colours, its objects with coloured underlying sets are well-quasi-ordered by colour-preserving morphisms, then its representations over a left-Noetherian ring form a locally Noetherian category. Unlike the Gr\"obner method of Sam and Snowden, this criterion requires no ordering compatible with the morphisms.

papers.title: A Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
papers.abstract: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. We obtain existence and uniqueness results for arbitrary finite time horizons.

papers.title: Global existence and scattering of large solutions of the cubic Dirac equation
papers.authors: Timothy Candy, Sebastian Herr, Kenji Nakanishi
papers.abstract: We construct global dispersive solutions to the massive cubic Dirac equation (Soler Model) for initial data with large critical Sobolev norm. Because of a lack of a coercive energy in the Dirac equation, the only previously known large solutions are solitons (which are non-dispersive) and Majorana-solutions (which are in fact solutions to a linear equation). Here, the new strategy is to exploit the non-relativistic limit, which connects the Dirac equation to a system of Schr\"odinger equations with cubic nonlinearities, and then to develop a scattering theory for this limiting system.

papers.title: Approximation of the Nonautonomous Maxwell System with an Interface
papers.abstract: To obtain higher-regularity solutions for nonautonomous Maxwell systems with an interface, we approximate the initial data and coefficients by smoother counterparts. To preserve compatibility conditions of the approximations, required to obtain solutions to the Maxwell systems, we systematically adjust the approximating sequence of initial data. While the existing well-posedness theory in [14] guarantees more regular solutions, standard a-priori estimates fail to ensure convergence in the desired norm. We overcome this by a mollification argument and a div-curl estimate from [4] and [7].

papers.title: A Higher-Dimensional Extension of the Laugesen--Siudeja Lower Bound
papers.abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional analogue of the lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture, using a covariance normalization of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. We give a covariance-dependent lower bound for every bounded convex domain. From this bound we obtain the optimal constant for convex planar domains and for simplices in every dimension \(d\geq2\). If the simplex covariance inequality stated in a 2026 preprint holds, the same constant is optimal over all bounded convex domains in dimensions \(d\geq3\). In each of these cases, the infimum is approached by compressing a regular simplex in the direction of an edge and is unattained.

papers.title: Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares
papers.abstract: Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near typical service. Thus one-time power distributions alone do not determine reliability.

papers.title: On the Role of Fisher Information, Variance and Asymptotics in Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: Bahadur's \emph{Lectures on the Theory of Estimation} close with a chapter on asymptotics: asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimator, Fisher's bound on its asymptotic variance with Hodges's counterexample, and local asymptotic normality. A companion paper read the earlier lectures with one modification, replacing the point estimator by a generalized estimator---Fisher's continuum of significance tests---assessed by information rather than variance. This paper reads Chapter 8 the same way. At each of its three parts the classical statement is an approximation about a point estimator, while the corresponding statement about the score is exact at every sample size. Superefficiency does not arise, because information is bounded by the Fisher information at every $n$; Hodges's estimator, computed exactly, is fully efficient at the origin and loses information only where its mean square error is worst. The information of a generalized estimator is argued to be Fisher information: the mean rate at which a continuum of tests responds to the parameter, standardized by its variance. The resulting Fisher upper bound differs geometrically, not merely algebraically, from the Cram\'er--Rao lower bound. The extension is not empty: the $t$-test continuum loses about half an observation's worth of the information in $\bar X$ at every $n$.

papers.title: Proximity and Remoteness in Trees with given Segment Sequence
papers.authors: Imran Allie, Brandon Du Preez, Zion Hefty, Sonwabile Mafunda
papers.abstract:
The average distance of a vertex $v$ of a connected graph $G$ is the arithmetic mean of the distances from $v$ to all other vertices of $G$. The proximity $\pi(G)$ and the remoteness $\rho(G)$ of $G$ are the minimum and the maximum of the average distances of the vertices of $G$, respectively. A segment $S$ of a tree is a path-subtree whose terminal vertices are either branching or pendant vertices, and all internal vertices have degree $2$. The segment sequence $(\ell_{S_1}, \ell_{S_2},\ldots,\ell_{S_m})$ of T is the non-increasing sequence of the lengths of all segments of T.
  In this paper, we characterise trees with a given segment sequence that minimise proximity and those that maximise remoteness. For trees that minimise remoteness, we establish sufficient conditions under which the tree is starlike and conjecture that a remoteness-minimising tree is always either starlike or a ($\Delta,2$)-tree. For trees that maximise proximity, we derive a collection of necessary conditions that any tree maximising proximity must satisfy.

papers.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
papers.authors: Shiqi Li, Jiawei He, Jianhua Huang
papers.abstract: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(\mu\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_\mu\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_\mu\) is upper semicontinuous at \(\mu=0\) almost surely.

papers.title: Linear support bounds for supercuspidal matrix coefficients of p-adic groups
papers.authors: Itay Glazer, Erez Lapid, Zhengyu Mao, Mark Shusterman
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. For any standard congruence tower $K_{\bullet}=(K_n)$ in $\mathbf{G}(F)$, supercuspidal matrix coefficients between $K_n$-fixed vectors are supported in an adjoint ball of radius $an+b_{K_{\bullet}}$, compact modulo the center, with $a$ depending only on $F$ and $\mathbf{G}$. When $\mathbf{G}(F)$ is non-compact modulo its center, the linear dependence on $n$ is optimal. In algebraic families we obtain a uniform radius $An+Bk+C+\operatorname{val}_{F}(N)$, where $k$ bounds the logarithmic height of the parameter. We deduce a sharp linear bound for the exponent in Bernstein's stabilization theorem. For quasi-split classical groups, we also remove the dyadic level restriction in the limit multiplicity theorem.

papers.title: Dynamics of a spherical ferromagnet on a non-conducting incline in an external magnetic field
papers.authors: Rasmus C. Raschke, Tim Matthies, Roland Wiesendanger, Elena Y. Vedmedenko
papers.abstract: Magnetic particles of various shapes and sizes are used in biomedical applications, robotics, nanomagnetism, electrotechnology, and education. Yet despite years of study, a theoretical description of the rolling motion of a solid magnetic sphere still eludes us. One of the reasons is that coupling magnetic fields with mechanical degrees of freedom creates a highly non-linear motion with non-holonomic constraints, which makes modeling these systems analytically or by simulations non-trivial. The Lagrange-d'Alembertian approach to holonomic systems remains one of the most versatile methods to prove central theorems and solve problems in analytical mechanics and electrodynamics. While non-holonomic systems are not accessible by the original theory, recent developments generalize the principle to certain dissipative systems. Here, we present a successful application of these developments to a simple mechanical system comprising a magnetic solid sphere on an incline within an external magnetic field. Using numerical simulations, we characterized how the system depends on its initial parameters. Furthermore, our findings are in line with recent experiments, demonstrating that even very weak magnetic fields can cause unexpected motion of ferromagnetic objects. The simplicity of this example also makes it a promising candidate for undergraduate physics education where the treatment of non-holonomic variational principles is still widely uncommon.

papers.title: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading
papers.abstract: A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.

papers.title: Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean-Field Games
papers.abstract: We study second order variational mean-field games with quadratic Hamiltonian. In analogy with entropic optimal transport, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and the second author recently proposed an entropy-minimization formulation of the problem, which could be interpreted as the Lagrangian counterpart of the classical Eulerian approach. We investigate the small-noise $\Gamma$-limit for the Lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation and establish $\Gamma$-convergence of second order mean-field games towards their deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into another (dynamical) proof of the convergence of the Schr\"odinger problem to optimal transport. Moreover, we study the original Eulerian problem and prove a first order energy expansion, which establishes a selection principle for minimizers of the deterministic problem.

papers.title: Extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number
papers.abstract:
The binding number of a graph, introduced by Woodall [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1973], is a central topic in structural and extremal graph theory. Recently, Chen et al. introduced the $k$-th binding number $\beta^k(G)$. Anderson [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1971] proved that every graph $G$ of even order with $\beta^1(G)\ge\frac43$ contains a perfect matching, and that the bound $\frac43$ is best possible. For $k\ge2$, Chen et al. proved that $\beta^k(G)\ge1$ guarantees a $k$-factor whenever $kn$ is even, and that the bound $1$ is best possible. The above facts reveal a fundamental distinction between the higher-order binding number and the classical binding number. This distinction makes extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number particularly intriguing.
  For positive integers $n,$ $k$ and $r$, we in this paper determine the maximum size and spectral radius among all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\beta^k(G)<r$, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs, respectively. In particular, when $k=1$, our results imply the corresponding extremal results of Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin., 2024] and Liu, Chen and Fan [Electron. J. Combin., 2026]. Our proofs develop a structural framework that relates higher-order neighborhood inequalities to the structure of the complements of graphs. This framework may provide an approach to Tur\'{a}n-type problem involving the $k$-th binding number, and the approach may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
papers.abstract:
This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology.
  In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a subscheme of a certain projective variety. Varying the hopping-rate parameter $p$, we give a one-parameter family $S$ of the solution sets. We show that, for the ASEP with $n$ sites and $m$ particles, the fiber $S|_p$ with generic $p$ contains $\binom{n}{m}$ points with multiplicity, which equals the expected number of admissible Bethe roots to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equation.

papers.title: Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally
papers.authors: Jorge Acu\~na Flores, Joscha Henheik, Marius Lemm, Daniele Toniolo
papers.abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. This allows us to use one-body transport results to establish the expected many-body transport behavior on finite time scales in the following two illustrative settings: (i) We prove quantum diffusion, as quantified by a certain operator spreading diagnostic, in weakly interacting and weakly disordered Fermi systems in dimensions $D\geq2$ on large finite time scales based on the non-interacting diffusion result of Black, Drogin, and Hern\'andez [arXiv:2506.06468]. (ii) We show for Fermi-Hubbard models with initially low spin-down density, that all local multi-time spin-up correlation functions are approximated by their free counterparts. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].

papers.title: Applicability of the MPCC approach to Zeng reformulations of nonlinear pessimistic bilevel programming
papers.abstract: The vanilla method in bilevel programming is to reformulate it as a single-level mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCC), via the KKT conditions of the lower-level. This method seemed to work only for optimistic formulations. However, in (Zeng, 2020), B. Zeng presented a general method to reduce pessimistic bilevel problems to optimistic ones. In this note, we study how to apply the MPCC approach to the pessimistic counterpart through Zeng's reformulation (Zeng, 2020). While we show that it cannot be applied directly since constraint qualification can be destroyed by the reformulation, it still can be used to solve natural relaxations, in the spirit of (Wiesemann,2013),(Loridan & Morgan,1989), (Loridan & Morgan,1996).

papers.title: Projectively Flat Spherically Symmetric Sprays of Constant Curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays of constant curvature. We derive a system of equations that is equivalent to the constant-curvature condition for such sprays and solve it to obtain a complete classification of the projective factor \(p(r,s)\) into four explicit families. We further show that the sprays induced by projectively flat spherically symmetric Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature \(K=0\), \(K=-1\), and \(K=1\) are all special cases of our classification, thereby confirming that the sprays induced by these constant-flag-curvature Finsler metrics are fully contained in our framework.

papers.title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
papers.abstract: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.

papers.title: Convex Structure-Preserving EDMD: Passive Koopman Matrices as $Q$-Contractions
papers.abstract: Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) approximates the Koopman operator using a matrix based on a finite set of observables. However, the least-squares matrix of a port-Hamiltonian (pH) system is generally neither passive nor invariant-preserving. We demonstrate that the implicit midpoint discretization of a lifted pH model precisely preserves energy balance, passivity, and all linear Casimirs for every step size. For a fixed storage metric $Q$, the resulting Koopman matrices are the Cayley transforms of $(J-R)Q$, where $J$ is skew-symmetric and $R$ is positive semidefinite. This set does not depend on the step size and is the closure of all Q-contractions. This set is LMI-representable; therefore, structure-preserving EDMD, including ports through a discrete-time Kalman-Yakubovich-Popov condition and Casimirs through affine constraints, is a semidefinite program.
