We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

papers.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
papers.abstract:
For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $\Delta^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[
  c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matou\v{s}ek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound.
  The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Cocomparability, Co-Bipartite, and Distance-Hereditary Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether $\omega(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete on connected cocomparability graphs of diameter two and independence number three. The reduction supplies a partition into three cliques, a maximum clique, an optimal ordinary coloring, and a dominating edge. Every constructed graph needs either $\omega(G)$ or $\omega(G)+1$ PCF colors. The result also gives NP-completeness on AT-free graphs. For the co-bipartite subclass, we give a complete matching characterization and an $O(n^6)$-time algorithm for an optimal coloring. The cocktail-party graphs are exactly the co-bipartite graphs requiring two more colors than their ordinary chromatic number; every other co-bipartite graph needs at most one additional color. The matching method extends to all graphs with independence number at most two, giving an $O(n^6\log n)$-time optimization algorithm. Finally, for distance-hereditary graphs, we decide whether $k$ colors suffice in $O(n+m+nk^{10})$ time and compute an optimal coloring in $O(n^{11}+m)$ time without fixing the palette size. The algorithm uses a binary decomposition and groups colors according to five possible behaviors at the boundary of a subgraph.

papers.title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
papers.authors: Cyril B\'en\'ezet, Cyril Nefzaoui-Blanchard, Sergio Pulido
papers.abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.

papers.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
papers.authors: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle
papers.abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

papers.title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
papers.authors: \'Angela Tajuelo-Valbuena, Jorge Hidalgo, Ricardo Guti\'errez, Carlos P\'erez-Espigares
papers.abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

papers.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
papers.abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the improved bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})^2)}. \] An exponential dependence is necessary, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.

papers.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
papers.abstract: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

papers.title: A boundary integral equation solver for capsule suspensions
papers.authors: Joar Bagge, Ziyu Du, George Biros
papers.abstract: Deformable capsules serve as models for biological cells, such as red blood cells, as well as for synthetic capsules in biomedical and industrial applications. In this work, we introduce a framework for fast and robust simulation of deformable capsules in three-dimensional Stokes flow, both in unbounded domains and in pipe-confined geometries. We solve the Stokes equations using a boundary integral formulation, employing a partition-of-unity discretization for the capsule membrane and the trapezoidal rule with regularization to handle the singular quadrature. Dense periodic interactions are evaluated via a fast Ewald summation scheme, achieving $O(N \log N)$ complexity for $N$ grid points. The interfacial forces on the capsule membrane are modeled using the Skalak constitutive law. We carry out a spectral analysis of this model for small perturbations of a spherical capsule, which indicates that the relaxation dynamics are intrinsically stable. However, the nonlinear character of the Skalak model induces aliasing errors that can compromise numerical stability. To address this when needed, we perform de-aliasing through upsampling and spectral filtering, and we derive guidelines for choosing appropriate filter parameters, thereby stabilizing the method. We investigate the stability and convergence behavior of the resulting scheme and conduct simulations of long-time dynamics, focusing on the relaxation of unconfined capsules and the lateral migration of pipe-confined capsules under various flow conditions.

papers.title: Incentive Compatible Mechanisms for Sequential Fair Resource Allocation with Private Demands
papers.authors: Ramtin Salamat, Sean R. Sinclair, Seyed M. R. Iravani
papers.abstract: We study a strategic variant of the canonical online fair allocation problem, where a planner must sequentially allocate a divisible resource to agents with privately known demands. At each stage, the planner announces an allocation rule, the agent reports their demand, and the planner allocates resources according to the rule and the reported demand. Unlike the standard model, we allow agents to strategically misreport their needs, as can arise in nonprofit settings where demand is self-reported and monetary transfers are unavailable. We characterize the structure of incentive-compatible (IC) allocation rules in this model, and use this to identify conditions under which the optimal mechanism has a simple cap structure. We then develop an approximation method for the optimal IC mechanism through a careful reduction of the discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Numerical experiments show that ignoring strategic reporting can be substantially more costly than imposing incentive compatibility.

papers.title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
papers.authors: Benjamin Luke, Sudip Shiwakoti, Shayan Nadeem, Ronald Morgan, Walter Wilcox
papers.abstract: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.

papers.title: Estimating contextual networks via Fisher-scoring surrogate likelihood
papers.abstract: When networks are accompanied by vertex-level covariates, effectively integrating and aligning the information underlying both data sources becomes a natural yet critical task. Current spectral approaches, despite their popularity, may yield suboptimal results and necessitate the specification of additional tuning parameters that are contingent upon unobservable signal-to-noise ratios. We propose a tuning-free, likelihood-based learning framework for estimating latent positions in contextual generalized random dot product graphs in the presence of high-dimensional vertex covariates with a low-rank structure. Our method constructs a smooth surrogate likelihood and implements a Fisher-scoring algorithm to iteratively estimate latent positions without introducing additional tuning parameters that depend on the network sparsity. We establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the Fisher-scoring estimator. Application to real-world data further demonstrates the method's practical utility, offering a principled and scalable alternative to spectral approaches for analyzing contextual networks in high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Estimating conditional means under missingness-not-at-random with incomplete auxiliary variables
papers.authors: Maya B. Mathur, Shaun Seaman, Willi Zhang, Sean McGrath, Ilya Shpitser
papers.abstract:
Estimators assuming missingness at random (MAR) can fail under missingness not at random (MNAR). Introducing complete auxiliary variables sometimes restores MAR by breaking dependence between analysis variables and missingness. However, if the auxiliaries are themselves incomplete, MAR typically remains violated.
  We derive necessary and sufficient, weaker-than-MAR conditions under which the MAR functional $\mu_{\rm MAR}$ for a conditional mean $E[Y \mid X]$ is correct. We also propose an alternative identifying functional for $E[Y \mid X]$, called $\mu_{\rm MIA}$ for "Marginalization over Incomplete Auxiliaries", along with sufficient conditions for $\mu_{\rm MIA}$ to be correct.
  For MNAR distributions in which all missingness patterns can occur and certain context-specific independences do not occur, there are two straightforward cases where $\mu_{\rm MIA}$ is correct for a strict superset of the MNAR distributions for which $\mu_{\rm MAR}$ is correct: (1) $X$ is complete and $Y$ is incomplete; or (2) all auxiliary variables are incomplete. In case (1), $\mu_{\rm MAR}$ is always incorrect, barring knife-edge cases. Determining whether either case holds requires no knowledge of the MNAR mechanism.
  We propose estimators of $\mu_{\rm MIA}$, including g-computation and doubly robust estimators. Our R package miapack implements a semiparametric iterated-conditional-expectations estimator. We illustrate with real data and present simulations comparing estimators of $\mu_{\rm MIA}$ and $\mu_{\rm MAR}$.

papers.title: Magnetic vector potentials and helicity in periodic domains
papers.abstract: For a magnetic field in three-dimensional Euclidean space, we argue about the existence of a magnetic vector potential in a finite cuboid with periodic boundary conditions. We first argue in physical terms by representing periodic domains as tori and show that in some cases, the generating electric current is unphysical. We then represent magnetic fields and vector potentials as differential 2 and 1-forms. For a given magnetic field we ask the question whether a corresponding vector potential exists. Singly periodic domains are shown to always allow for a vector potential. For doubly periodic domains it only exists if the net magnetic flux through the non-periodic dimension vanishes, while for triply periodic domains the net flux must vanish in all directions. This has implications for the definition of magnetic helicity in periodic domains. We show that periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental contradictions to the interpretation as the linking of magnetic field lines. For the helicity we can even construct magnetic fields in periodic domains for which the magnetic helicity exists, but the calculations of the magnetic helicity do not lead to meaningful results due to the gauge freedom. With that we conclude that in presence of a mean magnetic field the calculated magnetic helicity cannot be interpreted geometrically in a straightforward way. However, using the winding gauge we can recover the geometric interpretation of the helicity as the flux averaged magnetic field line winding. Finally, for the solar relevant non-periodic domain with finite point-wise flux and zero integrated flux, using an appropriate gauge transformation the magnetic helicity can be shown to vanish. The winding helicity, however, would lead to a non-vanishing value here.

papers.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
papers.abstract: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. Frequent itemset mining, at its lowest feasible support, finds no set above five conditions; hierarchical clustering cannot control cluster size. With a clinical large language model, the database could suggest which further conditions a patient is at risk of.

papers.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
papers.authors: Siavash Ameli, Chris van der Heide, Liam Hodgkinson, Michael W. Mahoney
papers.abstract: Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for "spectral decompression": a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts the spectral decompression problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform of the companion matrix. This approach bypasses the instabilities of traditional inversion and provides a robust methodology for scaling covariance matrices and even their generalized variants (including Hessian matrices) that lack unitary invariance. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through experiments on a variety of random matrix examples, showing that DD successfully captures the complex spectral signatures of large-scale systems.

papers.title: Subspace Inference for Multilayer Latent Space Networks: Intrinsic Geometry and One-Step Estimator
papers.abstract: Multilayer networks on a common node set, such as brain connectomes of several animals with one layer per animal, often share a low-dimensional geometry but differ in how strongly each layer expresses it and in node activity. We study a multilayer latent space network model that combines an invariant subspace common to all layers with layer-specific interaction matrices and node-by-layer degree effects. By introducing the generalized Cayley transform of the invariant subspace, we characterize the intrinsic geometry of the model and obtain sharp convergence rates for the maximum likelihood estimator, asymptotic normality and Neyman orthogonality for vertex-level parameters, and asymptotic normality for the interaction matrices with a non-negligible bias. Plug-in estimates of the bias and covariance give debiased confidence regions and tests of equality between layers. We also propose an easy-to-implement one-step estimator that attains the same vertex-level limits. In a real-world mouse connectome dataset, the inbred strain that lacks a corpus callosum shows about twice the hemispheric segregation of the other three strains.

papers.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
papers.abstract: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

papers.title: Fair Property Tax: Reducing Regressivity in Machine-Learning Valuation
papers.authors: Nicolas Acevedo Villena, Haihao Lu, Michael Wagner, Timothy Sparer
papers.abstract: Advanced machine-learning models are increasingly used for property valuation in tax assessment. Although these models can achieve high predictive accuracy, they may systematically assign higher valuation-to-sale ratios to lower-priced properties, a pattern known as regressivity. In collaboration with the Cook County Assessor's Office (CCAO), we develop and evaluate two training methods that substantially reduce this regressive pattern while maintaining price-scale predictive accuracy. The Direct method has been incorporated into CCAO's public residential valuation software. Retaining the LightGBM model class used at CCAO, we propose a Direct penalty on squared covariance between log valuation errors and log sale prices, and an observation-additive Surrogate that yields a weighted squared-error loss. We evaluate both methods in our implementation of the CCAO workflow, using seven chronological validation folds, a held-out test set, and a 2025-forward test set. Measured by the magnitude of price-related bias (PRB), regressivity falls by approximately 49% on held-out sales and 39% on 2025 sales at a Surrogate setting selected by cross-validation, relative to the same LightGBM model fitted without the penalty. Price-scale $R^2$ is essentially unchanged. Its small rise, from 0.893 to 0.897 on held-out sales and from 0.904 to 0.908 on 2025 sales, reflects overall valuation level. Log-price RMSE rises by 3.1% and 1.7%, respectively. Paired sale-bootstrap 90% intervals for the PRB reductions lie within about two percentage points of these estimates. In an additional eight-county benchmark, both methods reduce regressivity in every county, with higher log-price prediction error as the expected tradeoff. These findings demonstrate a practical way to reduce measured regressivity within an existing assessor workflow while preserving price-scale predictive performance.

papers.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
papers.abstract: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks. For the coordinate-facet complex of the six-simplex, we compute a coning index of six over the integers and three after inverting two, allowing arbitrary integral directions within each facet. A class in the homology of the unrestricted kernel complex characterizes the remaining seven-input problem; its vanishing is equivalent to an integral filling of a fixed target. We also construct a finite character that separates rational from three-local representability in a dictionary containing two known constructions and all pairs of edge-disjoint three-edge forests. This obstruction permits nonsymmetric coefficients and is confined to the specified dictionary. Control of lower-dimensional remainders yields a sufficient criterion in the top-dimensional quotient. Exact certificates and verification programs accompany the finite calculations.

papers.title: Algebraic dark solitons versus rogue waves in the massive Thirring model
papers.abstract: We address the existence of algebraically decaying solitary waves on the nonzero wave background in the massive Thirring model (MTM) in laboratory coordinates. We find the precise condition of the spectral stability and instability of the nonzero wave background. In the case of instability, we distinguish modulational, side-band, and full-band instabilities and show that the rogue wave exists if and only if the nonzero wave background is modulationally unstable. For the other unstable cases and in the case of stability, we show that there exist exactly two algebraic dark solitons which correspond to the end points in the admissible range of the wave speed for the dark soliton propagation.

papers.title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
papers.abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bu\v{z}ek, Hillery, and Werner.

papers.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
papers.authors: Eduardo Bittencourt, Sante Carloni, Giuseppe De Maria, Peter K. S. Dunsby
papers.abstract: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|\lambda|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|\lambda|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|\lambda|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|\lambda|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

papers.title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
papers.abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

papers.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
papers.abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

papers.title: Smoothed Conformal Testing with Small Calibration Sets
papers.abstract: A small calibration sample restricts split conformal $p$-values to a coarse rank grid. Randomization removes this discretization, but its effect depends on both the smoothing interval and the allocation of auxiliary random variables. Independent tie-block randomization is exactly valid under null exchangeability. When calibration and null scores are jointly exchangeable conditional on the alternative scores, we prove positive regression dependence and hence Benjamini--Hochberg false discovery rate control, including for atomic score distributions. Smoothing over calibration-dependent rank cells agrees with tie-block randomization when calibration scores are distinct and no test score ties a calibration score, but can fail marginal validity with atoms. Assigning sorted random draws according to score order can invalidate even a single null $p$-value. An exact two-test example violates the usual $\pi_0\alpha$ bound, and simulations with continuous scores exhibit false discovery rates above the nominal level $\alpha$. Finally, conditional moment identities and normal-model illustrations show that removing the rank grid does not remove calibration uncertainty. Randomization can produce additional discoveries, including when ordinary conformal testing cannot reject at all, but it does not generally substitute for a larger calibration sample.

papers.title: Gap-label bounds and optical reconstruction of Landau-subband quantum geometry
papers.abstract: We derive a magnetic gap-label lower bound on the internal quantum weight of Landau subbands that remains nonzero even when the occupied Chern number vanishes. Using the second fundamental forms of nested subbundles to decompose the quantum geometric tensor, we isolate the constraint imposed by the uniform parent curvature and show that the excess quantum weight above the bound equals twice the weaker circular transition weight. For a noninteracting parabolic band with a periodic scalar potential, Landau-level mixing preserves the integrated relative curvature while the occupied direct gap remains open. Nevertheless, uncorrected sub-cyclotron absorption need not satisfy the projected bound. Using exact circular-dipole relations, we reconstruct the low-frequency guiding-centre weight and signed dichroism from circularly polarized absorption. This reconstruction removes the first-order orbit-polarization contribution. For an insulating filling of an isolated lowest-Landau-level-derived cluster, a potential-gradient estimate bounds the omitted remote-transition weight quadratically at weak coupling. This yields a finite-window lower bound on reconstructed quantum weight and bounds the deviation of reconstructed dichroism from the integrated relative curvature.

papers.title: Gradient-based optimization of buoyancy distributions for lazy-wave risers
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel gradient-based approach for optimizing the buoyancy distribution of lazy-wave offshore risers. The static response is modeled with a total potential energy formulation for a geometrically nonlinear, inextensible beam on an elastic seabed. The total potential energy is discretized by finite differences and the resulting nonlinear equilibrium system is solved by a two stage continuation procedure, in which the line length and then the buoyancy load are increased incrementally, with Newton--Raphson iterations and an Armijo line search. The design variables are the uplift ratios at the nodes where buoyancy modules may be installed. The optimization minimizes a quadratic measure of buoyancy demand subject to constraints on the maximum curvature and effective tension. The gradients of the constraints are computed by means of a discrete adjoint sensitivity analysis. Three design parametrizations are compared: a continuous formulation with independent nodal uplift ratios, a grouped formulation with fixed module assignments, and a formulation inspired by discrete material optimization that simultaneously selects the uplift ratios of a small catalog of module types and their placement along the riser. The latter yields practical designs with a limited number of module sizes. The framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for preliminary design of lazy-wave configurations.

papers.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

papers.title: Adaptive Redescending Regression with $q$-Polynomial Losses
papers.authors: Maoxuan Miao, Shurong Zheng, You-Gan Wang, Jiming Jiang
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of smooth $q$-polynomial losses for robust joint regression--scale estimation. The family contains the Cauchy loss at $q=1$ and converges pointwise to the squared loss as $q$ increases. For every finite $q$, its regression score is bounded and redescending, while its scale score is bounded and permits explicit analysis of scale existence. We formulate simultaneous estimation through a surrogate likelihood with a common scale calibration $\kappa=1/2$ and select $q$ by maximizing the normalized surrogate likelihood over a finite candidate set. We investigate existence, large-sample behaviour, and the robustness implications of the loss family and discuss how optional modification of the scale score, for example by taking $\kappa=q/2$, can increase the threshold against scale explosion. This breakdown-oriented adjustment is distinct from the baseline estimator and requires its own joint breakdown analysis. An MM-type algorithm provides a practical implementation. Numerical investigations assess the resulting robustness--efficiency trade-off under different tail regimes.

papers.title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
papers.abstract:
How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $\rho$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses.
  For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(\rho-2)/\rho$; at $\rho=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $\rho>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs.
  At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.

papers.title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
papers.authors: Pouriya Ghadimi, Maximilian Fr\"ohlich, Aaron Sander, Martin Eigel, Richard M. Milbradt
papers.abstract: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schr\"odinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

papers.title: The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
papers.authors: Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J. -Q. Liang
papers.abstract: We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ have purely imaginary energies $\pm i\hbar\omega(n+1/2)$. In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for $T>0$ and the growing antiresonant branch converging for $T<0$. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form $\pm i\hbar\omega(z(d/dz)+1/2)$, and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. The two convergence domains correspond to one-sided contraction semigroups of dilations. Finally, we construct bi-coherent states whose biorthogonal position and momentum second cumulants are purely imaginary and complex conjugate, with product $\hbar^2/4$. The corresponding Heisenberg expectation values follow the exact classical hyperbolic trajectories for arbitrary real initial positions and momenta.

papers.title: Banana D-modules
papers.authors: Giacomo Brunello, Wojciech Flieger, Yoshiaki Goto, Saiei-Jaeyeong Matsubara-Heo, Nobuki Takayama
papers.abstract: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

papers.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
papers.authors: P\'{e}ter Naszvadi, Marcell Tukora, Roman Ku\v{z}el, M\'{a}ty\'{a}s Koniorczyk
papers.abstract: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.

papers.title: Emergent Causality of Macroscopic Transport and Equilibration in Long-Range Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent $\alpha\in(D,D+1)$ in $D$ spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with $\alpha\in (1,3/2)$, whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.

papers.title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
papers.authors: Umberto Biccari, Junqing Huang, Kang Liu, Enrique Zuazua
papers.abstract: Generative models transform simple random inputs into samples that resemble observed data. For a finite training set, a central question is how its geometry shapes the terminal dynamics and the probabilities assigned to individual samples. We address this question for flow matching with linear interpolation between independent Gaussian and empirical samples. The squared distance to the training set generates explicit paths contracting exponentially toward the nearest sample. We prove that exact trajectories restarted at prescribed late-time states approximate these paths uniformly over all elapsed times and compact sets of starting states away from Voronoi interfaces, with an error exponentially small in the inverse squared restart noise scale. The initial mass near interfaces controls the quadratic Wasserstein error between the exact and reference laws. For Gaussian and fixed Gaussian-tube restart laws, this gives a square-root rate in the restart noise scale, uniform over time, which a two-site example shows to be sharp in general. At ties, the Clarke subdifferential characterizes the graphical limit of the rescaled velocity field. This geometry motivates two learning methods: fitting the distance potential with value and gradient supervision, and fitting velocities along explicit contraction paths. A transport estimate separates initialization mismatch, velocity error, incomplete contraction, and endpoint allocation. MNIST experiments illustrate the distinct roles of support proximity, nearest-site retention, and feature fidelity. These results connect flow matching and score-based diffusion through a common limiting geometry and show how asymptotic analysis can inform the design and evaluation of generative models.

papers.title: Detection of genuine multipartite entanglement by means of entanglement monotones
papers.authors: Sylvain Carrozza, Johann Chevrier, Luca Lionni
papers.abstract: We look for pure state entanglement monotones that may serve as certificates of a strong form of genuine multipartite entanglement, that we refer to as irreducible entanglement: a $D$-partite state (with $D\geq 3$) is irreducibly $D$-partite entangled if it cannot be decomposed as a product of states that are at most $(D-1)$-partite entangled. We start by establishing a no-go result proving that no reasonable genuine multipartite entanglement entropy can simultaneously obey LOCC-monotonicity and subadditivity. After relaxing the first condition to LO-monotonicity, we provide a simple method generating genuine multipartite entanglement monotones with the desired properties. Focusing on a subfamily of these monotones, we show that they are able to detect any form of genuine tripartite entanglement in three-qubit systems.

papers.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
papers.authors: Tiancheng Xu, Guowei Dou, Xiang Ji, ZhengTai Xiong, Long Wang, Wensheng Yu
papers.abstract: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

papers.title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
papers.authors: Han Yan, Jin Zhu, Chengchun Shi, Tengyao Wang
papers.abstract: Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. We show that a single pretrained Transformer can deliver efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass, without deriving efficient influence functions or estimating nuisance functions. Pretrained on simulated data with the true parameter as the only label, the Transformer learns the posterior mean and covariance of the queried estimand and hence returns an estimate and a Wald-type confidence region. Theoretically, we prove that, for locally flat pretraining priors of slowly growing complexity, the posterior mean is efficient for every queried estimand. The Transformer inherits this efficiency with asymptotically exact coverage, in probability over evaluation populations and queries, even under distribution shift. We also reveal that the guarantee places much higher demands on pretraining when the data-generating distribution is fixed, as in classical frequentist inference. Experiments on causal inference, partial linear regression, and survival analysis show that the pretrained model generally achieves the lowest estimation error among competing methods, with nearly nominal coverage, at a computational cost of only about 0.02 seconds per dataset.

papers.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
papers.abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

papers.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
papers.authors: Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu
papers.abstract: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.

papers.title: Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization
papers.abstract:
One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. Of the many consequences of this lack of conditional expectation, we consider the problem of defining the quantum conditional relative entropy, i.e., the relative entropy between two quantum states conditioned to a sub-region or sub-algebra. We discuss how, when the conditional expectation map is not defined, there are multiple, non-equivalent ways to define a quantum conditional relative entropy quantity, and we present some of their properties.
  Classical conditional relative entropy has played a fundamental role in many applications to spin systems, and in particular in proving logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. A key feature of conditional relative entropy that intervenes in these results is its quasi-factorization or approximate tensorization property: informally, the relative entropy is almost super-additive over weakly-dependent sub-algebras. It is then not surprising that the key to obtaining similar applications in the quantum setting, such as quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities in spin systems, has been to obtain approximate factorization results for the quantum conditional relative entropy, with the added complication that there is not a unique definition of conditional relative entropy to work with. We review the recent results regarding quasi-factorization of the quantum conditional relative entropy, in strong and weak forms.

papers.title: Complex chaotic Boltzmann machines as deterministic representations of quantum states
papers.abstract: Neural networks and tensor networks have opened new ways to explore quantum systems by parameterizing families of wave functions through the structure and parameters of a network. Here we extend this perspective to a dynamical representation: we introduce a complex chaotic Boltzmann machine that assigns a deterministic system to a pure quantum state. We extend Suzuki's construction to incorporate both Born probabilities and relative phases. The probabilities set the trajectory velocities in a hypercube, while the phases define a complex field that lifts its Poincare sections. The evolution is determined by the network parameters and initial conditions, without random choices during flights or configuration changes. Our analysis of two qubits and study of three-qubit families show how relations between probabilities organize regular curves, islands, and unstable regions, and how phases distinguish states that share the same Born dynamics. This architecture turns a wave-function parameterization into a geometry of trajectories, providing a tool to explore probabilities, phases, and symmetries together across families of states.

papers.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
papers.abstract: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

papers.title: Energy-preserving Bayesian model reduction: closed-form structured posteriors and probabilistic stability certificates for quadratic operator inference
papers.authors: Jo\~ao Victor Galv\~ao da Mata, Mengwu Guo
papers.abstract:
Bayesian operator inference learns reduced-order models (ROMs) with polynomial structure from state data and returns a closed-form Gaussian posterior over the reduced operators. That posterior is unconstrained, so it gives positive probability to operators with unbounded dynamics, and current practice controls this only through finite-horizon simulation tests on a few samples. We show that energy preservation of the quadratic operator is a set of linear equality constraints, which can be imposed exactly inside the Bayesian formulation without losing the closed form. In particular, the constrained posterior follows from one Kalman-type update of the unconstrained one, and its samples are obtained exactly, by the same correction applied to unconstrained draws. Under this structure, global boundedness for all initial conditions and bounded inputs reduces to a linear matrix condition on the symmetric part of the linear operator. The simulation test is then replaced by a probabilistic stability certificate: the posterior probability that the ROM is globally bounded, estimated with exact confidence bounds; the posterior restricted to certified models is then sampled exactly by rejection. For energy-conserving systems, the linear part can be constrained to be skew-symmetric as well: every draw then grows at most linearly in time, and conserves energy exactly when unforced.
  On a forced viscous Burgers' equation, the Korteweg-de Vries equation and a two-dimensional viscous Burgers' equation, every sample of the constrained posterior integrates to a bounded trajectory, where up to all unconstrained draws diverge, and beyond the observation window the former is also the more accurate of the two.

papers.title: Tackling Many-Body Coulomb Singularity by Randomization
papers.abstract: Many-body Coulomb dynamics is central to quantum chemistry and molecular simulation, yet the Coulomb singularity undermines both the standard error analysis and performance of product formulas. Even for the simple hydrogen ground state, the celebrated Trotter formulas converge more slowly than their nominal order, and going to higher order does not help. Randomization by itself does not resolve this. We show that conventional qDRIFT suffers the same loss of accuracy, and that for general initial states, the errors of both Trotter formulas and qDRIFT can decrease more slowly than any power of the number of time steps (logarithmically). To overcome these limitations, we introduce supersmoothing qDRIFT, a randomized product formula that turns a physical property of free particle propagation into an algorithmic resource. Our algorithm achieves an error bound that decreases linearly with the time step, uniformly over \textit{all} initial states and without any smoothness or energy assumptions. Combined with spatial discretization analysis, the resulting end-to-end gate count improves on those of qubitization and high-order Trotter formulas applied directly to the discretized Hamiltonian, despite first-order convergence in time. This work demonstrates new ways of utilizing continuum dynamics to achieve algorithmic advantage.

papers.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
papers.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
papers.authors: Zhiyu Yan, Shiao Liu, Rahul Mahajan, Anand Viswanathan, Christopher D. Anderson, Rui Duan
papers.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components, improves as more sites contribute summaries, and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across a range of data settings. Applied to real-world multi-facility EHR data for stroke patients, the method learns interpretable patient representations that highlight clinically distinct subgroups and could help inform subgroup-specific care.

papers.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
papers.authors: Aryan Gadhave, Asghar Ghorbanpour, Liam Hickey, Masoud Khalkhali, Allison Klingler, Nathan Pagliaroli, Andrew Parks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

papers.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
papers.authors: Mayank Goswami, Vasilis Livanos, Pasin Manurangsi, Arturo Merino, GiBeom Park, Adarsh Srinivasan
papers.abstract:
We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter.
  We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $\Theta(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid.
  A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

papers.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
papers.authors: Dominik Pabst, Michael A. Klatt, Klaus Mecke
papers.abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

papers.title: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
papers.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

papers.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
papers.authors: Artin Tajdini, Jasper C. H. Lee, Jonathan Scarlett, Kevin Jamieson
papers.abstract:
We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $\alpha$-moment $\nu$ for some unknown $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $\alpha$ or $\nu$, we have with probability at least $1-\delta$ that $ \|\widehat\theta-\theta^*\|_\Sigma
  \lesssim_\alpha
  \nu^{1/\alpha}
  \big(\frac{d+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\big)^{\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $\Sigma$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_\Sigma:=(v^\top\Sigma v)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $\alpha$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $\alpha$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

papers.title: $L^p-L^q$ estimates for maximal operators associated to families of finite type curves
papers.abstract: We investigate the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) boundedness of maximal operators associated with averages over families of finite-type curves in the plane. These operators are defined by \[ \mathbb{M}f(x):=\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2} \left|\int_{\mathbb{C}}f(x-ty)\rho(y)\,d\sigma(y)\right|, \] where \(d\sigma\) denotes the normalized Lebesgue measure on the curve \(\mathbb{C}\), and \(\rho\) is a smooth cutoff function. Let \(\triangle\) denote the closed triangle with vertices \[ P=\left(\frac25,\frac15\right),\qquad Q=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right),\qquad R=(0,0). \] We establish that, whenever \[ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right) \in \bigl(\triangle\setminus\{P,Q\}\bigr) \cap \left\{ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right): \frac1p<\frac2q,\quad p>\frac{(m+1)q}{q+1} \right\}, \] there exists a constant \(B>0\) such that \[ \|\mathbb{M}f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^2)} \leq B\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)}. \] As an application, we derive \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) estimates for solutions of higher-order strictly hyperbolic pseudodifferential equations.

papers.title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
papers.abstract: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $\Delta_\xi$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.

papers.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
papers.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls.
