These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.

papers.title: Lofty Models of Peano Arithmetic
papers.abstract: If M is a nonstandard model of Peano Arithmetic, then M is lofty iff M has a simple elementary extension that is recursively saturated. This had previously been known for countable M.

papers.title: Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
papers.abstract:
We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results.
  First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a<1/2, and on position space balls for a<1. For a set of N of full density and for Hecke eigenbases, almost all eigenstates, and even all of them, are equidistributed at polynomial scales.
  Second, every invariant probability measure is the semiclassical measure of quasimodes of order 1/log N, one for each N, that are not equidistributed at any scale between 4N^(-1/8) and a prescribed scale tending to zero.
  Third, there are orthonormal bases of quasimodes of order 1/log N for every N, and eigenbases for N with short periods, in which a full density subset is equidistributed at every fixed scale, but not at the scales (log N)^(-a) for a>1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.

papers.title: A Certified Reduced Basis Method for Linear Parametrized Parabolic Optimal Control Problems in Space-Time Formulation
papers.authors: Maria Strazzullo, Francesco Ballarin, Gianluigi Rozza
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose to efficiently solve time dependent parametrized optimal control problems governed by parabolic partial differential equations through the certified reduced basis method. In particular, we will exploit an error estimator procedure, based on easy-to-compute quantities which guarantees a rigorous and efficient bound for the error of the involved variables. First, we propose analyzing the problem at hand, proving its well-posedness thanks to Ne\v cas - Babu\v ska theory in a space-time formulation. Then, we derive error estimators to apply a Greedy method during the offline stage, to perform, during the online stage, a Galerkin projection onto a low-dimensional space spanned by properly chosen high-fidelity solutions. We tested the error estimators on two model problems governed by a Graetz flow with physical and geometrical parametrization. The results have been compared to a previously proposed bound, based on the exact computation of the Babu\v ska inf-sup constant, in terms of reliability and computational costs. We remark that our findings still hold in the steady setting, and we also propose a brief insight for this simpler formulation.

papers.title: Harmonic mean closed vector lattices
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the harmonic mean on certain Archimedean vector lattices, which we call harmonic mean closed. Using this concept, we provide a new characterization of positive orthogonally additive polynomials from a harmonic mean closed Archimedean vector lattice to a uniformly complete Archimedean vector lattice space entirely in terms of harmonic means. This result yields polynomial versions of the QM-AM-GM-HM inequalities on Archimedean vector lattices where the only additional requirement on the domain space is that it is harmonic mean closed.

papers.title: The homotopy types of $Sp(n)$-gauge groups over $S^{4m}$
papers.abstract: Let $m$ and $n$ be two positive integers such that $m < n$. Denote by $P_{n,k}$ the principal $Sp(n)$-bundle over $S^{4m}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ be the gauge group of $P_{n,k}$ classified by $k\varepsilon'$, where $\varepsilon'$ is a generator of $\pi_{4m}(B(Sp(n)))\cong\mathbb{Z}$. In this article, we will partially classify the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ by giving a lower bound for the number of homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$. Also, in special cases $Sp(3)$-gauge groups over $S^8$ and $Sp(4)$-gauge groups over $S^{12}$ we give an upper bound for the number of homotopy types of these gauge groups.

papers.title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente \`a la formule des traces en caract\'eristique p>0
papers.abstract: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.

papers.title: Structure theorem for cofibrant tame functors indexed by posets of dimension 1
papers.authors: Wojciech Chach\'olski, Barbara Giunti, Claudia Landi, Francesca Tombari
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss certain circumstances in which the category of tame functors inherits an abelian category structure with minimal resolutions and a model category structure with minimal cofibrant replacements. We also present a structure theorem for cofibrant objects in the category of tame functors indexed by realizations of posets of dimension 1 with values in the category of chain complexes in an abelian category whose all objects are projectives. Moreover, we introduce a general technique to generate indecomposable objects in the abelian category of functors indexed by finite posets.

papers.title: Monodromy groups of Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication
papers.authors: Victoria Cantoral-Farf\'an, Davide Lombardo, John Voight
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field. The connected monodromy field of $A$ is the minimal field over which the images of all the $\ell$-adic torsion representations have connected Zariski closure. We show that for all even $g \geq 4$, there exist infinitely many geometrically nonisogenous abelian varieties $A$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of dimension $g$ where the connected monodromy field is strictly larger than the field of definition of the endomorphisms of $A$. Our construction arises from explicit families of hyperelliptic Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication.

papers.title: Fitting height and lengths of laws in finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a finite solvable group, and let h(G) denote its Fitting height, namely the length of a shortest normal series in G with nilpotent factors. We show, that h(G)/5 is a lower bound for the length of any law in G. It follows, that the cardinality of G is bounded from below by an exponential function of h(G). The proof is accomplished by showing an interesting result about the behaviour of non-trivial reduced words in permutation actions of finite solvable groups.

papers.title: Euler characteristics and moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions
papers.abstract: Fujiki--Oka resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities of type $\frac{1}{r}(1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)$ are constructed using multidimensional continued fractions. In this paper, we compute the Euler characteristics of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in arbitrary dimension using the heights of the coefficients of the associated remainder polynomials. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in dimension three.

papers.title: Categorical concentration
papers.abstract: Given a torus action on a compact space $X$, a fundamental result of Borel and Atiyah-Segal asserts that the equivariant cohomology of $X$ is concentrated in the fixed locus $X^T$, up to inverting enough Chern classes. For algebraic varieties and stacks over an arbitrary field, we prove an analogous concentration statement for equivariant derived categories of sheaves. On the localized categories, restriction to the fixed locus coincides with Braden's hyperbolic localization, and as an application we obtain torus localization for the Donaldson-Thomas perverse sheaves of (-1)-shifted symplectic spaces. Concentration holds more generally for actions of affine algebraic groups, and for abstract six functor formalisms (e.g. motivic sheaves). For $\mu_\ell$-actions, it recovers Treumann's sheaf-theoretic Smith theory. We also prove a categorification of the virtual localization formula for torus actions.

papers.title: Associativity conditions for linear quasigroups and equivalence relations on binary trees
papers.abstract: We characterise the bracketing identities satisfied by linear quasigroups with the help of certain equivalence relations on binary trees that are based on the left and right depths of the leaves modulo some integers. The numbers of equivalence classes of $n$-leaf binary trees are variants of the Catalan numbers, and they form the associative spectrum (a kind of measure of non-associativity) of a quasigroup. Every group-based equivalence relation arising here can be replaced by one defined by an abelian group generated by at most two elements. The fine associative spectra form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of rank-two subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with an additional least element. This classifies the equivalence relations completely; closed formulas for all their numbers of classes remain open.

papers.title: Odd Fredholm modules over differential graded algebras: Chern character and spectral flow
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a locally convex differential graded algebra. For $q \in \mathbb{N}_0$ we construct the Chern character of $\vartheta$-summable $\mathcal{C}_q$-Fredholm modules over $\Omega$, an entire cyclic cocycle which extends the JLO cocycle to the differential graded setting. For $q = 0$ it is the Chern character of even $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $\Omega$ due to G\"uneysu and Ludewig; for $q = 1$ it yields a Chern character for odd $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $\Omega$, which reduces to Getzler's odd Chern character for $\Omega$ trivially graded with trivial differential. We prove that this cocycle is Chen normalized and invariant under homotopies. Moreover, we generalize the constructions by Cacciatori and G\"uneysu to arbitrary $\Omega$ and $g \in \mathrm{GL}_m(\Omega^0)$ to get an odd chain $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ and prove the following odd index theorem: the pairing of the odd Chern character with $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ may be written as an explicit integral formula which equals $\sqrt{\pi}$ times the spectral flow from $Q$ to $\mathbf{c}(g)^{-1} Q \mathbf{c}(g)$ whenever $\mathbf{c}(g)$ is unitary. For odd-dimensional spin manifolds (where $\mathbf{c}$ is Clifford multiplication) this supplies the cochain side of the loop space approach to the odd-index theorem.

papers.title: Pseudo-random Instance Generators in C++ for Deterministic and Stochastic Multi-commodity Network Design Problems
papers.authors: Eric Larsen, Serge Bisaillon, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Cordeau, Emma Frejinger
papers.abstract: Network design problems constitute an important family of combinatorial optimization problems for which many exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed over the last few decades. Two central problems in this family are the multi-commodity, capacitated, fixed charge network design problem (MCFNDP) and its stochastic counterpart, the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP with recourse. These are standard problems that often serve as workbenches for devising and testing models and algorithms in stylized but near-realistic settings. Progress on solution methods requires instances of varying size, structure and difficulty. We present two open-source C++ generators. The deterministic generator modernizes and extends the generator underlying the Canad instances, with new topologies and continuous control of capacity tightness and cost structure. The stochastic generator, which is to our knowledge the first publicly available one for the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP, builds scenarios that match user-specified moments and correlations. We also release libraries of configurations for 6,000 deterministic and 416 stochastic instances, as well as the base instances and configurations of 20 stochastic instances on hub-and-spoke benchmark networks. The generators aim to support systematic and reproducible experimentation, including the training and out-of-sample evaluation of learning-based and stochastic programming methods.

papers.title: Quotients of Leavitt path algebras over commutative rings by graded ideals
papers.authors: Sevgi Harman, M\"uge Kanuni, Guillermo Vera de Salas
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a graph and $R$ a unital commutative ring. We study quotients of the Leavitt path algebra $L_R(E)$ by graded ideals which, unlike in the case of field coefficients, need not be basic. Using the saturated functions of Rigby and van den Hove, we introduce $I$-basic graded ideals, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$, and we prove that, for an arbitrary graph $E$, the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by an $I$-basic graded ideal is isomorphic to the Leavitt path algebra of a quotient graph of $E$ with coefficients in $R/I$. More precisely, for every graded ideal there is a canonical epimorphism from such an algebra onto the quotient, and it is an isomorphism if and only if the graded ideal is $I$-basic. This extends a result of Larki for basic graded ideals. We also introduce graded ideal functions, defined on the vertices of $E$ and on the pairs $(H,v)$ formed by a hereditary saturated set $H$ and a breaking vertex $v$ of $H$, and we show that they form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of graded ideals of $L_R(E)$. As an application, for a finite graph $E$ in which no cycle has an exit, we describe the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by any graded ideal as a direct sum, indexed by the sinks and the cycles of $E$, of Leavitt path algebras over quotient rings of $R$, namely matrix algebras over quotient rings of $R$ and of $R[x,x^{-1}]$. Finally, examples on the infinite binary tree and Toeplitz graph show that the hypothesis on the finiteness and cycles cannot be removed.

papers.title: Critical-Point Characterization of Rank-Constrained Optimization and Global Convergence of Projected Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: We study the rank-constrained problem $\min_{\mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{X})\leq r} f(\mathbf{X})$ when the unconstrained minimizer $\mathbf{X}_*$ has rank $r_*\leq r$. We apply a sharp matrix inequality to characterize critical points and establish deterministic global linear convergence of projected gradient descent (ProjGD). First, assuming that $f$ satisfies rank-$(r+r_*)$ restricted smoothness and strong convexity with constants $L$ and $\mu$, respectively, where $0<\mu<L$, we show that every nonoptimal rank-$r$ critical point satisfies the inequality $\|P_{T(\mathbf{X})^\perp}\nabla f(\mathbf{X})\|/\sigma_r(\mathbf{X}) \geq (2L\mu/(L-\mu))\sqrt{r/r_*}$. Here $P_{T(\mathbf{X})^\perp}\nabla f(\mathbf{X})$ is the component of the gradient normal to the tangent space $T(\mathbf{X})$ and $\sigma_r(\mathbf{X})$ is the $r$-th singular value of $\mathbf{X}$. Second, this inequality implies that $\mathbf{X}_*$ is the unique fixed point of ProjGD whenever the step size $\eta$ satisfies $\eta>\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-\mu)/(2L\mu)$. Finally, under an additional rank-$2r$ restricted smoothness assumption, we apply the argument to the actual ProjGD iterates, establish a uniform improvement estimate for every iteration, and prove deterministic global linear convergence from every initialization of rank at most $r$ for $\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-\mu)/(2L\mu)<\eta<1/L$. The result allows arbitrary rank overparameterization $r\geq r_*$, and its convergence rate is independent of the singular-value condition number of $\mathbf{X}_*$. As a consequence, a rank-preserving curve argument proves the no-spurious-local-minima property whenever $(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)<(1+\sqrt{r_*/r})^{-1}$. This matches the sharp threshold established by McRae et al. (2026). A quadratic example shows that the lower bound on the step size $\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-\mu)/(2L\mu)$ is also sharp.

papers.title: On the Unipotent $p$-adic Simpson Correspondence
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to show a (derived) $p$-adic Simpson correspondence for (locally) unipotent coefficients on smooth rigid-analytic varieties. Our results depend on a deformation to $\mathbf{B}_\mathtt{dr}^+/\xi^2$, and not on a choice of exponential (as required for more general coefficients). Our methods are higher categorical, hinging on the theory of modules over $\mathbf{E}_\infty$-algebras.

papers.title: A characterization of compactness via bilinear $T1$ theorem
papers.authors: Mingming Cao, Honghai Liu, Zengyan Si, K\^oz\^o Yabuta
papers.abstract:
In this paper we develop the bilinear $T1$ theorem to characterize the (weighted) compactness of bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators. Let $T$ be a bilinear operator associated with a standard bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernel. We prove that $T$ can be extended to a compact bilinear operator from $L^{p_1}(w_1^{p_1}) \times L^{p_2}(w_2^{p_2})$ to $L^p(w^p)$ for all exponents $\frac1p = \frac{1}{p_1} + \frac{1}{p_2}>0$ with $p_1, p_2 \in (1, \infty]$ and for all weights $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(p_1, p_2)}$ if and only if the following hypotheses hold: (H1) $T$ is associated with a compact bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund kernel, (H2) $T$ satisfies the weak compactness property, and (H3) $T(1,1), T^{*1}(1,1), T^{*2}(1,1) \in \mathrm{CMO}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. This is also equivalent to the endpoint compactness: (1) $T$ is compact from $L^1(w_1) \times L^1(w_2)$ to $L^{\frac12, \infty}(w^{\frac12})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(1, 1)}$, or (2) $T$ is compact from $L^{\infty}(w_1^{\infty}) \times L^{\infty}(w_2^{\infty})$ to $\mathrm{CMO}_{\lambda}(w^{\infty})$ for all $(w_1, w_2) \in A_{(\infty, \infty)}$. Besides, any of these properties is equivalent to the fact that $T$ admits a compact bilinear dyadic representation.
  Our main approaches consist of the following new ingredients: (i) a resulting representation of a compact bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operator as an average of some compact bilinear dyadic shifts and paraproducts; (ii) extrapolation of endpoint compactness for bilinear operators; and (iii) compactness criterion in weighted Lorentz spaces. Finally, to illustrate the applicability of our result, we demonstrate the hypotheses (H1)-(H3) through examples including bilinear continuous/dyadic paraproducts, bilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear commutators.

papers.title: The Baire property and precompact duality
papers.authors: M. Ferrer, S. Hern\'andez, I. Sep\'ulveda, F. J. Trigos-Arrieta
papers.abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a totally bounded abelian group \st\ its dual group $\widehat{G}_p$ equipped with the finite-open topology is a Baire group, then every compact subset of $G$ must be finite. This solves an open question by Chasco, Dom\'inguez and Tkachenko. {Among other consequences, we obtain an example of a group that is $g$-dense in its completion but is not $g$-barrelled. This solves a question proposed by Au${\beta}$enhofer and Dikranjan.}

papers.title: Secure Distributed Matrix Multiplication with Precomputation
papers.authors: Ryann Cartor, Rafael G. L. D'Oliveira, Salim El Rouayheb, Daniel Heinlein, David Karpuk, Freeman Slaughter, Alex Sprintson
papers.abstract:
We consider secure distributed matrix multiplication, in which a user computes the product of two matrices with the help of honest-but-curious servers, any $T$ of which may collude. Using the outer-product partition, the matrices are split into $K$ and $L$ blocks and hidden by random masks. Assuming the user has precomputed the products of the random matrices, we develop methods that use this precomputation to reduce the number of servers required.
  Polynomial codes are designed through degree tables, whose distinct entries count the servers. We show that precomputation can reduce the minimum number of servers by designing degree tables specifically for this setting. For Gap Additive Secure Polynomial (GASPr) codes, we give a precise formula and show that it is monotone in the chain length $r$, so only the extremes GASP_small and GASP_big matter. We also prove lower bounds attained by GASP_small in several regimes. Consequently, any fraction of colluding servers below one can be tolerated, compared to the threshold of one half without precomputation, and the order of the total computational complexity decreases when the colluders are a fixed fraction of the servers. We show that no existing construction uses fewer servers than the better of GASP_small and GASP_big once the mask products are precomputed.
  We introduce Gap-Reduced Additive Secure Polynomial (GRASP) codes, which retain a single interval for the mask degrees while selecting the information degrees carefully. For $K = T = 4$ and every $L \geq 3$, we give an explicit GRASP code that uses one fewer server than every GASPr code and is within two servers of optimal. For large $T$, the configuration becomes an integer packing problem independent of $T$, and the number of servers saved by GRASP over GASPr grows quadratically in $K$ and $L$.

papers.title: H(curl)-based approximation of the Stokes problem with slip boundary conditions
papers.authors: Wietse M. Boon, Ralf Hiptmair, Wouter Tonnon, Enrico Zampa
papers.abstract: Reformulating the incompressible Stokes equations with the velocity sought in H(curl) has recently emerged as a promising approach for the design of helicity-preserving schemes in magnetohydrodynamics and pressure-robust finite element methods on polygonal meshes. A key challenge in this setting, however, is the treatment of Navier slip boundary conditions. In this paper, we overcome this difficulty by recasting the slip condition as a Robin boundary condition and proving well-posedness (up to a finite-dimensional kernel) of the resulting continuous problem. We further identify the geometric and regularity assumptions on the domain and the exact solution under which the classical Stokes solution is recovered. Finally, we study a finite element Galerkin discretization, establishing stability and a priori error estimates. Numerical experiments validate the optimal convergence rates predicted by the theory.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
papers.abstract: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.

papers.title: A polytopal discontinuous Galerkin method for the pseudo-stress formulation of the unsteady Stokes problem
papers.authors: Paola F. Antonietti, Michele Botti, Alessandra Cancrini, Ilario Mazzieri
papers.abstract: This work aims to construct and analyze a discontinuous Galerkin method on polytopal grids (PolydG) to solve the pseudo-stress formulation of the unsteady Stokes problem. The pseudo-stress variable is introduced due to the growing interest in non-Newtonian flows and coupled interface problems, where stress assumes a fundamental role. The space-time discretization of the problem is achieved by combining the PolydG approach with the implicit theta-method time integration scheme. For both the semi- and fully-discrete problems we present a detailed stability analysis. Moreover, we derive convergence estimates for the fully discrete space-time discretization. A set of verification tests is presented to verify the theoretical estimates and the application of the method to cases of engineering interest.

papers.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
papers.abstract: The $\lambda$-backbone coloring of a graph $G$ with backbone $H$ is a proper vertex coloring in which the endpoints of every edge from $H$ are assigned colors which differ by at least $\lambda$. In this paper we prove that $BBC_\lambda(G,H)\le\lambda+5$ for every graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $4$ and every connected spanning bipartite backbone $H$, provided that $\lambda\ge3$. A suitable coloring can be found in linear time. The bound is sharp for $\lambda\ge4$, even for spanning tree backbones. The proof combines degree-list coloring with a balanced choice of vertices in an auxiliary bipartite multigraph. We also settle the previously open complexity status for graphs with maximum degree $4$ and connected bipartite backbones, proving NP-completeness even for spanning tree backbones for every fixed $\lambda\ge2$. Furthermore, we obtain an almost complete classification of the complexity of deciding whether $BBC_{\lambda}(G,H)\le k$ for graphs with maximum degree at most $4$ and matching, galaxy, Hamiltonian path, and spanning tree backbones. We also determine the effect of allowing isolated vertices in matching and galaxy backbones.

papers.title: Revisiting Unicity Distance: A Channel Transmission Perspective and Its Limits
papers.abstract: This paper revisits the classical notion of unicity distance for substitution ciphers from an information-theoretic perspective. We frame simple-substitution encryption as a noisy transmission channel, in which the plaintext is the message, the unknown key is the noise, and the attacker is the receiver. Using typical sets to motivate the notion of meaningful plaintexts, we apply the channel coding theorem to blocks encrypted with independent fresh keys. We show that a block length exceeding $H(K)/D$ permits reliable communication at the language's entropy rate using suitably chosen codebooks across many blocks. This provides a channel transmission interpretation of the classical unicity-distance formula. We then test how well this formula describes plaintext recovery when the message is a passage from six known novels. More than $99\%$ of the passages are uniquely identifiable at 18 letters, well before the classical estimate of about 28. N-gram language models, based on the frequencies of short letter sequences, predict the recovery probabilities much more closely. In this experiment, the classical formula misses the recovery transition, while a more detailed model of the language captures it.

papers.title: The K\"ahler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for K\"ahler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete K\"ahler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is K\"ahler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is K\"ahler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.

papers.title: Asymptotic expansions for normal deviations of random walks conditioned to stay positive
papers.authors: Denis Denisov, Alexander Tarasov, Vitali Wachtel
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ having i.i.d. increments with zero mean and finite variance. We continue our study of asymptotic expansions for local probabilities $\mathbf P(S_n=x,\tau_0>n)$, which has been started in \cite{DTW23}. Obtained there expansions make sense in the zone $x=o(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log^{1/2} n})$ only. In the present paper we derive an alternative expansion, which deals with $x$ of order $\sqrt{n}$.

papers.title: New Nonbinary Quantum Codes from Quasi-Twisted Codes with Scalar and Matrix Twists
papers.authors: Tushar Bag, Hai Q Dinh, Daniel Panario
papers.abstract: We construct quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields from one-generator index-$2$ quasi-twisted codes and from codes invariant under a $2\times2$ matrix twist, via the symplectic construction. For one-generator quasi-twisted codes, we give direct proofs of the dimension formulas and of matrix and polynomial tests for symplectic self-orthogonality. When the same scalar twist $\lambda$ acts on both blocks, we show that $\lambda^2\ne1$ gives only quantum distance $1$. Thus, in this construction, distance greater than $1$ requires $\lambda=\pm1$, corresponding to quasi-cyclic and quasi-negacyclic codes. We also study determinant-one $2\times2$ matrix twists. For twists given by companion matrices, we describe the resulting codes and their symplectic duals by polynomials over the base field. When the associated quadratic is irreducible over $\mathbb F_q$, these codes correspond to Hermitian constacyclic codes over the quadratic extension. With a rank criterion for the minimum distance and standard propagation rules, our explicit constructions present quantum codes that improve the recorded minimum-distance lower bounds for $164$ distinct entries in Grassl's tables of quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields.

papers.title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
papers.abstract:
Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types.
  To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.

papers.title: Hardy operators: In the footsteps of Brown, Halmos, and Shields
papers.authors: Eva A. Gallardo-Guttierrez, Jonathan R. Partington, William T. Ross
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the two classical Hardy operators $\mathcal{H}_{1}$ on $L^2(0, 1)$ and $\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$ on $L^2(0, \infty)$ initially studied by Brown, Halmos and Shields. Particular emphasis is given to the construction of explicit cyclic and $*$-cyclic vectors in conjunction with a characterization of their invariant and reducing subspaces. We also provide a complete description of the frame vectors for $I - \mathcal{H}_{1}^{*}$.

papers.title: Performance guarantees for optimization-based state estimation using turnpike properties
papers.authors: Julian D. Schiller, Lars Gr\"une, and Matthias A. M\"uller
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop novel accuracy and performance guarantees for optimal state estimation of general nonlinear systems (in particular, moving horizon estimation, MHE). Our results rely on a turnpike property of the optimal state estimation problem, which essentially states that the omniscient infinite-horizon solution involving all past and future data serves as turnpike for the solutions of finite-horizon estimation problems involving a subset of the data. This leads to the surprising observation that MHE problems naturally exhibit a leaving arc, which may have a strong negative impact on the estimation accuracy. To address this, we propose a delayed MHE scheme, and we show that the resulting performance (both averaged and non-averaged) is approximately optimal and achieves bounded regret with respect to the infinite-horizon solution, with error terms that can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of the delay. In various simulation examples, we observe that already a very small delay in the MHE scheme is sufficient to significantly improve the overall estimation error by 20-25% compared to standard MHE (without delay). This finding is of great importance for practical applications (especially for monitoring, fault detection, and parameter estimation) where a small delay in the estimation is rather irrelevant but may significantly improve the estimation results.

papers.title: Recovery guarantees for compressed sensing photoacoustic tomography
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.

papers.title: Generalized De Bruijn Words, Invertible Necklaces, and the Burrows-Wheeler Transform
papers.abstract: We define generalized de Bruijn words as those words having a Burrows--Wheeler transform that is a concatenation of permutations of the alphabet. We show that generalized de Bruijn words are in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles in the generalized de Bruijn graphs, introduced in the early 1980s in the context of network design. We prove that generalized de Bruijn words retain the asymptotically maximal factor complexity of ordinary de Bruijn words over a fixed alphabet. We then use this class to construct an infinite binary family on which the Burrows--Wheeler transform reduces this complexity from asymptotically maximal to the constant $2$. In particular, this shows that the BWT can substantially improve dictionary compressibility. When the size of the alphabet is a prime $p$, we define invertible necklaces as those whose BWT-matrix is nonsingular. We show that invertible necklaces of length $n$ correspond to normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$, and that they form an abelian group isomorphic to the Reutenauer group $RG_p^n$. Using known results in abstract algebra, we can establish a connection between generalized de Bruijn words and invertible necklaces. In particular, we highlight a correspondence between binary de Bruijn words of order $d+1$, binary necklaces of length $2^{d}$ having an odd number of $1$'s, invertible BWT matrices of size $2^{d}\times 2^{d}$, and normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2^{d}}}$.

papers.title: Strichartz estimates for the half Klein-Gordon equation on asymptotically flat backgrounds and applications to cubic Dirac equations
papers.abstract:
The aim of this paper is to establish the $L^2_t$-endpoint Strichartz estimate for (half) Klein-Gordon equations on a weakly asymptotically flat space-time. As an application we prove small data global well-posedness and scattering for massive cubic Dirac equations in the full subcritical range in this setting.
  Crucial ingredient is a parametrix contruction following the work of Metcalfe-Tataru and Xue and complements Strichartz estimates obtained by Zheng-Zhang. The proof of the global result for the cubic Dirac equation follows the strategy developed by Machihara-Nakanishi-Ozawa in the Euclidean setting.

papers.title: On coarse tree decompositions and coarse balanced separators
papers.authors: Tara Abrishami, Jadwiga Czy\.zewska, Kacper Kluk, Marcin Pilipczuk, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski

papers.title: Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient Methods for Stochastic Composite Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose {\sf ALFPG}, an Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient framework for stochastic composite nonconvex minimization. It adapts stepsizes from the optimization trajectory without requiring smoothness constants or line search. For finite-sum problems, {\sf ALFPG-FS} combines coordinate-wise stepsizes, Nesterov extrapolation, and a SPIDER estimator; {\sf ALFPG-D} is its full-batch specialization. Under component-wise smoothness, bounded sublevel sets, and separate lower bounds on $f$ and $h$, {\sf ALFPG-FS} achieves expected $\epsilon$-stationarity with $\mathcal O(N+\sqrt N \epsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations. For expectation problems, we develop {\sf ALFPG-MVR1} and {\sf ALFPG-MVR2} (MVR: Momentum-based Variance Reduction). Both use one fresh sample per iteration. MVR1 uses one stochastic-gradient evaluation; MVR2 uses at most two evaluations at different points with the same sample. MVR1 requires smoothness of the expected loss; MVR2 additionally requires uniformly smooth sample losses. When the regularizer is convex or Lipschitz continuous on its effective domain and stochastic gradients are almost surely bounded, both methods achieve expected $\epsilon$-stationarity using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sigma^2\epsilon^{-4}+\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sigma\epsilon^{-3}+\epsilon^{-2})$ stochastic-gradient evaluations, respectively. Here, $N$ is the number of component functions, $\sigma^2$ bounds the gradient noise variance, and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ hides polylogarithmic factors. Neither expectation variant requires prior knowledge of $\sigma$, and both recover $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ complexity in the zero-noise regime. Numerical experiments on sparse phase retrieval, linear eigenvalue problems, and neural network regression show that all four ALFPG variants generally outperform state-of-the-art proximal-gradient baselines.

papers.title: Positionality of Dumont--Thomas numeration systems for integers
papers.authors: Savinien Kreczman, S\'ebastien Labb\'e, Manon Stipulanti
papers.abstract: Introduced in 2001 by Lecomte and Rigo, abstract numeration systems provide a way of expressing natural numbers with words from a language $L$ accepted by a finite automaton. As it turns out, these numeration systems are not necessarily positional, i.e., we cannot always find a sequence $U=(U_i)_{i\ge 0}$ of integers such that the value of every word in the language $L$ is determined by the position of its letters and the first few values of $U$. Finding the conditions under which an abstract numeration system is positional seems difficult in general. In this paper, we thus consider this question for a particular sub-family of abstract numeration systems called Dumont--Thomas numeration systems. They are derived from substitutions and were introduced in 1989 by Dumont and Thomas. We exhibit conditions on the underlying substitution so that the corresponding Dumont--Thomas numeration is positional. We first work in the most general setting, then particularize our results to some practical cases. Finally, we link our numeration systems to existing literature, notably properties studied by R\'{e}nyi in 1957, Parry in 1960, Bertrand-Mathis in 1989, and Fabre in 1995.

papers.title: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.

papers.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
papers.authors: Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda
papers.abstract: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.

papers.title: Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras
papers.abstract:
Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes, which divides the non-associ\-ative parts into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Malcev's identity and categorise non-associative loops. Analysing the non-associativity structure of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras uncovers octonion and three quasi-octonion, power-associative subalgebras. Power-associativity is proved to grow by multiples of seven that introduce zero divisors in factors of 84 for all Cayley-Dickson algebras. It is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with ultracomplex numbers to capture the fact that sedenions and all higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras contain quasi-octonions that are ultracomplex. The non-associative types reduce the 84 zero divisors in sedenions via three cycles and four modes down to seven primary zero divisor pairs of two-term sums of basis elements providing new techniques to analyse the seven quasi-octonions loops in sedenions. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven quasi-octonion subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation.
  The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are described showing 180 zero divisors and the other split algebra is analogous to sedenions with 84 zero divisors. These split algebras are shown to involve quasi-octonion algebras with mixed signature.

papers.title: Stable Nonlinear Dynamical Approximation with Dynamical Sampling
papers.authors: Daan Bon, Benjamin Caris, Olga Mula
papers.abstract: We present a nonlinear dynamical approximation method for time-dependent Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). The approach makes use of parametrized decoder functions, and provides a general, and principled way of understanding and analyzing stability and accuracy of nonlinear dynamical approximations. The parameters of these functions are evolved in time by means of projections on finite dimensional subspaces of an ambient Hilbert space related to the PDE evolution. For practical computations of these projections, one usually needs to sample. We propose a dynamical sampling strategy which comes with stability guarantees, while keeping a low numerical complexity. We show the effectiveness of the method on several examples in moderate spatial dimension.

papers.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
papers.abstract: We construct a short-time parametrix for the exterior Dirichlet wave equation on the complement of a solid torus. The construction involves freezing one coefficient of the conjugated Laplacian. This results in a family of radial P\"oschl--Teller equations. We bound the $L^2$ error in terms of the energy of the initial data. We then give several examples of Gaussian wavepackets in toroidal coordinates.

papers.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.

papers.title: The empirical discrete copula process
papers.authors: Gery Geenens, Ivan Kojadinovic, Tommaso Martini
papers.abstract: This paper develops a general inferential framework for discrete copulas on finite supports in any dimension. The copula of a multivariate discrete distribution is defined as Csiszar's I-projection (i.e., the minimum-Kullback-Leibler divergence projection) of its joint probability array onto the polytope of uniform-margins probability arrays of the same size, and its empirical estimator is obtained by applying that same projection to the array of empirical frequencies observed on the sample. Under the assumption of random sampling, strong consistency and $\sqrt{n}$-asymptotic normality of the empirical copula array is established. The theory is illustrated by deriving the large-sample distribution of Yule's concordance coefficient (the natural analogue of Spearman's $\rho$ for bivariate discrete distributions) and by constructing a test for quasi-independence in multivariate contingency tables.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of Distributed Simple Binary Hypothesis Testing under Information Constraints
papers.authors: Hadi Kazemi, Ankit Pensia, Varun Jog
papers.abstract: This paper resolves two open problems from a recent paper, arXiv:2403.16981, concerning the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing under information constraints. The first open problem asks whether interaction reduces the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing. In this paper, we show that sequential interaction does not help. The second problem suggests tightening existing sample complexity bounds for communication-constrained simple binary hypothesis testing. We derive optimally tight bounds for this setting and resolve this problem. Our main technical contributions are: (i) a one-shot lower bound on the Bayes error in simple binary hypothesis testing that satisfies a crucial tensorisation property; (ii) a streamlined proof of the formula for the sample complexity of simple binary hypothesis testing without constraints, first established in arXiv:2403.16981; and (iii) a reverse data-processing inequality for Hellinger-$\lambda$ divergences, generalising the results from arXiv:1812.03031 and arXiv:2206.02765.

papers.title: A residual driven multiscale method for Darcy's flow in perforated domains
papers.authors: Wei Xie, Shubin Fu, Yin Yang, Yunqing Huang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a residual-driven multiscale method for simulating Darcy flow in perforated domains, where complex geometries and highly heterogeneous permeability make direct simulations computationally expensive. To address this, we introduce a velocity elimination technique that reformulates the mixed velocity-pressure system into a pressure-only formulation, significantly reducing complexity by focusing on the dominant pressure variable. Our method is developed within the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (GMsFEM) framework. For each coarse block, we construct offline basis functions from local spectral problems that capture key geometric and physical features. Online basis functions are then adaptively enriched using residuals, allowing the method to incorporate global effects such as source terms and boundary conditions, thereby improving accuracy. We provide detailed error analysis demonstrating how the offline and online spaces contribute to the accuracy and efficiency of the solution. Numerical experiments confirm the method's effectiveness, showing substantial reductions in computational cost while maintaining high accuracy, particularly through adaptive online enrichment. These results highlight the method's potential for efficient and accurate simulation of Darcy flow in complex, heterogeneous perforated domains.

papers.title: Tangent Lie Algebras of Automorphism Groups of Free Algebras
papers.abstract: We study an analogue of the Andreadakis-Johnson filtration for automorphism groups of free algebras and introduce the notion of tangent Lie algebras for certain automorphism groups, defined as subalgebras of the Lie algebra of derivations. We show that, for many classical varieties of algebras, the tangent Lie algebra is contained in the Lie algebra of derivations with constant divergence. We also introduce the concepts of approximately tame and absolutely wild automorphisms of free algebras in arbitrary varieties and employ tangent Lie algebras to investigate their properties. It is shown that nearly all known examples of wild automorphisms of free algebras are absolutely wild -- with the notable exceptions of the Nagata and Anick automorphisms. We show that the Bergman automorphism of free matrix algebras of order two is absolutely wild. Furthermore, we prove that free algebras in any variety of polynilpotent Lie algebras -- except for the abelian and metabelian varieties -- also possess absolutely wild automorphisms.

papers.title: An introduction to the symmetric group algebra
papers.abstract:
This is an introduction to the group algebras of the symmetric groups, written for a quarter-long graduate course. After recalling the definition of group algebras (and monoid algebras) in general, as well as basic properties of permutations, we introduce several families of elements in the symmetric group algebras $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ such as the Young--Jucys--Murphy elements, the (sign-)integrals and the conjugacy class sums. Then comes a chapter on group actions and representations in general, followed by the core of this text: a study of the representations of symmetric groups (i.e., of left $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$-modules), including the classical theory of Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers. We prove in detail the main facts including the characterization of irreducible representations (in characteristic $0$), the Garnir relations, the standard basis theorem, the description of duals of Specht modules, and the hook length formula, as well as a number of less known results. Finally, we describe several bases of $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ that arise from the study of Specht modules, including the Murphy cellular bases.
  The methods used are elementary and computational. We aim to assume as little as possible of the base ring $\mathbf{k}$, and to use as little as possible from representation theory (nothing more advanced than Maschke and Jordan--H\"older).
  Over 100 exercises (without solutions) are scattered through the text.

papers.title: Irreducible representations of pointed Hopf algebras of type $A_2$
papers.authors: Agust\'in Garc\'ia Iglesias, Alfio Antonio Rodriguez
papers.abstract: We classify the irreducible representations of a family of finite-dimensional pointed liftings $H_\lambda$ of the Nichols algebra associated with the diagram $A_2$ with parameter $q=-1$. We show that these algebras have infinite representation type and construct an indecomposable $H_\lambda$-module of dimension $n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Finally, we study a semisimple category $\underline{\operatorname{Rep}} H_\lambda$ arising as a quotient of $\operatorname{Rep} H_\lambda$.

papers.title: Solvable points on intersections of quadrics, cubics, and quartics
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not 2 or 3. We establish polynomial bounds on the ambient dimension $N$, such that if $N$ is at least as big as this bound, every intersection $X\subset\mathbb{P}^N$ of quadrics, cubics and quartics has a solvable point, and a general one has a dense collection of solvable points, i.e. points in $X(k^{\mathrm{Sol}})$ where $k^{\mathrm{Sol}}/k$ is a solvable closure. Our method connects the classical theory of polar hypersurfaces to Fano varieties $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$ of linear subspaces on $X$, and we use this to obtain improved control on the arithmetic of $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$

papers.title: Weighted Kernel Functions on Planar Domains
papers.abstract: We study the variation of weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels on planar domains with respect to the weight and establish a Ramadanov-type convergence theorem. As a consequence, we obtain detailed information on the behaviour of the zeros of the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels for weights close to the constant function $1$ on the boundary. We also study the weighted Ahlfors map and strengthen known results concerning its boundary behaviour. Explicit examples of the weighted kernels are presented for certain classes of weights. We strengthen Nehari's construction of the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels by showing that the meromorphic function associated with the weight can be chosen holomorphic. We further identify his auxiliary kernels with reproducing kernels of finite-codimensional Hardy subspaces, and derive further representation formulas and consequences. Finally, we discuss the weighted Carath\'{e}odory metric, and describe relations between the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels with certain classical kernel functions.

papers.title: Contractive kinetic Langevin samplers beyond global Lipschitz continuity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we examine the problem of sampling from log-concave distributions with (possibly) superlinear gradient growth under kinetic (underdamped) Langevin algorithms. Using a carefully tailored taming scheme, we propose two novel discretizations of the kinetic Langevin SDE, the tamed exponential euler scheme and tamed OBABO and we show that they are both contractive and satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality. Building on this, we establish a series of non-asymptotic bounds in $2$-Wasserstein and total variation distance between the law reached by each algorithm and the underlying target measure. In particular, we show that both algorithms can reach almost optimal $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1})$ convergence rate in Wasserstein and Total Variation distances, and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-\frac{1}{2}})$ under increased Hessian local regularity for the tamed OBABO scheme.

papers.title: Parity in vector balancing and reverse Littlewood--Offord problems
papers.abstract:
We consider the probability that the random signed sum $\xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n$ lies within a given distance $r$ of the origin, where $v_1,\dotsc,v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are fixed unit vectors and $\xi_1,\dotsc,\xi_n$ are independently and uniformly distributed on $\{-1,+1\}$. We demonstrate that, for certain values of $r$, the infimum of this probability is sensitive to the parity of $n$.
  We prove that, for any $d\geq 3$, there is some $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(d) > 0$ such that for any $n \not\equiv d \mod 2$ and unit vectors $v_1,\dotsc,v_n\in \mathbb{R}^d$, there are signs $\eta_1,\dotsc,\eta_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $\|\sum_{i=1}^n \eta_i v_i\| \leq \sqrt{d - \varepsilon}$. In other words, $\mathbb{P}(\| \xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n \| \leq \sqrt{d-\varepsilon}) > 0$. This is in contrast to the case of $n\equiv d \mod 2$, in which this probability can be zero. In the case of $d=2$ and odd $n$, we give a construction demonstrating that $\mathbb{P}(\|\xi_1 v_1 + \dotsb + \xi_n v_n\| \leq 1)$ can decay exponentially as $n$ increases, improving on the previous best-known bound of $O(n^{-3/2})$.

papers.title: Don't Look Back in Anger: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization with Nonstationary Data
papers.authors: Dominic S. T. Keehan, Edward J. Anderson, Wolfram Wiesemann
papers.abstract: We study data-driven decision problems where historical observations are generated by a time-evolving distribution whose change over time is bounded in Wasserstein distance. We address this nonstationarity using a distributionally robust optimization model with an ambiguity set that is a Wasserstein ball centered at a weighted empirical distribution, thereby allowing for the time decay of past data in a way which accounts for the drift of the data-generating distribution. Our main technical contribution is a concentration bound for weighted empirical distributions that explicitly captures both the effective sample size (i.e., the equivalent number of equally weighted observations) and the distributional drift. Using our concentration bound, we select observation weights that optimally balance the effective sample size against the distributional drift of the data-generating process, taking into account the order of the Wasserstein ball. We also consider simple weighting schemes, and find that across a wide range of problem settings, a triangular weighting scheme is an effective choice that outperforms the classical weighting schemes of time windowing and simple exponential smoothing. Numerical experiments on a multi-item newsvendor problem illustrate the benefits of our approach.

papers.title: New Best-Known Max-Cut Solution for the G63 Instance in the G-Set Benchmark
papers.abstract: For over two decades, the G-set benchmark has remained a cornerstone challenge for combinatorial optimization solvers. Remarkably, it continues to yield new best-known solutions even to the present day. Here, we report a new best-known Max-Cut of 27,047 for the 7000-node G63 instance-one of the two instances in the benchmark with the largest number of edges. This result is achieved using an optimized Population Annealing Monte Carlo framework, augmented with adaptive control of stochasticity and the periodic introduction of non-local moves, and accelerated on a GPU platform.

papers.title: Attractors of sequences coding $\beta$-integers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we describe minimal string attractors of prefixes of simple Parry sequences. These sequences form a coding of distances between consecutive $\beta$-integers in numeration systems with a real base $\beta$. Simple Parry sequences have been recently studied from this point of view and attractors of prefixes have been described. However, the authors themselves had doubts about their minimality and conjectured that attractors of alphabet size should be sufficient. We confirm their conjecture. Moreover, we provide minimal attractors of prefixes of some particular form of binary non-simple Parry sequences.

papers.title: Regularity for a strongly degenerate equation with explicit $u$-dependence
Lie Algebra Decomposition Classes for Reductive Algebraic Groups in Arbitrary Characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the decomposition classes of the Lie algebras of connected reductive algebraic groups, over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We extend some results proved previously under restrictions on the characteristic, including a formula for the dimension of a decomposition class, and introduce Levi-type decomposition classes to account for some of the difficulties encountered in bad characteristic. We also establish properties of Lusztig--Spaltenstein induction of non-nilpotent orbits, such as parabolic independence, extending the known results for nilpotent orbits. Finally, we determine the covering relation for the closure order on decomposition classes, in the case of good characteristic.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis of 2D Stochastic Navier--Stokes Equations with Transport Noise: Regularity and Spatial Semidiscretization
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a strong convergence rate for the spatial finite element discretization of a two-dimensional stochastic Navier--Stokes system with transport noise and no-slip boundary conditions on a convex polygonal domain. The main challenge arises from the lack of spatial $D(A)$-regularity of the solutio (where $A$ is the Stokes operator), which prevents the direct applicability of standard error analysis techniques. Under a smallness assumption on the transport noise, for a MINI-element spatial semidiscretization, we establish a strong convergence rate of order $h^{\varrho} \log\big(1 + \frac{1}{h}\big)$, where $\varrho \in (0,1/2)$.

papers.title: Solution concepts for a model of visco-elasto-plasticity with slight compressibility
papers.abstract: We study a model for the deformation of a visco-elasto-plastic material that is nearly incompressible. It originates from geophysics, is given in the Eulerian description and combines a Kelvin-Voigt rheology in the spherical part with a Jeffreys-type rheology in the deviatoric part. Despite a constant density, the model allows for non-isochoric deformation and the propagation of pressure waves. An additive decomposition of the strain rate into elastic and inelastic parts leads to an evolution equation for the small elastic strain, which is coupled with an adapted momentum equation. As plasticity is modeled through a non-smooth dissipation potential, we introduce a weak formulation in terms of a variational inequality. Since the well-posedness in such a weak setting is out of reach, we study two possible modifications: the regularization in terms of stress diffusion, and the relaxation of the solvability concept by transition to energy-variational solutions. In both cases, solutions are constructed by the same time-discrete scheme, consisting of solving a saddle-point problem in each time step.

papers.title: The Ultra-Radical: Analytic Continuation, Branching, and Stability of the Principal Branch
papers.abstract: We study the ultra-radical $\sqrt[{n;a;b}]{x}$, the multi-valued solution to $y^{a}=1+a x y^{b}$. Inside the convergence radius $|x|<R$, every branch is given by a Master-J power series; for $|x|\ge R$, analytic continuation requires switching to one of two conjugate series. We introduce a deterministic geometric criterion that selects, for each branch index $n$, the correct conjugate series, thereby eliminating heuristic search and guaranteeing branch continuity across $|x|=R$. Key finding: Only the principal branch ($n=0$) remains continuous when the parameters $a$, $b$, and $x$ vary smoothly. This includes the critical limits $a\to0$ (transition to an exponential equation) and $b\to0$ (transition to a binomial root), where the principal branch converges to the corresponding classical solution. In contrast, branches with $n\neq0$ exhibit oscillatory divergence as $a\to0$ and lose their identity in these limits. This structural continuity singles out the principal branch for applications where parameters may vary with the system's state, such as in nonlinear media with field-dependent exponents or adaptive dynamical systems.

papers.title: Chromatic numbers from edge ideals: Graph classes with vanishing syzygies are polynomially $\chi$-bounded
papers.abstract:
The chromatic number $\chi$ of a graph is bounded from below by its clique number $\omega,$ but the gap between these two values can be arbitrary large. Perfect graphs are defined by the condition that $\chi=\omega$ for all induced subgraphs. An interesting relaxation are $\chi$-bounded graph classes, where $\chi\leq f(\omega)$ for some suitable function $f.$ It is not always possible to achieve this with a polynomial $f.$
  The edge ideal $I_G$ of a graph $G$ is generated by monomials $x_ux_v$ for each edge $uv$ of $G.$ The bi-graded betti numbers $\beta_{i,j}(I)$ are central algebraic geometric invariants. We study the graph classes where for some fixed $i,j$ that syzygy vanishes, that is, $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0.$
  We prove that $\chi\leq f(\omega),$ where $f$ is a polynomial of degree $2j-2i-4.$ For the elementary special case $\beta_{i,2i+2}(I_G)=0,$ this amounts to that $(i+1)K_2$--free graphs are ${\omega-1+2i \choose 2i}$--colorable, improving on an old combinatorial result by Wagon. We also show that triangle-free graphs with $\beta_{i,j}(I_G)=0$ are $(j-1)$--colorable.
  Complexity wise, we show that these colorings can be derived in time $O(n^3)$ for graphs on $n$ vertices. Moreover, we show that for almost all graphs with parabolic $i,j,$ there are better bounds on $\chi.$

papers.title: An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line
papers.abstract: The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths alpha and $1 - \alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. We show that there are precisely five distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1 - \alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread, meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice. The proof of this surprising fact combines the construction and analysis of a related family of primitive substitution tilings, Solomon's criterion for uniform spreadness, and a classification of Pisot-Vijayaraghavan polynomials.

papers.title: Defect of projective hypersurfaces with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a hypersurface with isolated singularities defined by $f$ in ${\bf P^{n+1}}$ with $n>1$. The difference ${\rm def}(X):=h^{n+1}(X)-h^{n-1}(X)$ is called the defect of $X$ (for self-duality of the cohomology of $X$). It is known that its vanishing is closely related to ${\bf Q}$-factoriality of $X$ without assuming rational singularities when $n=3$. This number coincides with the dimension of the cokernel of the inclusion $H^{n-1}(X)\to{\rm IH}^{n-1}(X)$, the rank of the morphism from the vanishing cohomologies of $X$ to $H^{n+1}(X)$ for a one-parameter smoothing of $X$ with total space smooth, and also with the dimension of the unipotent monodromy part of the Milnor fiber cohomology of $f$ with degree $n$. In the case $X$ has only weighted homogeneous isolated singularities, the defect ${\rm def}(X)$ is then given by the $E_2$-term of the spectral sequence of the double complex with differentials ${\rm d}f\wedge$ and $\rm d$ by the $E_2$-degeneration of the pole order spectral sequence. It can be calculated explicitly using a computer even for analogues of the Hirzebruch quintic threefold with more than one hundred ordinary double points found by B.\ van Geemen and J.\ Werner in a compatible way with their computation. We give also an example with ${\rm def}(X)>0$ and $|{\rm Sing}\,X|=1$ in the non-projective cone case where $n=3$.

papers.title: SC-LDPC Codes Over $\mathbb{F}_q$: Minimum Distance, Decoding Analysis and Threshold Saturation
papers.abstract: We investigate random spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) code ensembles over finite fields. Under different variable-node edge-spreading rules, the random Tanner graphs of several coupled ensembles are defined by multiple independent, uniformly random monomial maps. The two main coupled ensembles considered are referred to as the standard coupled ensemble and the improved coupled ensemble. We prove that both coupled ensembles exhibit asymptotically good minimum distance and minimum stopping set size. Theoretical and numerical results show that the improved coupled ensemble can achieve better distance performance than the standard coupled ensemble. We introduce the essential preliminaries and analytical tools needed to analyze the iterative decoding threshold of coupled ensembles over any finite field. We consider a class of memoryless channels with special symmetry, termed q-ary input memoryless symmetric channels (QMSCs), and show that, for these channels, the distribution of channel messages (in form of probability vectors) likewise exhibits this symmetry. Consequently, we define symmetric probability measures and their reference measures on a finite-dimensional probability simplex, analyze their foundational properties and those of their linear functionals, endow their respective spaces with metric topologies, and conduct an in-depth study of their degradation theory. Based on our analytical framework, we establish a universal threshold saturation result for both of the coupled ensembles over a q-ary finite field on QMSCs. Specifically, as the coupling parameters increase, the belief-propagation threshold of a coupled system saturates to a well-defined threshold that depends only on the underlying ensemble and the channel family.

papers.title: Bilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions and applications
papers.authors: Anji Dong, Nicolas Robles, Dirk Zeindler
papers.abstract: We establish bounds for bilinear forms $\sum\sum_{m,n}\alpha_m\beta_n\,e(a\overline{m}/n)$ with Kloosterman fractions, where $M<m\le 2M$, $N<n\le 2N$ and $(m,n)=1$, for arbitrary sequences of complex numbers $(\alpha_m)$ and $(\beta_n)$ and for positive integer numerators $a\ll X^{1/10}$, where $X=\max(M,N)$, and for the corresponding trilinear forms with an average over $a$. In the balanced case, where $M$ and $N$ are of the same order of magnitude, and for bounded $a$, the saving over the trivial bound is $X^{1/16-\varepsilon}$, which improves upon the savings $X^{1/48-\varepsilon}$ of Duke, Friedlander and Iwaniec and $X^{1/20-\varepsilon}$ of Bettin and Chandee. The proof follows the amplification method of these authors; where they apply Weil's bound, we use for most of the terms the estimates of Deshouillers and Iwaniec for sums of Kloosterman sums, in the form given by Pascadi. As an application, we prove an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta-function with Dirichlet polynomials of length $T^{\theta}$ for $\theta<14/27$, extending the range $\theta<17/33$ of Bettin, Chandee and Radziwill. We also give applications to a determinant equation and to convolutions in arithmetic progressions with a fixed residue, on average over moduli as large as $x^{14/27-\varepsilon}$.

papers.title: Succinct Strict Pair Certificates for Reduced Groebner Bases
papers.authors: Chandrasekhar Gokavarapu, Lakshmi Gayathri Isukapalli, Janardhana Rao Kolli, Fathima Sulthana Md, Sai Durga Rolla
papers.abstract: We classify verification of supplied strict critical-pair witnesses for Groebner bases in a graph model with shared polynomial and exponent computations. Over the rationals, unrestricted verification in two variables is polynomial-time many-one equivalent to identity testing for powerful skew circuits over the integers. The reverse reduction uses a fixed two-element reduced Groebner basis and preserves the formal monomial bound on every witness it constructs. The forward reduction gives a one-sided-error randomized polynomial-time verifier without a support bound. We also prove matching bounds on certificate length for explicit families. For a bivariate family indexed by $k$, literal shifts require $\Theta(k^2)$ bits, shared exponent computations require $\Theta(k)$ bits, and an expanded certificate requires $\Omega(k2^k)$ bits. For a multivariate family with $K=\sum_i k_i$, the bounds are $\Theta(nK+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for full shift vectors and $\Theta(K\log_2(n+1)+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for sparse shift labels.

papers.title: The many faces of multivariate information
papers.abstract: Total correlation, dual total correlation, S-information, and O-information are usually presented as a family of related but distinct measures of higher-order dependency in complex systems. Here we show that three of them (S-information, dual total correlation, and negative O-information) are in fact collinear samples of a single affine function of an integer parameter $k$, which we call $\Delta^{k}$. This form provides a well-defined notion of interaction order: fragility under single-variable deletion. We then show that $\Delta^{k}$ has a conjugate partner, $\Gamma^{k}$, which arranges S-information, total correlation, and O-information into a dual spectrum of redundancy rather than synergy. Finally, we relax the implicit maximum-entropy reference distribution built into all of these measures, defining a Kullback-Leibler generalization $\Lambda^{k}(P\|Q)$ that measures higher-order information gain when updating from an arbitrary prior to an arbitrary posterior.

papers.title: Components of the nested Hilbert scheme of few points
papers.abstract: We study the existence and the schematic structure of elementary components of the nested Hilbert scheme on a smooth quasi-projective variety. More precisely, we establish a new lower bound for the existence of non-smoothable nestings of fat points on a smooth $n$-fold, for $n\geqslant 4$. Moreover, we develop a systematic method for building generically non-reduced elementary components. We also investigate the irreducibility of the Hilbert scheme of points on a singular hypersurface of $\mathbb A^3$. Explicitly, we show that the Hilbert scheme of points on a hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ having a singularity of multiplicity at least 5 admits elementary components.

papers.title: Existence and partial regularity of suitable weak solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations
papers.authors: Renjun Duan, Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Jianbo Yu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations coupled with the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation, which describes a two-phase mixture of the viscous incompressible fluid with particles or bubbles through a frictional force term. In the three-dimensional whole space, we construct a new class of suitable weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system satisfying energy estimates and three local or global energy inequalities of different forms. These obtained local energy inequalities play an important role in characterizing the measure of the singularity set of weak solutions. The main difficulties in deriving these inequalities lie in establishing the convergence of the density function $f$ in bounded or unbounded domains and dealing with the convergence of the non-local frictional force term. The strong $L^1$ convergence of $|v|^k f$ for $0\le k<\kappa$ and of $|v|^k f\log f$ locally in $x$ for $0\le k<\kappa/2$ is proved by using new a priori estimates for the velocity, Tao's $L^p$ decomposition, and the DiPerna-Lions compactness method. Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the existence result, we are able to describe the Hausdorff dimension of set of singular points of the fluid velocity $u$ and also establish the $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder continuity of $f$ at the regular points of $u$.

papers.title: Convergence Rate of the Last Iterate of Stochastic Proximal Algorithms
papers.authors: Kevin Kurian Thomas Vaidyan, Michael P. Friedlander, Ahmet Alacaoglu
papers.abstract: We analyze two classical algorithms for solving additively composite convex optimization problems where the objective is the sum of a smooth term and a nonsmooth regularizer. The first algorithm is the proximal stochastic gradient method for a single regularizer; the second is the randomized incremental proximal method, which uses the proximal operator of a randomly selected function when the regularizer is given as the sum of many nonsmooth functions. We focus on relaxing the bounded variance assumption that is common, yet stringent, for getting last iterate convergence rates. We prove the $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ rate of convergence for the last iterate of both algorithms under componentwise convexity and smoothness, which is optimal up to log terms. Our results apply directly to graph-guided regularizers that arise in multi-task and federated learning, where the regularizer decomposes as a sum over edges of a collaboration graph.

papers.title: Higher rank bundles on Hopf surfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove the existence of filtrable stable bundles on the Hopf surface with any rank and $c_2>0$, and show they must have jumps.In the opposite direction, for each integer $r\ge 2$ we prove the existence of irreducible rank $r$ vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant, $c_2=1$, and no jumps.
  We apply codimension $2$ operations to elements of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{r,n}$ of rank $r$ stable vector bundles with $c_2=n$ on the Hopf surface, obtaining families of torsion free sheaves in the closure of $\mathcal M_{r,n+1}$ when $c_2>1$.

papers.title: On the Existence of Koopman Linear Embeddings for Controlled Nonlinear Systems
papers.authors: Xu Shang, Masih Haseli, Jorge Cort\'es, Yang Zheng
papers.abstract: Koopman linear representations have become a popular tool for control design of nonlinear systems, yet it remains unclear when such representations are exact. In this paper, we establish sufficient and necessary conditions under which a controlled nonlinear system admits an exact Koopman linear representation in both infinite-dimensional and finite-dimensional settings. We show that such a system must be transformable into a special control-affine preserved (CAP) structure, which enforces affine dependence of the state on the control input and isolates all nonlinearities into an autonomous subsystem. We further prove that a finite-dimensional representation additionally requires this autonomous subsystem must itself admit a finite-dimensional Koopman linear model with a sufficiently-rich Koopman invariant subspace. Finally, we introduce a symbolic procedure to determine whether a given controlled nonlinear system admits the CAP structure, thereby elucidating whether Koopman approximation errors arise from intrinsic system dynamics or from the choice of lifting functions.

papers.title: On the singularity and the inverse of 3-colored digraphs
papers.abstract: This article investigates the singularity and invertibility of simple connected 3-colored digraphs, with particular emphasis on the classes of unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs. A digraph $G$ is said to be non-singular (resp. singular) if its adjacency matrix $A(G)$ is non-singular (resp. singular). The main objective of this article is to characterize the non-singular 3-colored unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs. For a non-singular digraph $G$, if the diagonal entries of $A(G)^{-1}$ are all zero, then $A(G)^{-1}$ can be realized as the adjacency matrix of a weighted digraph with complex weights. We characterize all non-singular 3-colored unicyclic and bicyclic digraphs for which this condition holds. Furthermore, we investigate the invertibility of these digraphs and characterize those whose inverses are also 3-colored digraphs.
