In particular, our characterization of the unicyclic case extends earlier results by removing the assumption that the digraph possesses a unique perfect matching.

papers.title: Asymptotic formulas for products of Poisson distributions
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour of the product tail probability $
  \mathbb{P}(\xi_1\cdots\xi_N \geqslant n), $ where $\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\}$ is a finite collection of independent Poisson random variables with positive parameters $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N$. We derive a refined Laplace-type asymptotic formula for the tail probability, based on Stirling's logarithmic approximation, a constrained saddle-point method, the Lambert function, and a careful evaluation of the constrained Gaussian prefactor. This yields an explicit approximation with an $O(\log n)$ remainder term in the exponent.

papers.title: Explicit Formulas, Duality, and Periodicity for Multi-Indexed Poly-Bernoulli Numbers
papers.authors: Yuna Baba, Tomoko Kikuchi, Maki Nakasuji
papers.abstract: We study multi-indexed poly-Bernoulli numbers defined through multiple polylogarithms. The central result is an explicit formula in terms of Stirling numbers of the second kind and multinomial coefficients, valid in arbitrary depth and for arbitrary integral upper indices. We present a direct coefficient-extraction proof of the formula and derive the duality relation for negative upper indices from a symmetric multivariate exponential generating function. We then use these formulas to establish congruence periodicity in each lower index modulo an arbitrary prime power, extending the double-indexed result of Baba, Nakasuji, and Sakata. A second application gives a congruence for the sum over one complete period in the first lower index.

papers.title: Relative Gr\"obner bases of modules and applications in persistence theory
papers.authors: Fritz Grimpen, Matthias Orth, Anastasios Stefanou
papers.abstract:
Finitely generated modules over the polynomial ring in $n$ indeterminates are isomorphic to quotients of finite rank free modules.
  We introduce a theory of relative Gr\"obner bases for those quotients of free modules and, equivalently, for pairs of submodules; we prove corresponding Buchberger- and Schreyer-type theorems.
  As applications of this theory, we consider three problems in persistence theory, which can be solved by relative Gr\"obner bases.
  First, we show that the relative Schreyer's theorem can be used to compute free presentations of complexes of finitely generated torsion-free modules.
  In contrast to previous approaches, this allows computation of free presentations for multicritical persistent homology directly at the chain module level without additional topological constructions.
  Second, any finitely generated Artinian module embeds in an Artinian injective hull, giving rise to a flat-injective presentation.
  We represent the embedding of the module in this injective hull by a quotient of a free module and apply the relative Schreyer's theorem to construct an algorithm for the computation of a free presentation from a flat-injective presentation.
  Third, we investigate how free presentations, and more generally free resolutions, obtained by the two preceding applications can be minimized by standard reduction techniques.

papers.title: A Fujita-type threshold for the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity and initial data from homogeneous Besov spaces
papers.authors: Thuy Hien Thi Nguyen, Duc An Phan
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity $\mathcal{I}_\gamma(|u|^{p_1})|u|^{p_2}$, where $0<\gamma<n$, and initial data possessing additional negative regularity in $\dot{B}_{2,\infty}^{-\beta}$, $0\leq\beta<n/2$. We first establish decay estimates for the corresponding linear equation in homogeneous Besov spaces $\dot{B}_{q,r}^s$, allowing low-frequency data in $\dot{B}_{m,\infty}^{-\beta}$ under the condition $s+\beta+n(1/m-1/q)>0$. We then prove the existence of a unique global mild solution for sufficiently small initial data in the critical and supercritical range $$ p_1+p_2\geq1+\frac{4+2\gamma}{n+2\beta}, $$ under the remaining assumptions on $p_1$ and $p_2$. Furthermore, for initial data satisfying a positive lower bound, we prove the nonexistence of global weak solutions when $$ 2<p_1+p_2<1+\frac{4+2\gamma}{n+2\beta}. $$

papers.title: Out-of-the-Box Global Optimization for Packing Problems: New Models and Improved Solutions
papers.authors: Timo Berthold, Dominik Kamp, Gioni Mexi, Sebastian Pokutta, Imre Polik
papers.abstract:
Recent LLM-driven discoveries have renewed interest in geometric packing problems. In this paper, we study several classes of such packing problems through the lens of modern global nonlinear optimization. Starting from comparatively direct nonlinear formulations, we consider packing circles in squares and fixed-perimeter rectangles, packing circles into minimum-area ellipses, packing regular polygons into regular polygons, and packing Platonic solids into Platonic solids. For ellipse packing, we derive a novel containment formulation based on the S-lemma. For polygon and Platonic solid packing, we develop compact non-overlap formulations based on the Farkas lemma and study several natural modeling variants computationally.
  Using off-the-shelf global optimization solvers, namely FICO Xpress and SCIP, we obtain numerous new incumbent solutions as well as first solutions for previously unstudied variants without any problem-specific solver modifications beyond writing down the models. Our computational results analyze the impact of various formulation choices.
  Beyond the individual packing results, the paper illustrates a broader point. It provides further evidence that global nonlinear optimization has matured into an increasingly practical model-and-solve technology for highly nonconvex problems.

papers.title: Superintegrability in the Interaction of Two Particles with Spin: First-Order Pseudo-Scalar Integrals of Motion
papers.authors: Fatih T\"urkkan, O. O\u{g}ulcan Tuncer, \.Ismet Yurdu\c{s}en
papers.abstract: In a recent work, we initiated a research program aimed at the systematic investigation of quantum superintegrable systems describing the interaction of two non-relativistic spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ particles in three-dimensional Euclidean space. In that study, we classified all such superintegrable systems admitting additional first-order scalar integrals of motion. In the present paper, we continue this program by focusing on systems that admit additional pseudo-scalar integrals of motion. Starting from the most general rotationally invariant Hamiltonian for two interacting spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ particles, we construct the most general pseudo-scalar operator of differential order at most one in the form of a matrix polynomial in the momenta. Imposing the commutativity of this operator with the Hamiltonian leads to a system of determining equations. By solving these equations, we obtain a complete classification of Hamiltonians in the considered class admitting additional pseudo-scalar integrals of differential order at most one, and determine these integrals explicitly. The resulting classification provides new families of spin-dependent Hamiltonians with additional pseudo-scalar symmetries. These systems enrich the class of integrable models relevant to nucleon-nucleon interactions and contribute to the broader program of classifying superintegrable quantum systems with spin. For selected cases, we further construct the associated polynomial symmetry algebras generated by the integrals of motion, providing additional insight into the algebraic structure of the systems.

papers.title: Arboreal Galois Groups of a PCF Map with Strictly Pre-periodic Critical Points
papers.authors: \"Ozlem Ejder, Zofia Go{\l}aska, Yasemin Kara, Leonie Nienhaus, \"Ozge \"Ulkem
papers.abstract: We study the arithmetic and geometric iterated monodromy groups associated to the postcritically finite (PCF) quadratic rational function $f(x)=\frac{2}{(x-1)^2}$ defined over a number field $k$, whose critical points are both strictly pre-periodic. We give explicit recursive descriptions of the topological generators of the geometric iterated monodromy group of $f$ and show that the arithmetic iterated monodromy group has Hausdorff dimension zero. We describe an explicit criterion to determine the values $a \in k$ for which the associated arboreal Galois group achieves its maximum possible size. In particular, we show that maximality of the arboreal Galois group can already be verified at level four, which is computationally accessible. We also determine the normalizer of the geometric IMG of $f$ and show that the arithmetic IMG equals the normalizer if $\zeta_8$ is not contained in $k$. Finally, we show that when $k=\mathbb{Q}$, the constant field contains $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_{2^{\infty}})$, providing the first full study of a PCF quadratic map with non-abelian constant field.

papers.title: Torsional Rigidity and Spherical Deficit for a Dirichlet Problem on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this work, we study several inequalities related to a Dirichlet problem on Riemannian manifolds whose Ricci curvature is bounded from below. First, we establish sharp inequalities involving the torsional rigidity and show that equality forces the domain to be isometric to a geodesic ball in a space form, with no symmetry assumption on the ambient manifold. Next, we derive an integral identity associated with the same Dirichlet problem, which measures the spherical deficit arising in this context. In particular, we apply this identity to Einstein manifolds, where it yields a rigidity result and a bound for the weighted spherical deficit in terms of the deviation of the normal derivative from a constant.

papers.title: A pathological set regarding the propagation of almost sure properties of Gaussian measures
papers.abstract: We provide a complementary result to the quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures supported on Sobolev spaces with high regularity under the dynamics of the three-dimensional periodic defocusing nonlinear wave equation from Gunaratnam-Oh-Tzvetkov-Weber (2022). Namely, given $p > 2$, $\sigma$ large enough and $\alpha \in [\max\{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{p} , 0\} , 1 - \frac{2}{p})$, we prove the existence of dense subsets of the Sobolev space $W^{\sigma + \alpha,p}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ which do not preserve the $L^p$-based regularity $\sigma$ throughout the aforementioned dynamics. This is in sharp contrast with the propagation under the flow of almost sure properties.

papers.title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
papers.authors: Levente Bodn\'ar, Jun Gao, Jared Le\'on, Xizhi Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Shumin Sun
papers.abstract: The inducibility constant $\lambda_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $\lambda_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $\lambda_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).

papers.title: Dimension-free estimates for covering functionals of simplices and $\ell_p$ balls
papers.authors: Feifei Chen, Chan He, Senlin Wu
papers.abstract: We study \(\Gamma_{2^n}(K)\), the least positive number \(\gamma>0\) such that an \(n\)-dimensional convex body \(K\) can be covered by \(2^n\) translates of \(\gamma K\). For \(n\)-simplices \(\Delta_n\), we prove that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(\Delta_n)\), as a sequence in \(n\), tends to \(1/2\). For the cross-polytope \(B_1^n\), we show that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(B_1^n)\leq5/6\) holds for all \(n\geq2\), and that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{2^n}(B_1^n)\leq0.641\cdots\). Finally, we prove the existence of a constant \(\kappa_*<1\) such that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(B_p^n)\leq\kappa_*\) for all \(n\geq2\) and all \(p\in[1,\infty]\).

papers.title: Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion: Definition and Fundamental Properties
papers.abstract: We introduce the $n$-th order multifractional stable motion ($n$-MFSM), a symmetric $\al$-stable process ($\al\in(1,2]$) whose Hurst parameter is a function $H(t)\in(n-1,n)$, obtained by a Taylor regularization of order $n\ge1$ of the kernel of the linear multifractional stable motion. It contains the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of Kawai as the special case of constant $H$, and, up to explicit deterministic factors, the linear multifractional stable motion ($n=1$) and the moving-average $n$-th order multifractional Brownian motion ($\al=2$). We prove existence, give the harmonizable representation in the Gaussian case, and show that, if $H$ is of class $\mathcal C^n$ near $t_0$, the rescaled $n$-th order increments at $t_0$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to the $n$-th order increments of the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of index $H(t_0)$. We then study the dependence structure through the codifference. For $s>0$ fixed and $H(t)\to H_+$ with $(H(t)-H_+)\log t\to0$, we obtain the exact power rate of $\tau(X(s),X(t))-c_0(s)$ as $t\to\infty$ away from the boundaries of three explicit parameter regimes, where $c_0(s)=\|X(s)\|_\al^\al$ if $\al<2$ and $c_0=0$ if $\al=2$; the constants are explicit and of known sign when $n\ge2$ or $\al=2$, while for $n=1$ and $\al<2$ part of one regime yields only convergence or a modified constant. In particular this codifference does not tend to zero when $n\ge2$. For the $n$-th order increments with constant $H$, whose codifference asymptotics were obtained by Kawai, we give a self-contained proof with the sign of the leading constants and treat the boundary cases of the long-range dependence criterion $H\ge n-1/\al$; for a non-constant Hurst function this criterion is extended only to functions that are eventually constant.

papers.title: Twisted generalized Weyl Poisson algebras of type $(A_1)^n$
papers.abstract: We introduce a generalization of generalized Weyl Poisson algebras. This is a Poisson analogue of the twisted generalized Weyl algebras defined by Mazorchuk and Turowska. We prove existence of these algebras in two ways, using Ore extensions and by using skew Laurent Poisson algebras. It is shown that this structure is preserved under tensor products, Poisson twists, and by taking invariant rings. Finally, we prove a simplicity criterion for these Poisson algebras.

papers.title: On some geometrization of compact metric spaces: A solution to the Banach-Ulam conjecture
papers.abstract: We propose a geometrization of compact metric spaces that is based on ideas of S. Banach and J. Mycielski. Then we prove the following conjecture of S. Banach and S. Ulam from 1935: in every compact metric space there exists a finitely additive probability measure, invariant under congruences. Moreover, our techniques allow us to solve a problem of M. Talagrand related to the Marczewski problem and the Banach-Tarski paradox with pieces having the property of Baire. We give also a very simple proof of the conjecture of Ulam about the product Lebesgue measure in the Hilbert cube and explain the existing results about congruence-invariant Borel measures in the language of our geometrization.

papers.title: The dual Artin isomorphism for Artin groups of XL type
papers.abstract: We show that an Artin group $A_\Gamma$ of XL type (with all defining integers satisfying $m_{ij} \geq 4$) is isomorphic to the corresponding dual Artin group for any choice of Coxeter element. Our proof involves the set of Hurwitz words $Q$ which arise from the Hurwitz action on tuples of elements of the free group. We show that the canonical epimorphism from $A_\Gamma$ to the dual Artin group is an isomorphism if and only if the projection from $A_\Gamma$ to the Coxeter group is injective on the image of $Q$. Then, using geometric properties of $Q$ and the solution to the word problem for Coxeter groups, we show this to be the case when all $m_{ij} \geq 4$.

papers.title: The difference of the sums of odd and even parts of restricted partitions
papers.abstract: For a subset $D \subset \mathbb{N},$ denote by $S\!\left(D,n\right)$ the total sum of all odd parts minus the sum of all even parts of all partitions of $n$ in which parts from $D$ do not repeat. In this paper, we derive the generating function for $S\!\left(2\mathbb{N},n\right)$ and use it to give some congruences modulo 4. We also derive the generating function for $S\!\left(2\mathbb{N}-1,n\right)$ and give three congruences for these functions, one of which was previously proved by Garvan and Sarma.

papers.title: A note on the image of graded multilinear polynomials on upper triangular matrices
papers.authors: Adison Tim\'otio Silva, Felipe Yukihide Yasumura
papers.abstract:
We investigate the image of polynomials multilinear in graded variables evaluated on the algebra of upper triangular matrices endowed with a group grading. We show that, in general, such an image need not be a vector subspace. However, under the additional assumption that the identity component of the grading is commutative, we prove that the image is always a vector subspace.
  We further investigate the image of polynomials evaluated on inverse and direct limits of algebras. As a consequence, we prove that the image of a polynomial evaluated on a direct limit of upper triangular matrix algebras whose identity component is commutative is always a vector subspace.

papers.title: Operator Learning for Backstepping Control of Parabolic Equations on Time-Varying Domains
papers.authors: Jinrun Yan, Kai Liu, Zhong-Jie Han
papers.abstract: This paper develops a neural operator approach to boundary stabilization of a parabolic equation on a time-varying domain, reducing the cost of backstepping kernel computation. Specifically, we establish the continuity of the operator mapping moving boundaries to backstepping kernels and apply the universal approximation theorem to establish the existence of an approximate kernel. Due to the compactness requirement, the approximate kernel is derived only on a finite time interval, limiting the exponential decay estimate to a finite horizon. To extend the result to an infinite horizon, we must circumvent the compactness requirement. Taking periodic moving boundary as an example, we propose a modified DeepONet architecture that lifts the non-compact time domain into a compact, higher-dimensional space. This modification relaxes the constraint of approximation accuracy and extends finite-horizon exponential decay to uniform exponential stability over an infinite horizon. Numerical simulations demonstrate accelerated backstepping kernel computation and closed-loop stabilization.

papers.title: Minnaert resonances and higher-order acoustic modes for bubbles in a viscous fluid with surface tension
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Xin Fu, Wenjia Jing, Hongjie Li
papers.abstract: We study the low-frequency resonances (Minnaert resonances) for micro-bubbles in a viscous fluid with surface tension. The interior pressure is coupled to the exterior pressure--velocity system through a normal hydrodynamic Neumann-to-Dirichlet operator. We analyze the incompressible limit of this operator and its coupling to the linearized curvature operator. This coupling introduces an additional non-resonance condition needed to isolate the low-frequency acoustic modes considered here. Under this non-resonance condition, we derive leading-order asymptotic formulas for the resonant frequencies in terms of the difference in the acoustic impedance at the interface between the gas and the fluid. For multiple bubbles, the collective resonances are governed by an effective capacitance matrix. The spherical calculation recovers the known viscosity and surface-tension corrections. Possible extensions to higher-order resonances, i.e., beyond the subwavelength regime, are discussed.

papers.title: Zeta-regularization and natural boundaries: Sums and products of integers and primes
papers.authors: P. L. Krapivsky, J. M. Luck
papers.abstract: Euler regularized the divergent product of all positive integers and found beautiful formulas for regularized sums of integer powers of positive integers. These derivations essentially relied on what is now called the zeta-regularization technique, although analytical continuation had not yet been invented. This classic method is however not applicable to the product of all primes, as the prime zeta function has a natural boundary along the imaginary axis. Mu\~noz Garc\'ia and P\'erez-Marco overcame this obstacle and evaluated the product of all primes to $4\pi^2$ by finding an appropriately regularized value of the derivative of the prime zeta function at the origin, lying on the natural boundary. Their approach heavily relies on the M\"obius function and could therefore be called a M\"obius regularization. We extend this approach in two novel directions. First, we show how to make sense of the sum of all primes. This regularization requires going a finite distance beyond the natural boundary. Second, we determine the regularized products of integers and primes in the nine imaginary quadratic fields where integers have a unique factorization into primes, and establish a general power-law relationship between products of integers and primes. Two well-known examples are Gauss and Eisenstein integers. The interest in this approach goes beyond number theory. In a variety of physical situations, the zeta-regularization technique is indeed not applicable because the relevant zeta function has a natural boundary.

papers.title: Existence of weak solutions of the surface Beris-Edwards model
papers.authors: Gonzalo A. Benavides, Ricardo H. Nochetto, Mansur Shakipov
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of weak solutions to the surface Beris-Edwards model for nematic liquid crystals posed on a $d$-dimensional ($d \in \{2,3\}$) closed hypersurface of class $C^{2,1}$. This thermodynamically consistent model, recently introduced by Bouck, Nochetto and Yushutin (2024), couples the incompressible tangent Navier-Stokes equations with a kinematic equation for the Q-tensor field that encodes the orientation of the liquid crystal particles with a general state of orientational order. Extending ideas by Abels, Dolzmann and Liu (2014) and Guill\'en-Gonz\'alez and Rodr\'iguez-Bellido (2015) for the Beris-Edwards model in flat domains, we design a Faedo-Galerkin scheme based upon eigenfunctions of an appropriate tangent Stokes operator and tensor-valued Laplace-Beltrami operator and recover a weak solution via standard compactness arguments.

papers.title: Euler characters for general linear Lie superalgebra
papers.abstract: M. Gorelik and Th. Heidersdors in the papers \cite{GH} investigated Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ and $\frak{osp}(m.2n)$. In the present paper we also investigate Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ but we use a different approach and our results are formulated in different terms.

papers.title: Transferring supremum-norm rates and weak convergence of covariance kernel estimators to functional principal components
papers.abstract: We show that $L_2$-perturbation theory can be used to transfer rates of convergence in the supremum norm as well as weak convergence in the space of continuous functions from covariance kernel estimators to the associated functional \rev{principal} components. As an application we obtain optimal rates of convergence in sup-norm, including minimax-lower bounds, as well as asymptotic normality for estimating the functional principal components in a discrete observational model with errors under fixed, synchronous design. The sparse to dense transition which has previously been observed for mean function and covariance kernel estimators also applies here. Surprisingly, eigenvalue estimation exhibits a discretization-dominated regime under sparse designs, too. Our results further apply to estimators of cross-covariance and long-run covariance kernels, as well as to covariance kernels of derivative processes. We also present results of numerical experiments in which we use the Nystr\"om method to compute functional principal components and eigenvalues, and give an empirical illustration to series of daily temperature curves.

papers.title: The Gauss periods and cyclotomic matrices involving Gauss sums over cyclic groups
papers.authors: Xiao-Han Ji, Li-Yuan Wang, Hai-Liang Wu
papers.abstract:
In this paper, by using the arithmetic properties of the Gauss periods and character sums over cyclic groups, we study the cyclotomic matrix
  $$A_k(\chi)=\left[G_N(\chi^{ki+ki})\right]_{0\le i,j\le \varphi(N)/k-1},$$
  where $N=p^m$ is a prime power, $\varphi(\cdot)$ is the Euler totient function, $k$ is a divisor of $\varphi(N)$, $\chi$ is a generator of character group $\widehat{(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{\times}}$, and
  $$G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}}\chi^{ki+kj}(x)e^{2\pi ix/N}$$
  is the Gauss sum over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$.

papers.title: On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the group randomness of 0-1 real sequences derived from a binary linear code through the spectral anlysis of a suitable normalization of the Gram matrix of a $p \times n$ random matrix whose rows are uniformly and independently drawn from those 0-1 real sequences, where $p/n \to y \in (0,1)$. We show that as $n \to \infty$, its empirical spectral distribution converges to the Marchenko-Pastur law at a rate at least of the order $n^{-1/4}$ with high probability as a consequence of eigenvalue interlacing with the $\pm 1$ sequence model studied in 2021 [14], and that its largest eigenvalue, after centering by $p+1+y$, converges to a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance $4y$, provided that the dual distance of the code is at least 5. Furthermore, we show that when this is the only control parameter, the lower bound 5 is optimal in general by demonstrating that the binary Simplex codes and first-order Reed-Muller codes of dual distance 3 and 4 respectively do not possess either property.

papers.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
papers.abstract: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\to\tau$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(\tau/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

papers.title: On the Generalized Arithmetic Picard--Lefschetz Formula
papers.abstract: This paper establishes an explicit arithmetic Picard--Lefschetz formula for isolated singularities of diagonal type. We investigate proper flat families of varieties over a henselian discrete valuation ring whose fraction field has characteristic zero. When the smooth generic fibre degenerates into a special fibre with isolated diagonal singularities, we construct an explicit eigenbasis for the tame inertia action on the local cohomology and obtain formulas for the intersection pairing and the variation morphism in this basis. When the residue field is finite, we also compute the traces of geometric Frobenius on the inertia invariants in terms of Jacobi sums. We apply this framework to the arithmetic study of symmetric powers of the Airy sheaf. Using geometric realizations associated with Airy moments, we establish specialization exact sequences for compactly supported and middle cohomology and determine the Frobenius characteristic polynomials of inertia-invariant local contributions.

papers.title: A unified perspective of Gaussian process approximation for differential equations
papers.abstract: The use of Gaussian processes for approximating differential equations has expanded rapidly, leading to a growing, diverse, and fragmented body of numerical methods. We present a unified Bayesian perspective that places these techniques within a common probabilistic framework, based on a derivative matching interpretation for incorporating differential equation constraints into likelihood. This unified perspective supports both parameter estimation and solution approximation, and shows how a range of existing methods can be understood within it. This work aims to consolidate current developments and provide a foundation for future research.

papers.title: Finite quotients of full surface braid groups and complex surfaces of general type: cyclic, dihedral, and extra-special quotients
papers.authors: Massimiliano Alessandro, Michelangelo Migliano, Francesco Polizzi
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf{B}_2(\Sigma_g)$ be the full braid group on two strings on a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We compute the number of epimorphisms $\varphi \colon \mathsf{B}_2(\Sigma_g) \to G$, where $G$ is a finite cyclic, dihedral or extra-special group, under the assumption that $\varphi$ does not factor through $\pi_1(\operatorname{Sym}^2\Sigma_g)$. We then apply our algebraic results to the geometric problem of constructing smooth surfaces of general type as Galois covers of $\operatorname{Sym}^2\Sigma_g$ branched along the diagonal. Notably, when the branching order is at least $3$, we obtain surfaces with positive signature, i.e. $c_1^2>2c_2$. In particular, we construct two $3$-dimensional families of minimal surfaces of general type with $p_g(S)=154$, $q(S)=2$ and $K_S^2=1269$, such that members of different families have the same numerical invariants, the same Betti numbers and the same positive signature, but different torsion subgroups in their first integral homology groups.

papers.title: Positive definite matrices and involutions: the manners of their infinite cousins
papers.authors: Pere Ara, Ken Goodearl, Kevin C. O'Meara
papers.abstract: Matrices and involutions in/on the algebras $B(\mathbb{R})$ and $B(\mathbb{C})$ of real (resp., complex) row- and column-finite $\omega\times\omega$ matrices are studied. It is proved that any positive definite $\mathbb{R}$-algebra involution on $B(\mathbb{R})$ (resp., any positive definite conjugate-linear involution on $B(\mathbb{C})$) is given by conjugating the transpose involution (resp., the conjugate-transpose involution) with a positive definite matrix from the algebra in question. All positive definite matrices in these algebras have Cholesky factorizations within the algebra. Examples are constructed to show that such positive definite matrices need not have any eigenvalues for their canonical action on column-finite column vectors, and they need not have any square roots in $B(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: Intercity EV Charging Readiness in T\"urkiye: A Countrywide Scheduling and Economic Assessment
papers.abstract: This paper assesses whether T\"urkiye's 9,641 public charging stations licensed by the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK) can support intercity electric vehicle (EV) travel, and at what cost relative to internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. A charging scheduling framework based on a directed acyclic graph plans the charging stops of 3 million synthetic intercity trips on a 55,236-link highway network built from OpenStreetMap. Virtually all trips can be completed with the existing stations under both 10--100% and 20--80% state-of-charge windows; the 0.3% feasibility that a 20--80% window can produce arises only when trips must also start within the window, not from gaps in the network. Capacity, not coverage, is the binding constraint: with plug counts calibrated to EPDK socket statistics, uncoordinated charging builds long queues at the stations where trips converge, whereas coordinating charging times with reservations nearly eliminates waiting at today's adoption level of about 3%. In the 350 kW scenario at 3% adoption, the EV is 49.8% cheaper than the ICE vehicle in operating costs (energy, refueling, detour, and charging time) and 7.4% cheaper in total cost of ownership, an advantage that holds as long as the EV costs at most about 9% more than a comparable ICE vehicle. Adding the cost of charging infrastructure makes the EV more expensive at low adoption with high-power chargers and cheaper as adoption grows.

papers.title: An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.

papers.title: Fundamental group schemes of globally F-regular varieties
papers.abstract: Let X be a globally F-regular projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We show that the Nori fundamental group scheme of its regular locus is finite and linearly reductive. Finiteness is the counterpart of theorems of Xu and Braun on the fundamental group of the smooth locus of a complex log Fano variety. The key input is that if a cover of a splinter is a torsor in codimension one and induces an isomorphism on global functions, then its structure group is linearly reductive. We then show that towers of such covers stabilize, both over globally $F$-regular varieties and, in mixed characteristic, over the globally $+$-regular schemes considered by Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker.

papers.title: Vertex-Ramsey theorems for Cartesian powers of graphs
papers.authors: N\'ora Alm\'asi, Maria Axenovich, Arsenii Sagdeev
papers.abstract:
For graphs $G,H$ and positive integers $r$ and $n$ we write $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$ if every $r$-vertex-coloring of the Cartesian power $G^{\square n}$ of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. Since chromatic number $\chi$ of $G^{\square n}$ is the same as $\chi(G)$, there is an $r$-vertex coloring of $G^{\square n}$ for $r=\chi(G)$, such that each color class is an independent set.
  We prove that for $r<\chi(G)$ there is a large class of graphs $H$ such that $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$. These graphs are so-called layered graphs in a hypercube. We also show that for some graphs $G$, such as for example odd cycles or cliques, the class of layered graphs $H$ is the only one satisfying the above Ramsey property when $\chi(G)/2 < r < \chi(G)$.
  In addition, we prove a more general result relating Ramsey properties of $G$ and graphs $H$ such that $G^{\square n} \xrightarrow{r} H$. One of the technical tools is a Ramsey-type statement for discrete cubes $[m]^n$ that we call the Cube Layered Lemma, which is of independent interest. One of the original motivations for studying Ramsey properties of Cartesian powers of $G$ is the fact that $G^{\square n}$ is a unit distance graph if $G$ is a unit distance graph. This provides applications in Euclidean Ramsey theory.

papers.title: Halpern Iteration Accelerates Solving High-Order Monotone Variational Inequalities
papers.authors: Lesi Chen, Xinliang Zhang, Hengyu Wang, Chengchang Liu, Yongchao Chen, Jingzhao Zhang
papers.abstract: In this short note, we revisit the classical Halpern iteration in 1967 and show its new applications in designing second- and higher-order methods for solving smooth monotone variational inequalities (MVI). By using a large-step inexact Halpern iteration, we propose a novel $p$th-order method Halpern-ATM, that achieves a fast convergence rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-p})$. This improves the best-known results for $p \ge 2$ since 2012.

papers.title: A negative exponent range for Audenaert's complementary McCarthy trace inequality
papers.abstract: Audenaert introduced a class of complementary McCarthy type trace inequalities in his work on completely monotone functions and Bernstein functions; the same problem was later included in the problem list of Audenaert and Kittaneh. The known results cover the corresponding directions for $q\le -2$, $0<q\le 1$, $1\le q\le 2$, and $2\le q\le 3$, while the negative range $-2<q<0$ was left as a conjectural case. We prove the negative exponent inequality, in fact for every $q<0$. After the inversion $X=A^{-1}$, $Y=B^{-1}$, the problem reduces to a trace inequality for the parallel sum $X:Y$. The proof uses the Kubo--Ando mean chain, an Ando--Hiai type log-majorization for matrix geometric means, and a finite-dimensional Schatten H\"older inequality, including the quasi-norm range. We also record that the positive exponent side $q\ge 3$ follows directly from Audenaert's norm-compression inequality for positive semidefinite $2\times2$ block matrices, and in fact holds for all $q\ge 2$. Finally, we determine the equality case on the negative side: equality holds if and only if $A=B$.

papers.title: Compactness phenomena in HOD and the Optimality of Magidor's Covering theorem
papers.authors: Tom Benhamou, James Cummings, Yair Hayut, Gabriel Goldberg, Alejandro Poveda
papers.abstract: We investigate compactness phenomena around the power-set functions of $V$ and HOD. We prove: (1) A singular strong limit cardinal with uncountable cofinality cannot be the first place where $\mathcal{P}(\cdot )$ and $ \mathcal{P}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(\cdot)$ disagree. (2) Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, $\aleph_\omega$ can be the first place where $\mathcal{P}(\aleph_\omega)\neq \mathcal{P}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(\aleph_\omega)$, answering a question of Hayut. (3) If $\kappa$ is strong limit singular of uncountable cofinality, $\kappa$ cannot be the first place where $(\mathrm{HOD}, V)$ fails to have the cover property; (4)Magidor's Covering Theorem is optimal.

papers.title: Convergence and acceleration of a nonlinear fixed-point iteration for computing the Fitness Centrality of general graphs
papers.abstract: We establish the global convergence of the (non-homogeneous) Fitness Centrality algorithm for general graphs, deriving an explicit convergence bound for the corresponding fixed-point iteration. From the computational point of view, we show how the convergence can be dramatically improved by Anderson acceleration and by switching to Newton's method once a sufficiently good approximation to the fixed point has been found. The efficacy of this strategy is illustrated by numerical experiments on different types of graphs.

papers.title: Counting Near-Spanning Matchings in Latin Squares and Steiner Triple Systems
papers.abstract: Montgomery proved that for sufficiently large $n$, every Latin square of order $n$ has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells, and every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges, thus confirming the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture for even $n$ and the conjecture of Brouwer. We prove sharp enumerative refinements of these results: there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, (1) every Latin square of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^n$ partial transversals with $n-1$ cells; (2) every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{2\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ matchings with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges. The first estimate confirms predictions of Montgomery and Kelly. We also provide sharp estimates for the numbers of partial transversals and matchings of every smaller size.

papers.title: Taut and Dupin Submanifolds (Updated Version)
papers.abstract: This is an updated version of a paper by the author which originally appeared in 1997. The original paper was a survey of the closely related fields of taut and Dupin submanifolds of Euclidean space, and this updated version includes many results in the field that have appeared since the publication of the original version. The emphasis is on stating results in their proper context and noting areas for future research, and relatively few proofs are given. The important class of isoparametric hypersurfaces is surveyed in detail, as is the relationship between the two concepts of taut and Dupin. Also included is a brief introduction to submanifold theory in Lie sphere geometry which is needed to state many known results on Dupin submanifolds accurately. The paper concludes with detailed descriptions of the main known classification results for both Dupin and taut submanifolds.

papers.title: Pauli Supported Invariants for Periodic Graphs-Derived Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Sarah Chehade, Andrew Vlasic, Rebekah Herrman, Rick Mukherjee
papers.abstract: We introduce a graph invariant obtained from Pauli decompositions of Hamiltonians derived from local graph neighborhoods. Given a rooted h-hop neighborhood, we construct a local adjacency operator, embed it into a common Hilbert space dimension, and define its Pauli-support set as the collection of Pauli strings appearing with nonzero coefficients. For periodic graphs, we prove invariance under lattice-compatible graph equivalence and establish converse results under root-separation hypothesis. The framework naturally extends to Lie closures, commutants, and Cartan-type structures generated by the associated Pauli supports. We further discuss extensions to aperiodic graphs with finite local complexity and make connections to cut-and-project models of quasicrystals and notably, Penrose tilings. From a quantum information perspective, the resulting invariants provide a operator-theoretic description of graph-based Hamiltonians and offer a new mechanism for comparing graph-based quantum systems through Pauli-support data.

papers.title: Polynomial Length Cycles In Tough Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every $n$-vertex $15$-tough graph contains a cycle of length $\Omega(n^{1/20})$.

papers.title: Dedekind Eta Powers and Interlacing in Lambert Series Quotients
papers.abstract: For each $0<q<1$ we prove that the zeros and poles of a quotient of Lambert series formed from the cube of Euler's product are simple, negative and strictly interlacing. The zeros of the sampled series decrease strictly as its shift increases through $(0,1]$. The quotient has a partial-fraction expansion with positive weights, and every average over the $d$-th roots of unity with $d$ odd exceeds the value of the quotient at the origin. For even $d$, every pole of the average in the parameter $q\in(0,1)$ is simple and has positive residue. We also characterize the cube as the unique positive integer power of Euler's product whose sampling kernel is a P\'olya frequency function. For a general positive integer power $k$ and integer dilation $a\ge2$, the quotient interpolates $z^{1-1/a}$ at geometric nodes selected by the nonzero coefficients of the Euler product power. We determine its radial limit away from two real rays and the asymptotic locations of the poles of the averages of even order near $q=1$. For the cube, convergence to the fractional power is exponentially fast on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]$. The positive discrete measures in the partial-fraction expansion converge vaguely on $(0,\infty)$ to $\pi^{-1}\sin(\pi/a)u^{-1/a}\,du$.

papers.title: Orlicz space relaxation of total variation denoising
papers.abstract: We consider variational image denoising with spatially dependent Orlicz regularization and introduce an Orlicz--Sobolev approximation of the ROF model based on a scaled $L\log L$-type density. For a general class of uniformly superlinear integrands satisfying a $\Delta_2$-condition, we establish existence and uniqueness of minimizers and derive a Fenchel dual problem with dual attainment and pointwise optimality conditions. We then specialize the framework to a logarithmic density whose correction is activated above a prescribed local gradient scale. For this model, we obtain explicit expressions of the Fenchel dual and optimality conditions as well as a pointwise radial formula for the dual proximal map involving the Lambert $W$-function. As the logarithmic parameter tends to zero, we prove equicoercivity and $\Gamma$-convergence to the ROF functional, together with convergence of the corresponding minimizers. Numerical illustrations indicate that the logarithmic correction can reduce staircasing for diffuse transitions, while retaining behavior comparable to ROF for sharp interfaces and a natural image.

papers.title: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
papers.abstract: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $\theta = \Pr(N=1) \in (0, \theta_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $\theta$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.

papers.title: New best-known coverings, packing-coverings and quantizers in low dimensions
papers.abstract: We construct periodic point sets that improve the best known covering densities in dimensions six and seven, packing-covering constants in dimensions five, six, and seven, and normalized second moments in dimensions five and six. In dimension five, a set of the original family of Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann has packing-covering constant $9/\sqrt{40}$, strictly below the proven optimum for the lattice case. All seven point sets belong to a two-parameter subfamily of a four-parameter generalization of the Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann family.

papers.title: Geometric Dissipation Structures and the Koszul Form
papers.authors: Romain Nimpa Pefoukeu, Prosper Rosaire Mama Assandje, Michel Bertrand Djiadeu Ngaha, Nozah Mba Frankel, Fr\'{e}d\'{e}ric Barbaresco
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the canonical Koszul one-form at the interface of Jean Marie Souriau's Lie group thermodynamics and Paulette Libermann's symplectically complete foliations to describe geometric dissipation. On the Poincar\'{e} half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ under $SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, the equivariant momentum map level sets form a regular Libermann foliation framing the conservative boundaries. The Koszul-derived dissipative vector field acts strictly transverse to these leaves, driving a metriplectic flow that breaks Noether conservation laws and generates entropy. Quantum wise, we develop Berezin quantization on para-K\"{a}hler symmetric spaces, where the Koszul potential acts as a weight determining state density via the Fisher Souriau metric, and formalize Kostant's geometric quantization using the real dual polarizations of a bi-Lagrangian web.

papers.title: Accelerated Bregman Proximal Gradient Methods from Dual Geometric Perspectives
papers.authors: Yuya Yamashita, Shota Takahashi, Akiko Takeda
papers.abstract: We study Bregman proximal gradient (BPG) algorithms under relative smoothness for convex, relatively strongly convex, and nonconvex objectives. Existing accelerated BPG algorithms for convex objectives typically require additional assumptions on Bregman divergences, most notably triangle-scaling conditions, which can lead to slower convergence rates. We propose a family of geometry-accelerated BPG algorithms that exploit Bregman geometry in both proximal-gradient and mirror-space updates, without imposing a triangle-scaling condition. Our methods adapt the stepsizes and mirror-space updates through local backtracking and computable acceptance criteria, without a global relative-smoothness constant as input. We derive convergence bounds in terms of the parameters accepted during the iterations. These bounds yield an $\mathcal O(k^{-2})$ rate for convex objectives and a linear rate for relatively strongly convex objectives when the geometry-acceleration parameters remain uniformly bounded. For nonconvex objectives, we establish an $\mathcal O(k^{-1})$ rate for a stationarity measure without requiring a lower Bregman bound or a full-domain Bregman divergence. Numerical experiments on inverse problems, entropy-regularized least squares, D-optimal design, and nonnegative matrix factorization demonstrate faster practical convergence than established Bregman baselines.

papers.title: Global Regularity for the Chemotaxis-Stokes System with Signal Consumption in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.authors: Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Guoxu Yang
papers.abstract:
Motivated by the continuum model of aerobic bacteria proposed by Tuval et al. in 2005, we study the large-data regularity problem for the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Stokes system with signal consumption. We prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ for smooth initial data with finite density mass and moment and finite signal Fisher information, without any smallness assumptions.
  The proof is based on three main ideas. First, we use a terminal heat-kernel representation to define a finite signal value at every spatial point and prove strong $L^a$ convergence of the backward parabolic signal rescalings to this value for every $1\le a<\infty$. Second, we prove a localized entropy estimate that remains uniform under density normalization, even when the resulting consumption coefficient becomes arbitrarily large. These estimates give two complementary mechanisms: consumption excludes normalized density concentration at points with positive terminal signal, while a localized weighted estimate improves density integrability at points with zero terminal signal. Third, we establish a local $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion based on smallness of scale-invariant density, velocity, and pressure quantities. A heat decomposition recovers the required signal-gradient smallness, removing it as a separate assumption. Together, these yield the decay of a scale-invariant density quantity and then exclude finite-time singularities.

papers.title: Affine balancing of complex dilatations: affine invariants and optimal distortion of harmonic quasiconformal mappings
papers.abstract: Target real-affine postcomposition induces a disk automorphism on the complex dilatation of orientation-preserving planar harmonic mapping. Motivated by the lack of intrinsic distortion measures for real-affine orbits, we introduce the affine circumradius, affine diameter, and affine circumcenter from the hyperbolic geometry of the dilatation range. The affine circumradius is the logarithm of the minimal value of the maximal differential distortion over the real-affine orbit, and the affine circumcenter describes minimizers up to Euclidean similarity. For non-constant dilatation, at most two or three contact points determine the minimal enclosing hyperbolic disk. We prove sharp two-sided radius-diameter bounds, with equalities realized by globally univalent harmonic quasiconformal mappings. Each orbit admits a canonical balanced representative, for which we derive a sharp norm bound for the gap between the harmonic pre-Schwarzian derivative and that of its analytic part. This bound exhibits quadratic small-dilatation asymptotics, and the balanced representative achieves the minimal dilatation parameter over the real-affine orbit.

papers.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
papers.authors: Lucas Chen, Joshua Im, Steven J. Miller, Devayani Pradhan
papers.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

papers.title: On C*-nuclearity of graph operator systems
papers.abstract: We classify the set of finite simple undirected graphs whose corresponding graph operator system is C*-nuclear. We prove that the operator system associated to the graph is C*-nuclear if and only if the graph is 2-chordal, as defined by McCullough. In particular, we present the first known example of a non-chordal graph whose graph operator system is C*-nuclear, as well as the first known examples of graph operator systems which are not C*-nuclear.

papers.title: Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
papers.abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.

papers.title: Interval Inverse Inequalities for Multiscale Kernel Primitives with Positive Exponential Spectra
papers.abstract: Inverse inequalities are fundamental for controlling derivative growth and ensuring sampling stability in kernel-based approximation. Extending whole-space and single-scale estimates to multiscale analytic spaces on bounded intervals requires uniform control of boundary truncation and cross-scale cancellation. We establish unweighted $L^2(0,1)$ inverse inequalities of sharp scaling order $h_*^{-1}$ for trial spaces spanned by affine functions and multiscale primitives of kernels with positive exponential spectra, where $h_*$ denotes the finest scale. Under geometric scale separation and within-scale center separation, the inverse constant depends only on the kernel and separation parameters; it is independent of the number of scales and centers, allowing centers at the endpoints and arbitrary cross-scale center coincidences. To prove the bound, we combine an exterior Gram decomposition with endpoint-distance weights to establish configuration-uniform Riesz bounds for normalized high-order derivatives of order $q$, whose lower constant approaches the optimal limit $1/2$. A synthesis-operator perturbation argument and parameterized interval interpolation then yield the first-order estimate. Two-center constructions confirm sharpness in both the scaling order $h_*^{-1}$ and the $q^{-1/2}$ asymptotic deficit from $1/2$ as $q \to \infty$. An application to deterministic least-squares sampling is derived, and numerical experiments on boundary-layer asymptotics, multiscale Gram spectra, sharp inverse constants, and midpoint sampling illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Curvature rank, numerical dimension, and cohomology growth
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be the least integer such that the first Bott--Chern class of $L$ is represented by a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form of rank at most $r$ at every point. For any nonzero coherent analytic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ whose support has dimension $d$, we prove that $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $0\le q\le d$. This is the exponent conjectured by Ma--Marinescu--Zelditch, up to an arbitrarily small loss. In the extreme degrees $q=0$ and $q=d,$ the bound can be taken to be $O(p^{\min\{r,d\}})$. If, moreover, $X$ is in Fujiki's class and $L$ is nef, then $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O(p^{\min\{\nu(L),\,d-q\}})$, where $\nu(L)$ is the numerical dimension of $L$. This answers a question of Demailly for compact Fujiki manifolds. Finally, for arbitrary $X$, any singular Hermitian metric \(h\) on \(L\) with semipositive curvature and analytic singularities, and any holomorphic vector bundle \(E\) on $X$, we have \(h^q(X,E\otimes L^p\otimes\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p}))=O_\varepsilon(p^{\min\{n-q,b+\varepsilon\}})\) for any $0\leq q\leq n$, where \(b\) is the maximum curvature rank outside the pole set of $h$, and $\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p})$ is the multiplier ideal sheaf. When $X$ belongs to Fujiki's class, the exponent is \(\min\{n-q,b\}\).

papers.title: The regionally proximal relation for commutative semigroup actions
papers.authors: Angelina Blahodatna, Lauren Detmold, Daniel Glasscock, Anh N. Le
papers.abstract: The regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are fundamental relations in topological dynamics that capture the equicontinuous behavior in a topological dynamical system and its factors. For minimal actions of abelian groups, these relations are known to be equivalence relations that coincide. In this paper, we generalize these facts to semigroup actions: for minimal actions of commutative semigroups, the regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are equivalence relations and the two coincide. We leverage our approach to prove a refinement: the regionally proximal relation for such actions is equal to an analogue and strengthening of Veech's D relation. We also develop the machinery of natural extensions for commutative, not-necessarily-cancellative semigroup actions that act by surjections, concluding that the maximal equicontinuous factor of a minimal action of a commutative semigroup is the same as the maximal equicontinuous factor of its natural extension. We formally verify all of the results in this paper in Lean. The main results are registered on Palomar, and we link to a Github repository containing code for the complete verification.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for $p$-adic Congruences and $p$-adic Interpolations of Sequences
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we treat the problem of determining, for a fixed prime $p$, a positive integer $\ell$ that is coprime to $p$, and a real number $r$, when a sequence $\{c_n\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ with the exponential generating function $F(t)$ satisfies the congruence $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ for all $k\ge0$ and large $n$ depending on $k$. Though this type of congruence is often observed for several number-theoretic or combinatorial sequences, such as Bernoulli numbers, Euler numbers, and Fibonacci numbers, it appears that their congruences have been shown individually.
  Traditionally, it is known that sequences derived as moments of $p$-adic measures satisfy stronger congruences. In this paper, instead of using $p$-adic measures, we investigate an algebraic structure of the set of generating functions and establish some conditions on $F(t)$ that are equivalent to or sufficient for the congruence and smoothness of the interpolating functions. This framework is an extension of the special case of $p$-adic moment sequences and provides a uniform manner to check the congruences $c_{n+\ell p^k}\equiv c_n \pmod{p^{k+r}}$ of concrete sequences. As an application, we also provide some equivalent conditions of the definition of Wall-Sun-Sun primes, also called Fibonacci-Wieferich primes.

papers.title: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

papers.title: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
papers.abstract: Recently, Matom\"{a}ki, Pandey, Pliego, Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^{\theta}$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\theta > \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for every $\frac{1}{2} < \theta < 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
papers.abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

papers.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
papers.authors: Elke Neuhaus, Irem Portakal, Luca Sodomaco, Katherine Tung
papers.abstract:
An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope.
  We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].

papers.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
papers.authors: Xi Chen, Kuangmiao Xiong, Boxi Xu
papers.abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon, and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_{1}$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

papers.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
papers.abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space. In particular, our results disprove Atiyah's conjecture on configurations of points and its hyperbolic analogue.

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.authors: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr
papers.abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

papers.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. To study the converse, we associate to each endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one a family of holonomic $A_2(k)$-modules over finite fields $k$. Kontsevich's conjecture predicts the existence of a $\mathcal D$-module in characteristic zero, unique up to isomorphism, whose reductions to positive characteristic are isomorphic to the prescribed modules. We prove uniqueness whenever such a lift exists. If these lifts exist for every such endomorphism, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge2$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb A^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. We also study an ultraproduct version of the lifting problem: whether these finite-field modules can be recovered as reductions of a single module in characteristic zero along a chosen ultrafilter. We prove that this is possible precisely when the Berest--Wilson invariants of these modules, regarded as left $A_1(k)$-modules, are bounded along that ultrafilter. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

papers.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
papers.authors: Hidekazu Yoshioka, Motoh Tsujimura, Ayumi Hashiguchi
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.

papers.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
papers.abstract: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-\delta}$, with absolute constants $C,\delta>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

papers.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle.
  More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles. For Picard number one and for isotropic N\'eron--Severi lattices of rank two, we further obtain modular-curve criteria for generation by reflective involutions and unipotent isometries, including a complete classification in the split case $N\cong U(d)$.

papers.title: A DG algebra structure for the edge ideal of any split graph
papers.authors: David Bronshvayg, Rachel Diethorn, Mario Stinson-Maas, Reed Wang
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit DG algebra structure on the minimal free resolution of the quotient of a polynomial ring by the edge ideal of any split graph (that is, a graph whose vertex set is a disjoint union of a clique and an independent set). The algebra structure is based on a simple combinatorial notion, which we call the fixing edge of a pair of edges, that directly captures the structure of the underlying graph. Our construction involves an explicit description of the minimal free resolution of the edge ideal of such a graph, including formulas for both the Betti numbers and the differentials.

papers.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

papers.title: Gaussian-efficient nonasymptotic confidence sets for unbounded means
